title: Tasks have no network access on current Agent Substrate because ax never creates an egress policy
body:
On Agent Substrate v0.2.0 and later, an actor can't open outbound connections until it has an egress policy. ax never creates one, and there's nothing on a Task or Workspace that would let you ask for one, so every task ends up with no network at all. Anything that calls a model API, clones a repo at runtime, or installs a package just hangs or fails.

Before the September restructure, the `Gateway` resource took care of this (see #350). Since it was removed there's no way to do it through ax.

**Example** (Agent Substrate v0.3.0, ax `main` at ac23328, `agentgateway` egress dataplane):

```yaml
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Task
metadata:
  name: net-test
  atespace: default
spec:
  image: "<runner image>@sha256:..."
  command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep infinity"]
  debug: true
```

```console
$ ax ssh net-test -- openssl s_client -connect www.google.com:443 -brief
write:errno=104
```

The connection is reset. If I add a policy for the actor by hand with Substrate's own CLI, it starts working right away:

```yaml
# policy.yaml
metadata: {atespace: default, name: default}
rules:
  - https:
      hostnames: [www.google.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com]
      ports: {numbers: [443]}
```

```console
$ kubectl ate create egress-policy net-test -a default -f policy.yaml
```

That works for a one-off test, but it means a second tool, access to the Substrate API, and remembering to do it for every task after its actor exists.

**Suggested fix**

- Add an optional `egress` section to `TaskSpec` (or to `Workspace`, if it's meant to be shared): a list of allowed hostnames and ports. Have the reconciler call `CreateActorEgressPolicy` right after `EnsureActor`, before the first resume. Since tasks are immutable, create-only is enough.
- Add an ax-server flag for a default policy applied to tasks that don't set one, for clusters that want open egress. Keep the default closed so this doesn't bring back the problem in #350.

Two Substrate details we ran into, in case they help whoever picks this up. On v0.3.0, `tlsPassthrough` rules are accepted but ignored by the gateway; that's fixed on Substrate `main` in 6c75a41f. Use `https` rules on v0.3.0. Also, the default Envoy egress dataplane didn't forward allowed TLS traffic for us, while the `agentgateway` dataplane did.

title: examples/task.yaml gives the task an empty workspace because the Task is listed before its Workspace
body:
`examples/task.yaml` lists the Task before the Workspace it uses. `ax apply` creates the documents in file order, so the Task is created and reconciled before its Workspace exists. `fetchWorkspaces` quietly skips references it can't find (`internal/server/server.go:364`), so the actor template is built without `AX_WORKSPACES_YAML`.

The runner then sets up an empty `/workspace`, writes its "initialized" marker, and reports ready. The Workspace created a moment later is never used. Because tasks are immutable, the only way out is to delete the task and apply again with the documents in the other order.

**Example**, using the same layout as the shipped example (a Task followed by a Workspace with a `git` entry and a `files` entry):

```console
$ ax apply -f task.yaml
task.ax.io/git-task created
workspace.ax.io/git-workspace created
$ ax resume task git-task
$ ax describe task git-task
...
  Ready           True    TaskRunning    Task is running and its workspace is ready
  WorkspaceReady  True    SetupComplete  Workspace setup completed at 10.59.128.81
$ ax ssh git-task -- sh -c 'ls -A /workspace; curl -s $AX_METADATA_URL/metadata/v1alpha1/ax/workspaces'
command.log
workspace metadata not available
```

There's no clone and no file from `files`, yet the task says the workspace is ready. With the Workspace listed first, the same spec gets its `files` written and a clone attempted (which then hits #427, but that's a separate problem).

**Suggested fix**

- Reject `CreateTask` when a referenced Workspace doesn't exist (`FailedPrecondition` naming the missing workspace), so the mistake is loud instead of silent.
- Have `ax apply` create Workspaces and Models before Tasks, whatever their order in the file.
- Put the Workspace first in `examples/task.yaml` and in the examples in `docs/manifests.md`.

title: docs/runner.md says suspend sends SIGTERM, but suspend freezes the sandbox without any signal
body:
`docs/runner.md` says "Stop and suspend both deliver `SIGTERM` to PID 1." In practice, suspend doesn't send any signal. Substrate checkpoints the sandbox and freezes it, so a runner that waits for SIGTERM to flush state never gets the chance. We saw the same on Agent Substrate v0.1.0-gke.1 and v0.3.0.

**Example**: a command that logs when it starts and when it gets SIGTERM, writing to the durable volume:

```yaml
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Task
metadata:
  name: term-test
  atespace: default
spec:
  image: "<runner image>@sha256:..."
  command:
    - sh
    - -c
    - |
      log() { echo "$(date +%T) $*" >> /workspace/term.log; }
      trap 'log got-SIGTERM; exit 0' TERM
      log "started pid=$$"
      while true; do sleep 1; done
  debug: true
```

```console
$ ax resume task term-test
$ ax suspend task term-test
$ ax resume task term-test
$ ax ssh term-test -- cat /workspace/term.log
22:25:18 started pid=9
22:26:00 started pid=10
```

There's no `got-SIGTERM` line. On v0.3.0 the command simply starts again after resume (new PID), while PID 1 still has the golden boot's start time. On v0.1.0-gke.1 the process memory came back from the golden snapshot instead. Either way, the only thing that reliably survives a suspend is `/workspace`. Files in `/tmp` and processes started after the golden boot are gone.

**Suggested fix**

- Correct `docs/runner.md`: suspend is a checkpoint with no signal, only `/workspace` survives, and the command may be started again on resume. It would also help to say plainly that `spec.command` can run during the golden boot (#428), since that's part of the same picture for runner authors.
- If a graceful suspend is wanted, ax could ask the runner before calling `SuspendActor`. For example, a `POST /suspend` on the runner's port 80 that forwards SIGTERM to the command's process group and waits (with a deadline) for it to exit or acknowledge.

Note: I opened #446 on the assumption that suspend sends SIGTERM. That request still makes sense for stop and delete, but it won't help suspend.

title: A slow resume gets cancelled partway, and a task can end up running while ax says it is suspended
body:
Since ac23328, ax-server reconciles inside the request handler, using the request's context (`internal/server/server.go:288` for suspend and `:336` for resume). The CLI gives `SuspendTask` and `ResumeTask` a 15-second deadline (`cmd/ax/main.go:834` and `:865`). When the CLI gives up, the cancellation goes all the way down to Substrate, and anything still in flight is abandoned partway.

We hit this two ways on Agent Substrate v0.1.0-gke.1.

**1. The first resume of a new task gets cancelled.** The worker hadn't pulled the runner image yet, so the restore took longer than 15 seconds:

```console
$ time ax resume task simple-task
Error: resuming task: rpc error: code = Internal desc = resuming task on substrate: resuming actor: resuming actor default/simple-task: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
real    0m15.045s
```

Substrate's API server logged the restore being abandoned:

```
"method":"/ateapi.Control/ResumeActor","err":"workflow failed at step CallAteletRestore: while restoring durable snapshot: rpc error: code = Canceled desc = context canceled","elapsed-time":"14.940267106s"
```

**2. The task ends up running while ax says it's suspended.** On a later attempt, `ResumeActor` finished in about 5 seconds, then the workspace readiness poll ran past the CLI's deadline. ax-server logged `task successfully reconciled and running ... phase=Running`, but the saved status stayed `Suspended` while the actor was running. After that, ax refused to work with it:

```console
$ ax ssh simple-task -- uname -a
Error: task "simple-task" is in phase "Suspended" (must be Running to ssh)
```

**Suggested fix**

- Run the reconcile on a context detached from the caller (`context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` plus its own timeout), so a client disconnect can't abort Substrate work or the status write.
- Optionally return early with the current status and let `ax watch` follow progress, so slow restores don't block the RPC at all.
- Give the CLI a longer default deadline for suspend and resume, or a `--timeout` flag.

title: `ax suspend` of a large workspace can lose the workspace while every command reports success
body:
`ax suspend` has a fixed 15 s deadline (`cmd/ax/main.go:834`). If the workspace snapshot takes longer to upload, the deadline cancels the suspend inside Substrate. The next commands all succeed, but the task comes back from an older snapshot and the new workspace files are gone.

I used only `ax` commands. Marker file `A` was in an earlier snapshot. Then I wrote marker `B` and a 3 GiB random file to `/workspace`.

| Step | Exit | AX phase | Substrate actor |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ax suspend task T` | `DeadlineExceeded` after 15 s | Running | SUSPENDING |
| `ax resume task T` | error, actor is SUSPENDING | Failed | SUSPENDING |
| `ax suspend task T` | 0 | Suspended | CRASHED |
| `ax resume task T` | 0 | Running | RUNNING |

After the last step `A` is still there, but `B` and the 3 GiB file are gone. The actor stayed SUSPENDING for at least 5 minutes after the first step, so waiting does not help.

### Why

1. ax-server passes the request context to `SuspendActor` (`reconciler.go:196`), so the CLI deadline cancels the Substrate workflow. At that point ateom has already checkpointed and removed the sandbox, and the cancel stops the upload. Substrate keeps no snapshot files after a failed upload ([substrate#362](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/issues/362)) and leaves the actor SUSPENDING for a retry.
2. The retried suspend runs `runsc pause` on the removed sandbox (exit status 128) and Substrate crashes the actor. `reconciler.go:196-203` only logs the `SuspendActor` error and sets the phase to Suspended, so the CLI reports success.
3. On the next resume `EnsureActor` finds the crashed actor and calls `RevertActor` (`internal/substrate/client.go:326-336`). The only trace is a log line, `existing actor is crashed, reverted to its last snapshot`.

The status write after a CLI deadline also uses the cancelled context and is dropped. That is why the task stays Running in step 1 although the actor is SUSPENDING. I saw the same after a slow resume, where the task stayed Suspended while the actor ran.

### Size

In my lab 512 MiB suspends in 7 to 10 s and 1 GiB in 11 to 16 s, so 1 GiB sometimes passes the deadline and leaves the task stuck. Data loss happened in 3 of 3 trials with 1.5 GiB on the older stack and 3 of 3 with 3 GiB on Substrate main. A 512 MiB control kept all files. `kubectl ate suspend actor` has no 15 s deadline and completes a 1.5 GiB suspend in about 16 s.

### Possible fixes

Running the Substrate lifecycle calls on a context that a client disconnect cannot cancel, with its own timeout, prevents the loss. A longer or configurable CLI deadline also helps. Returning the `SuspendActor` error and not reverting a crashed actor silently would make a failure visible to the user.

### Environment

A kind cluster on Docker Desktop, Apple Silicon. Same sequence on two stacks.

1. google/ax `ac23328` with Agent Substrate `1d7ca8c`
2. google/ax `be7b1a8` (the #443 fix from Ethereal49/ax) with Agent Substrate main `0b91488d`

title: kagent → AX → Substrate: Making AX the Runtime Boundary for Agent Applications
body:
# kagent → AX → Substrate: Making AX the Runtime Boundary for Agent Applications I've implemented and deployed an integration that changes kagent's runtime dependency from **kagent → Substrate** to **kagent → AX → Substrate**. The stack runs on Kubernetes with gVisor. In the demo, I create an Agent through the kagent UI, let AX prepare its runtime, and start a conversation with a DeepSeek-backed agent. The main idea is to make AX the runtime interface that kagent depends on: **kagent owns the application and its sessions; AX owns the runtime contract; Substrate provides the underlying execution mechanisms.** Implementation repositories: - [AX integration](https://github.com/ssrq1992/ax/tree/main) - [kagent integration](https://github.com/ssrq1992/kagent/tree/main) The additions described below are part of this integration, not features I am claiming are already available in upstream AX. The repository links point to development branches and may change after this post. ## 1. Why introduce AX between kagent and Substrate? In the kagent version I started from, kagent directly used Substrate to create and run agent instances. Substrate already provided the essential mechanisms: Actors, WorkerPools, isolation, snapshots, and suspend/resume. However, kagent also had to translate application requirements into those infrastructure resources. Creating a conversational agent involved constructing an ActorTemplate, preparing a golden snapshot, selecting a WorkerPool, creating an Actor, and handling backend routing. Checkpoint/fork and sandbox operations introduced further dependencies on snapshot semantics and the Guest protocol. This left two kinds of logic in kagent: - **Application logic:** models, prompts, tools, sessions, conversation history, permissions, and scheduled runs. - **Runtime integration:** templates, capacity, instance lifecycle, backend addressing, snapshots, and execution protocols. AX's existing Task abstraction offered a starting point for separating them. Rather than asking every agent application to implement its own Substrate integration, AX can expose a runtime contract that applications share. That is the value I wanted to explore: **an application should be able to ask AX to prepare, create, access, and restore an agent instance without constructing Substrate resources itself.** Adding AX also adds a service boundary and operational complexity. The abstraction needs to cover the whole interaction surface to justify that cost. Moving Actor creation behind AX while leaving WorkerPool management and backend routing in kagent would only partially solve the problem. ## 2. Goals and responsibilities The integration has four goals: 1. Make AX models and APIs the runtime dependency exposed to kagent. 2. Cover runtime preparation, capacity, lifecycle, and access together. 3. Preserve kagent's sessions, A2A behavior, history, credentials, scheduled runs, checkpoint/fork, and sandbox capabilities. 4. Extend AX while retaining its ordinary Task execution path. The intended division of responsibilities is: | Layer | What it owns | | --- | --- | | **kagent** | What the Agent does, who can use it, and how its sessions and application history work | | **AX** | How the runtime is prepared, which capacity it uses, how an instance is identified and accessed, and how its lifecycle is managed | | **Substrate** | How Actors execute, how worker capacity is provided, and how isolation, snapshots, and backend networking work | This does not make backend changes free. It gives those changes a defined integration boundary in AX instead of spreading them through kagent's business services. ## 3. Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph K["kagent — application layer"] Config["Harness + AgentTemplate
Compile a runtime revision"] Session["Session / Sandbox
Lifecycle and checkpoint / fork"] Dialer["RuntimeDialer
A2A access"] end subgraph A["AX — runtime interface"] Prepared["PreparedRuntime
Prepare and reuse"] Group["TaskGroup
Shared capacity"] Task["Task
Runtime instance"] Gateway["Shared TaskGateway
Route by Task UID"] Prepared -->|"Referenced by"| Task Group -->|"Hosts"| Task Gateway -->|"Targets"| Task end subgraph S["Substrate — execution backend"] Template["ActorTemplate + golden snapshot"] Pool["WorkerPool"] Actor["Actor"] end Config -->|"Compile and prepare"| Prepared Config -->|"Select group"| Group Session -->|"AX lifecycle APIs"| Task Dialer -->|"A2A over mTLS"| Gateway Prepared --> Template Group -->|"1:1"| Pool Task -->|"1:1"| Actor ``` The diagram shows logical relationships, not every network hop. Backend resource mappings stay inside AX. kagent does not construct ActorTemplates, manage WorkerPools, or address Actors directly. ## 4. The key design choices ### TaskGroup: replace direct WorkerPool management TaskGroup represents shared runtime capacity. In this implementation, **one TaskGroup maps to one Substrate WorkerPool**. Its configuration is deliberately small: | Field | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `replicas` | Number of workers, not the number of Tasks or Agents | | `sandboxClass` | The platform's supported isolation class, such as `gvisor` | | `snapshotLocation` | Snapshot storage location | Multiple Harnesses and sessions can share a TaskGroup. Each Task binds to its group using a name and UID, preventing an existing reference from silently attaching to a different group recreated under the same name. I initially considered a batch-oriented resource, but the semantics did not fit. Sessions arrive over time. The group should provide capacity, not maintain a fixed number of Tasks or replace a deleted session. The implementation includes scaling checks and reference protection for deletion. TaskGroups can be created while AX Server is running; they do not have to be declared at startup. The CLI currently provides `ax group create|get|list|scale|delete`. TaskGroup is an AX API resource, not a Kubernetes CRD, and `ax apply` does not yet handle it. ### PreparedRuntime: prepare an environment before creating sessions PreparedRuntime separates **preparing an Agent's environment** from **creating a particular session instance**. kagent compiles a Harness and AgentTemplate into an immutable revision. It then calls AX to prepare the image, command, runtime configuration, readiness requirements, and credential bindings. AX translates that configuration into the backend template and golden snapshot—the prepared starting state used to instantiate runtimes. The lifecycle is Prepare / Get / Release. kagent publishes Agent readiness only after preparation succeeds and the usable revision is persisted. Old revisions are released through reference-aware cleanup. Many sessions can reuse a prepared starting environment, while each session retains its own runtime state and identity. Creating an Agent therefore does not immediately create a user session's Task. A golden Actor used during preparation is separate from a session instance. ### Managed Tasks: replace direct Actor lifecycle operations For the conversation path, **one kagent Session binds to one AX Task**, backed by one Actor. An A2A Task still represents application work within that session; it is not the same thing as the AX runtime instance. The managed path adds `groupRef`, `preparedRuntimeRef`, optional `restoreFrom`, and separate runtime status. It covers create, resume, pause, suspend, delete, and checkpoint operations. Ordinary Tasks retain their existing path. Persisted ownership distinguishes managed resources, so omitting managed fields from a later request cannot bypass the managed-resource checks. ### Shared TaskGateway: hide backend addressing kagent's RuntimeDialer sends A2A traffic to a shared TaskGateway inside AX Server. The gateway validates access, identifies the target Task by UID, resumes it when needed, and forwards requests through Substrate's routing path. This is an added service capability within AX Server, **not a separate gateway deployment for each group**. A stateful conversation must reach its own Task rather than an arbitrary instance in the group. The gateway supports A2A unary calls, streaming, and cancellation. Sandbox process and filesystem operations use AX's TaskExecutionService, with AX-owned messages and backend Guest protocol conversion inside AX. Together, these changes move the dependency boundary beyond simply replacing an Actor reference with a Task reference. ## 5. What happens during a conversation? ### Prepare the Agent An operator creates or selects a TaskGroup. In kagent, a Harness chooses the adapter, runtime image, and group; an AgentTemplate defines the model, prompt, and tools; an Agent combines the two. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor U as User / operator participant K as kagent participant A as AX participant S as Substrate U->>A: Create or select TaskGroup A->>S: Ensure corresponding worker capacity U->>K: Configure model, Harness, template, and Agent K->>A: Resolve TaskGroup UID K->>K: Compile immutable runtime revision K->>A: PrepareRuntime with stable request identity A->>S: Prepare template and golden snapshot loop Observe preparation K->>A: GetPreparedRuntime A-->>K: Preparation status end Note over K,A: Successful preparation K->>K: Persist usable revision and AX references K-->>U: Agent Ready ``` No manual PreparedRuntime creation is needed: the kagent controller drives this process. ### Create the session and handle the first message The current UI creates the Session when the user submits the first message. Internally, session creation and message dispatch are separate steps: kagent records the creation intent, creates the AX Task, and persists its binding before dispatching the message. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor U as User participant K as kagent / TaskStore participant A as AX / TaskGateway participant S as Substrate participant R as ADK runtime participant M as Model API U->>K: Start a conversation with a message K->>K: Record Session and stable creation intent K->>A: CreateTask with group and runtime references A->>S: Create suspended Actor and runtime bindings A-->>K: Task identity K->>K: Persist Session-to-Task binding K->>A: Dispatch A2A request to Task UID A->>A: Validate caller and target opt Task needs activation A->>S: Resume instance S->>R: Restore runtime and check readiness end A->>R: Route A2A request through backend R->>K: HTTPS TaskStore call with runtime credential K->>A: Authenticate runtime A-->>K: Verified Task identity K->>K: Validate Session binding K-->>R: Session identity and requested business state R->>R: Use instance-local ADK conversation state R->>M: Call model through configured egress M-->>R: Model output R-->>A: A2A events A-->>K: Forward events K-->>U: Display response R->>K: Persist business state and coordinate completion K->>A: Request lifecycle transition when appropriate A->>S: Perform backend transition K->>A: Observe completion A-->>K: Runtime state and boundary reference K->>K: Persist boundary ``` This is a logical sequence. Streaming and state writes may interleave, and subsequent TaskStore requests still require authentication. kagent's public business history is distinct from the ADK runtime's private conversation state, stored in the instance's durable directory. A later message in the same Session targets the same Task UID. If the Task is suspended, AX restores it; otherwise, it routes to the running instance. A `boundaryRef` identifies the recorded runtime boundary without making kagent handle backend snapshot addresses. Checkpoint/fork builds on that separation: kagent owns the business history cutoff and creates a new Session, while AX creates a new Task from a validated restore reference. Deleting a Session cleans up its Task without deleting shared capacity or prepared runtimes that remain referenced. ## 6. The working demo ### Environment The demo runs on an existing Kubernetes cluster with: - Substrate using **gVisor** (`sandboxClass: gvisor`). - The extended AX Server and persistent Redis. - The paired kagent controller, UI, CRDs, and ADK runtime image, with PostgreSQL. - mTLS access to AX, HTTPS runtime callbacks, and the outbound credential and trust configuration needed for model calls. The application path requires more than healthy Pods: model access, runtime credential injection, and TaskStore callbacks must also work. ### Create a TaskGroup The group used in the demo was: ```yaml apiVersion: ax.dev/v1alpha1 kind: TaskGroup metadata: name: kagent-task-group-demo atespace: kagent spec: replicas: 1 sandboxClass: gvisor snapshotLocation: gs://ate-snapshots/kagent-ssd ``` With the AX endpoint and client certificates configured: ```bash ax --server "$AX_ENDPOINT" --atespace kagent group create \ --file "$DEMO_DIR/task-group-demo.yaml" \ --request-id create-kagent-demo ax --server "$AX_ENDPOINT" --atespace kagent group get \ --name kagent-task-group-demo ``` The snapshot location is specific to this deployment. Retrying the same creation uses the same request identity; a different operation should not reuse it. The creation returned Provisioning, followed by Ready with one ready worker: The corresponding WorkerPool and worker Pod were ready. This is an operator-side inspection of the mapping, not a direct dependency in kagent's application path: ### Configure the Agent through the UI The actual demo used these resources: | Resource | Demo configuration | | --- | --- | | ModelConfig | `deepseek-v4-pro`, using the OpenAI-compatible provider and model ID `deepseek-v4-pro` | | Model endpoint | `https://api.deepseek.com` | | Harness | `kagent-harness-demo`, with the `kagent` adapter and a digest-pinned ADK image | | TaskGroup | `kagent-task-group-demo` | | AgentTemplate | `kagent-template-demo`, with a general-knowledge assistant prompt | | Agent | `deepseek-agent-demo`, referencing that template and Harness | The model API key is stored in a Kubernetes Secret. The runtime receives a credential binding rather than embedding the actual key in the shared runtime configuration. The Harness form selects AX capacity directly. This particular demo also set a snapshot-location override; leaving it unset would use the group's location. The template supplies the model and prompt: The Agent references both resources: After AX preparation completed, the Agent appeared as Ready: ### Start a conversation and inspect its runtime I opened the Agent and sent two messages: “who are you?” and “what can you do?” The UI displayed responses from the configured agent: Inspecting the Session's AX Task showed its UID-bound TaskGroup and PreparedRuntime references, together with a recorded suspend boundary: The Task output contains `executionVersion: 3`, an idle Suspend operation, a `boundaryRef`, and `restorable: true`. This is a post-execution observation; it should not be mistaken for a capture immediately after initial Task creation. The corresponding PreparedRuntime query reported `kind: Service` and `phase: Ready`. The following selected fields show the runtime-to-group relationship: ```json { "metadata": { "name": "deepseek-agent-demo-5fb960b71a51", "atespace": "kagent", "uid": "24bfc8f1265b8ce5068360f39ae20828" }, "spec": { "groupRef": { "atespace": "kagent", "name": "kagent-task-group-demo", "uid": "5cde9957076ba25dfb2cb18bcc0477ed" }, "kind": "Service" }, "phase": "Ready" } ``` _Originally posted by @ssrq1992 in https://github.com/google/ax/discussions/447_

title: Workspace readiness waits 2 s for a direct check before it asks the router
body:
After `ResumeActor`, the controller polls `/readyz?check=workspace` in `checkReady` (internal/controller/reconciler.go). It tries `http://<workerIP>:80` first and only then the atenet router. The direct check cannot succeed. Substrate gives each worker pool a NetworkPolicy that accepts connections only from the atenet router (cmd/atecontroller/internal/controllers/networkpolicy_controller.go in Substrate), so the controller's packets are dropped. On my kind lab with Substrate main `c4129c9` the request therefore waits for the full 2 s `httpClient` timeout, and the router check that follows answers 200 in about 15 ms. So the first resume of every task spends 2 s on a request that cannot succeed.

I checked both paths from a pod in the cluster with the same headers the controller uses. From the `ax-system` namespace every port of the worker pod times out, and the policy that does it is `substrate-ax-workers-*`.

```
direct  http://<workerIP>:80/readyz?check=workspace           -> no answer after 5 s
router  http://atenet-router.ate-system.svc.cluster.local:80   -> 200 in 0.015 s
        (ate-target-actor: default/<actor>)
```

I swapped the order in a fork, so the router goes first when `ATENET_ROUTER_ADDR` is set. Only a router 200 ends the check. Any other result still goes on to the direct check, as now. It touches `checkReady` only, plus a test with two cases, a ready router with a worker that never answers, and a failing router with a ready worker. The first case fails with the current order. Over 5 small tasks each, resume went from 2.19 s to 0.17 s and the whole task from 3.85 s to 2.06 s (medians). Suspend and resume of 512 MiB and 2 GiB workspaces and a chaos run with 8 tasks still pass.

The change is at https://github.com/eren23/ax/compare/a3ad2af...1db4c33

This is separate from #387, which is about old Substrate releases that reject the router Host. Here the router answers fine and the time goes to the direct check before it.

title: fix(substrate): adapt to Substrate v0.4 API and harden actor RPCs
body:
fixes: https://github.com/google/ax/issues/443

Bump github.com/agent-substrate/substrate to v0.4.1-0.20261009152331-f6a1dc72a35d and adapt to its API changes:
- ContainerReadyz -> ContainerWakeupProbe.
- SnapshotsConfig -> SnapshotConfig with PreferredFidelity VOLUMES (equivalent to the previous data-only snapshot / resume-from-golden).
- WorkerAssignment.WorkerPodIp -> WorkerPodIps; use the first (primary) IP and build the readiness URL with net.JoinHostPort so IPv6 works.

Make Substrate calls more robust:
- Retry ResumeActor (ResourceExhausted/Aborted) and SuspendActor, DeleteActor, DeleteActorTemplate (Aborted) with jittered exponential backoff via github.com/cenkalti/backoff/v5.
- When CreateActorTemplate rejects the built template (InvalidArgument/ Unimplemented), fall back to cloning the cluster's base template with task overrides, preserving cluster-specific settings such as SnapshotConfig.

Other:
- Add v1alpha1.DefaultSystemNamespace and replace hard-coded "ax-system".
- Don't reuse an existing CLI tunnel that points at a different namespace/service.

title: Clarify suspend state preservation and runner signal handling
body:
The runner docs said suspend delivers `SIGTERM`, which could lead a runner to wait for a shutdown signal before saving its state. Both pages now explain that suspend checkpoints the durable workspace without a SIGTERM flush opportunity. They also distinguish state saved in `/workspace` from process state and describe repeated command starts.

Fixes #451.

Validation on Go 1.27.1, Linux/amd64 (all exited 0):

- Full tests: `make test`, `go test -count=1 ./...`, and `go test -race -count=1 ./...`.
- Build and checks: `make build`, `go vet ./...`, `go mod tidy`, clean `go.mod`/`go.sum`, and `git diff --check`.
- Live gVisor/kind test: two suspend/resume cycles preserved a workspace file, removed a `/tmp` marker, and restarted the command without recording SIGTERM.
- Positive signal controls: an explicit SIGTERM reached the command's trap; `docker stop` delivered SIGTERM to runner PID 1, which forwarded it to the child and exited 0.
- Removed the owned Tasks, Workspaces, actors, templates, control container, and private CLI tunnel.

Prepared with an AI coding assistant.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, captured output, and tested version limits</summary>

Live end-to-end reproduction used AX base `ac2332829f22360ff97b0ba34d94dd0dd782f17e` with the companion lab's [compatibility patch](https://github.com/erain/substrate-ax-firsthand/blob/main/compat/ax-substrate.patch), and Substrate `7245baad8a6fd58f81c32338395b74484547fc12` in the existing kind lab. Server image: `localhost:5001/firsthand-ax-server@sha256:ca5a1cd44037fe1e8b5da75d9371cdb81b02c8d445f2b627abc52dffd5996633`. Runner image is pinned in the manifest below. These local registry images are specific to this lab; other environments need their corresponding reachable runner image. No components were redeployed.

Save this as `lifecycle.yaml` (refuse to reuse these names if they already exist):

```yaml
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Workspace
metadata:
  name: ax-451-workspace-20261013
  atespace: firsthand
spec: {}
---
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Task
metadata:
  name: ax-451-lifecycle-20261013
  atespace: firsthand
spec:
  image: localhost:5001/firsthand-runner@sha256:3b2ce0b2b61ec404a57cd9ac644440f42d7320b97511e7c6aaaad529d77c988c
  debug: true
  workspaces:
    - name: ax-451-workspace-20261013
      path: /workspace
  command:
    - sh
    - -c
    - |
      trap 'echo got-SIGTERM >> /workspace/term.log; exit 0' TERM
      count=$(cat /workspace/starts 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
      count=$((count + 1))
      echo "$count" > /workspace/starts
      echo "started run=$count pid=$$" >> /workspace/term.log
      echo "$$" > /workspace/command.pid
      while true; do sleep 1; done
```

From a checkout built with `make build`, set `KUBECONFIG` to your lab's private kubeconfig. Use these CLI flags and assertions to reproduce (the captured run used the companion checkout's built CLI):

```bash
export KUBECONFIG=/path/to/your/private/lab.kubeconfig
export AX_HOME=$(mktemp -d)
unset AX_SERVER
ax() { ./bin/ax --context kind-firsthand -n firsthand-ax -a firsthand "$@"; }
task=ax-451-lifecycle-20261013
ax apply -f lifecycle.yaml
ax resume task "$task"
ax ssh "$task" -- sh -ec 'test "$(cat /workspace/starts)" -ge 1; echo durable-451 > /workspace/preserved; echo ephemeral-451 > /tmp/ax-451-marker; cp /workspace/starts /workspace/before-starts'
for cycle in 1 2; do
  ax suspend task "$task"
  ax resume task "$task"
  ax ssh "$task" -- sh -ec 'test "$(cat /workspace/preserved)" = durable-451; test ! -e /tmp/ax-451-marker; test "$(cat /workspace/starts)" -gt "$(cat /workspace/before-starts)"; test "$(grep -c got-SIGTERM /workspace/term.log || true)" = 0; cat /workspace/term.log; cp /workspace/starts /workspace/before-starts; echo ephemeral-451 > /tmp/ax-451-marker'
done
ax ssh "$task" -- sh -ec 'kill -TERM "$(cat /workspace/command.pid)"; for n in 1 2 3 4 5; do if grep -q got-SIGTERM /workspace/term.log; then cat /workspace/term.log; exit 0; fi; sleep 1; done; exit 1'
ax suspend task "$task"
ax resume task "$task"
ax ssh "$task" -- sh -ec 'test "$(grep -c got-SIGTERM /workspace/term.log)" = 1; test "$(cat /workspace/preserved)" = durable-451; cat /workspace/term.log'
ax delete task "$task"
ax delete workspace ax-451-workspace-20261013
ax tunnel stop kind-firsthand  # uses this test's private AX_HOME
```

Captured output across the two ordinary cycles and explicit-signal control:

```text
started run=1 pid=9
started run=2 pid=9
started run=3 pid=9
PASS: durable file preserved, /tmp marker gone, command restarted, no SIGTERM
got-SIGTERM
PASS: explicit SIGTERM reaches trap
started run=4 pid=9
PASS: SIGTERM record also preserved through DATA restore
PASS: fixture Task, Workspace and actor removed
EXIT STATUS: 0
```

Both saved suspended actor responses reported `SNAPSHOT_CONTENT_SCOPE_DATA`. Start counts prove reruns even though the sandbox reused PID 9. An isolated Docker control using the same runner image additionally sent SIGTERM to runner PID 1 via `docker stop --time 15`; the runner forwarded it to its child, logged `control-got-SIGTERM`, and exited 0. That container was removed, and a separate NotFound check confirmed the generated ActorTemplate was removed too.

The original documentation's suspend signal expectation is contradicted by these captured runs. The pinned Substrate source independently shows DATA checkpoint pauses the sandbox for volume archiving and then terminates application containers with SIGKILL, rather than giving a SIGTERM flush opportunity. Unmodified AX source at the base revision requests DATA snapshots with `RESUME_SOURCE_GOLDEN`; the live lab uses the explicitly identified compatibility patch below.

The private AX CLI tunnel was stopped after fixture cleanup; `ax tunnel list` then returned `No active tunnels`, and a TCP check confirmed its owned local port was closed.

Limits: this demonstrates the pinned gVisor/kind setup with the explicit lab compatibility patch, not an unmodified AX build or every Substrate release/backend. The lab patch removes `on_resume` and uses the installed Substrate's data-resume default. The golden-resume setting is established from unmodified AX source; the live run establishes data preservation, process restarts and signal behavior for the patched lab. Golden-boot command execution is permitted by runner startup and snapshot configuration; this experiment does not force that timing race. No runtime code changes or new repository tests are needed for this documentation correction. Full logs and reproducible harnesses are saved with the contribution workflow.

</details>

title: Document supported Google models and accurate manifest requirements
body:
Applying the documented Anthropic Model succeeds, but the workspace planner fails with `unsupported provider`. The guide now documents the implemented Google provider and removes the unsupported example. It also explains Model resource scope and secret namespace, corrects the supported-kind count and Task image requirements, and replaces a broken example link.

Fixes #371.

Validation on Go 1.27.1, Linux/amd64 (all exited 0):

- Uncached full tests, race tests, build, vet, module cleanliness, and whitespace checks.
- The actual documented YAML passes through a real gRPC API, memory store, planner, and Google-format loopback HTTP fixture; request and response assertions pass.
- The original Anthropic example fails the regression; the unsupported-provider control makes zero HTTP requests. Local documentation links resolve.

Prepared with an AI coding assistant.

<details>
<summary>Regression output, API/provider fixture, and validation limits</summary>

A regression test reads the actual Model YAML from `docs/manifests.md`, sends it through a real loopback gRPC AX server and memory store, then runs the workspace planner against a local Google-format HTTP fixture. It checks the saved spec, secret reference, request method/path/authentication, workspace goal/system instruction, exact returned plan, request count, and fixture cleanup. An Anthropic negative control verifies API acceptance followed by generation failure with zero provider requests.

### Reproduction and captured behavior

```bash
go test -count=1 -v ./internal/server -run '^TestManifestGuideModels$'
```

Before the documentation correction, on base `ac2332829f22360ff97b0ba34d94dd0dd782f17e` with the regression test added:

```text
YAML -> gRPC UpdateModel/GetModel: provider=anthropic model=claude-opus-5
generating environment plan for workspace guide-workspace: unsupported provider "anthropic"
--- FAIL: TestManifestGuideModels/claude-model/documented
exit_status=1
```

After the correction:

```text
YAML -> gRPC UpdateModel/GetModel: provider=google model=gemini-3.8-flash
store -> workspace planner -> Google HTTP: model=gemini-3.8-flash summary="fixture bootstrap plan"; requests=1
negative control: generating environment plan for workspace guide-workspace: unsupported provider "anthropic"; HTTP requests=0
HTTP provider fixture stopped
gRPC fixture stopped
--- PASS: TestManifestGuideModels
exit_status=0
```

### Validation

On Go 1.27.1, linux/amd64, all of these completed with exit status 0:

```bash
GOFLAGS=-count=1 make test
go test -race -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
make build
go mod tidy
git diff --exit-code go.mod go.sum
git diff --check
```

The full test suite contained no skipped tests. Checked all local links in the edited guide and reviewed the complete diff, including the new test.

The provider fixture runs entirely on loopback with a synthetic secret resolver; this is API/store/planner/client integration evidence, not a live Google service, Kubernetes Secret, paid-model, or Substrate sandbox test. It does not establish external availability of the example model ID. The current Task runner has its own Gemini bootstrap configuration; Model resources do not automatically configure arbitrary agent frameworks. The image digest and API key placeholders require user substitution.

</details>

title: Create the example workspace before its task
body:
`ax apply -f examples/task.yaml` submits resources in file order. The Task previously preceded its Workspace, so provisioning could initialize an empty workspace while reporting Ready=True. The example now creates its Workspace and Model first; all resource payloads remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

Refs #450. Missing-Workspace admission is covered by [draft PR #461](https://github.com/google/ax/pull/461); arbitrary-order CLI apply remains outside this PR.

Validation on Go 1.27.1, Linux/amd64 (all final checks exited 0):

- Shipped-example regression and twelve scope/order controls; the regression fails on the original ordering and passes after the change.
- Full tests, uncached tests, race tests, build, vet, formatting, and module/whitespace checks.
- Live CLI/API/runner comparison: Task-first has no workspace file or metadata; Workspace-first has both. The lab uses the explicitly documented compatibility patch below.
- Normal and forced-failure harness runs verified resource and private-tunnel cleanup.

Prepared with an AI coding assistant.

<details>
<summary>Captured ordering controls, copyable fixtures, and lab version limits</summary>

The regression decodes every shipped YAML example with the API types and requires every Task Workspace reference to have appeared earlier in that file and atespace. Twelve controls cover scope isolation, implicit/explicit `default`, wrong names, Task-first input, zero/multiple references and null input.

Validation on AX base `ac2332829f22360ff97b0ba34d94dd0dd782f17e`, Go 1.27.1:

- Baseline `go test -count=1 -v ./examples` exits 1: `document 1: Task default/task123 references Workspace default-workspace before it is defined in that atespace`. The simple example and all twelve controls pass. After reordering, everything passes (exit 0).
- `make test`, `go test -count=1 ./...`, `go test -race -count=1 ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `make build`, `go mod tidy`, `git diff --exit-code go.mod go.sum` and `git diff --check` exit 0. `gofmt` reports no unformatted test files.

Real CLI → AX API → Substrate runner controls use two unique inline-file fixtures, differing only in resource names and order. Both report Ready=True:

```text
Task-first: Task created, Workspace created
  initial actor template AX_WORKSPACES_YAML present=False
  PASS: Task-first silently initialized without referenced workspace file
Workspace-first: Workspace created, Task created
  initial actor template AX_WORKSPACES_YAML present=True
  /workspace/order-proof.txt = workspace-before-task-450
  PASS: Workspace-first wrote actual inline file and exposes workspace metadata
```

The live server is AX base `ac2332829f22360ff97b0ba34d94dd0dd782f17e` with the companion lab's [compatibility patch](https://github.com/erain/substrate-ax-firsthand/blob/main/compat/ax-substrate.patch), rather than an unmodified AX build. That existing patch updates its Substrate API binding and removes `on_resume`; the contribution does not include it. The pinned lab uses context `kind-firsthand`, namespace `firsthand-ax`, atespace `firsthand`, Substrate `7245baad8a6fd58f81c32338395b74484547fc12` and runner `localhost:5001/firsthand-runner@sha256:3b2ce0b2b61ec404a57cd9ac644440f42d7320b97511e7c6aaaad529d77c988c`. To reproduce the two ordering controls on an AX server with the tested base revision and lab compatibility patch, save these as `workspace.yaml` and `task.yaml`. Replace the runner image placeholder with a reachable digest-pinned AX runner image. Use a disposable atespace, and refuse to reuse the fixture names if they already exist.

```yaml
# workspace.yaml
---
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Workspace
metadata: {name: order-proof-workspace, atespace: firsthand}
spec:
  files:
    - path: order-proof.txt
      content: workspace-before-task-450
```

```yaml
# task.yaml
---
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Task
metadata: {name: order-proof-task, atespace: firsthand}
spec:
  image: "<reachable-task-runner-image@sha256:digest>"
  debug: true
  workspaces:
    - {name: order-proof-workspace, path: /workspace}
  command: [sh, -c, 'while true; do sleep 1; done']
```

With `KUBECONFIG` pointing at that lab, run from a checkout built with `make build`:

```bash
export AX_HOME=$(mktemp -d)
unset AX_SERVER
ax() { ./bin/ax --context kind-firsthand -n firsthand-ax -a firsthand "$@"; }
# Task-first negative control on the tested base revision:
cat task.yaml workspace.yaml > task-first.yaml
ax apply -f task-first.yaml
ax resume task order-proof-task
ax describe task order-proof-task
ax ssh order-proof-task -- sh -ec 'test ! -e /workspace/order-proof.txt; test -z "$AX_WORKSPACES_YAML"; echo "PASS: Task-first workspace absent"'
ax delete task order-proof-task
ax delete workspace order-proof-workspace
# Workspace-first control:
cat workspace.yaml task.yaml > workspace-first.yaml
ax apply -f workspace-first.yaml
ax resume task order-proof-task
ax describe task order-proof-task
ax ssh order-proof-task -- sh -ec 'test "$(cat /workspace/order-proof.txt)" = workspace-before-task-450; test -n "$AX_WORKSPACES_YAML"; echo "PASS: Workspace-first file and metadata present"'
ax delete task order-proof-task
ax delete workspace order-proof-workspace
ax tunnel stop kind-firsthand  # scoped to the private AX_HOME above
```

The harness runs `bin/ax --context kind-firsthand -n firsthand-ax -a firsthand apply -f <manifest>`, `resume task <name>`, `describe task <name>` and `ssh <name> -- sh -ec '<assertions>'`. Task-first asserts the file and `AX_WORKSPACES_YAML` are absent; Workspace-first asserts the exact file content and metadata presence. It captures Task/Workspace API responses, initial actor templates, timestamps, commands and exit statuses. Cleanup verifies owned Tasks, Workspaces, actors and templates are removed, then stops only its private AX_HOME tunnel and verifies its process is inactive. A controlled failure exits 1 with cleanup completed; the final normal run exits 0.

Full logs, fixtures, harnesses, checks and reviewed diff are saved with the contribution workflow.

This is a partial issue change. Missing-Workspace admission is covered by companion draft PR #461; arbitrary-order CLI apply remains outstanding. Runtime evidence covers the inline-file fixture and pinned local runner; the shipped remote image, Git clone, MCP/skills registries and Model credentials were not exercised.

title: Reject a Task whose bound Workspace does not exist
body:
Creating a Task that binds a Workspace that does not exist now fails with `FailedPrecondition` naming the Workspace and atespace, and nothing is saved or provisioned. Before this change, `CreateTask` looked the Workspace up after saving the Task and dropped any lookup error. Because Tasks are immutable, a Task created before its Workspace kept an empty `/workspace` until it was deleted and applied again. A store error during the lookup now fails with `Internal`.

Changes:

- `internal/server/server.go`: `CreateTask` resolves `spec.workspace` before saving and passes the resolved Workspace to `Suspend`. `SuspendTask` and `ResumeTask` are unchanged.
- `docs/manifests.md`: documents that the bound Workspace must exist first, and that `ax apply` creates documents in file order.

The examples on `main` (`examples/claude-code/task.yaml`, the README, `demo.sh`, and the E2E manifests) already list the Workspace before the Task that binds it. `examples/task.yaml`, which this PR previously reordered, was removed on `main`, so #460 no longer applies.

Refs #450. This PR does not reorder documents in `ax apply`; that remains open in the issue.

Testing (Go 1.27.1, linux/amd64):

- New `TestCreateTask_RequiresBoundWorkspace` (table-driven, real memory store, in-process Substrate fake). It covers a missing Workspace, a Workspace in another atespace, a wrapped `ErrNotFound`, a store error, a present Workspace in the default and a named atespace, and a Task with no binding. Rejected Tasks must leave no stored record and no actor. Accepted Tasks with a binding must get `AX_WORKSPACE_YAML` in their actor template.
- After merging `main` (explicit `Suspend`/`Resume` from #536): `go mod tidy && git diff --exit-code go.mod go.sum`, `go build ./cmd/ax ./cmd/ax-server ./cmd/ax-task-runner`, `go test -count=1 ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` all pass. Postgres and E2E tiers were not run (no store or E2E changes).

Prepared with an AI coding assistant; I reviewed and tested every change.

title: Return NotFound when watching a missing Task
body:
`ax watch task missing` now exits promptly with `NotFound`. Initial store lookup failures return `Internal`. The subscription still registers before the initial lookup to avoid losing updates, and its deferred close covers every subsequent exit.

Fixes #435.

This picks up [vincent0426's offered patch](https://github.com/vincent0426/ax/commit/d36bb3d), with coverage for the current main, and credits [Yi-111-a's diagnosis and reproduction](https://github.com/google/ax/issues/435#issuecomment-5926170534).

Validation on Go 1.27.1, Linux/amd64 (all final checks exited 0):

- Direct and real TCP/gRPC tests cover error codes, initial/modified delivery, terminal EOF, cancellation, subscription cleanup, and a deterministic update during the initial lookup.
- `WatchTask` has 100.0% statement coverage in the focused suite; 50 focused race repetitions passed. Missing-task and lookup-before-registration negative controls fail as expected.
- Full tests, uncached tests, race tests, build, vet, formatting, and module/whitespace checks.
- Stock CLI/API plus isolated Redis: the baseline times out (124); the fix returns NotFound (1) in 12 ms. Existing watches reach Completed, and all subscriber counts return to zero. No sandbox provisioning was needed.

title: controller,substrate: handle transient Substrate unavailability without permanent Task failure
body:
Fixes #421

### Problem
When the Substrate control plane (`ateapi`) is briefly unavailable (for example during a pod rollout or initial connection establishment), `EnsureAtespace`, `EnsureActor`, or `ResumeActor` fails immediately with `Unavailable` or `DeadlineExceeded`, and `TaskReconciler.Reconcile` permanently marks the Task as `Phase: Failed`. In addition, `CreateTask` and `ResumeTask` overwrite `Task.Status.Phase` to `Failed`, leaving no way for `ax apply` or `ax resume` to recover the task once Substrate is reachable again.

### Changes
- **`internal/substrate/client.go`**:
  - Configure default dial options with `grpc.WithDefaultCallOptions(grpc.WaitForReady(true))` and `grpc.WithConnectParams` (`BaseDelay: 100ms`, `MaxDelay: 5s`, `MinConnectTimeout: 1s`) on both `NewClientWithOptions` and `NewClient`.
  - Bound individual Substrate RPCs with `callContext` (`DefaultCallTimeout = 10s`) when the caller's context does not carry a deadline so `WaitForReady(true)` waits through brief connection drops without blocking indefinitely.
- **`internal/controller/reconciler.go`**:
  - Classify `codes.Unavailable`, `codes.DeadlineExceeded`, and `context.DeadlineExceeded` as transient via `isTransientSubstrateError`.
  - When `EnsureAtespace`, `EnsureActor`, or `ResumeActor` fails with a transient Substrate error, keep `task.Status.Phase = "Pending"` and record condition `Ready=False (Reason: SubstrateUnavailable)` instead of transitioning to `Phase: "Failed"`.
- **`internal/server/server.go`**:
  - Preserve `reconciled.Status` (`Phase: "Pending"` and `SubstrateUnavailable` condition) on transient Substrate errors in `CreateTask` and `ResumeTask`, and return `codes.Unavailable` to callers.
  - Allow `CreateTask` to re-run reconciliation when an existing task is still in `Phase == "Pending"`.
- **Unit Tests**:
  - `internal/substrate/client_test.go`: `TestClient_WaitForReady_WaitsForLateServer` and `TestClient_WaitForReady_HonorsCallTimeout`.
  - `internal/controller/reconciler_test.go`: `TestTaskReconciler_TransientSubstrateUnavailable`.
  - `internal/server/server_test.go`: `TestServer_TransientSubstrateUnavailableRecovery`.

title: Propagate SuspendActor error up from substrate
body:
Fix #441 

Return an error if substrate fails to suspend the actor instead of swallowing it with a warning log.

It ensures the following behavior:
1. retain the previous status if the substrate operation is failed
2. suspend the already suspended actor returns ok [ref](github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/blob/944abe3278b8/cmd/ateapi/internal/controlapi/workflow_suspend.go#L36-L74)
3. update the store only if the substrate operation returns success.

Tests:
- **`internal/controller/reconciler_test.go`**: Add `TestTaskReconciler_SuspendError` to verify `Reconcile` returns an error and preserves `WorkerIp` and `Conditions` when `SuspendActor` fails.
- **`internal/server/server_test.go`**: Add `TestServer_SuspendTask_ReconcileErrorRetainsRunningState` and `TestServer_SuspendTask_SuccessUpdatesStoredState` to verify `SuspendTask` error propagation and store state persistence.

title: Keep tasks pending until Substrate worker capacity becomes available
body:
Fixes #367.

A task that cannot find a free Substrate worker now waits and retries instead of becoming permanently `Failed`.

When a user resumes a task:

1. AX tries to start its actor on a worker.
2. If Substrate reports no capacity, AX saves the task as `Pending` with `Ready=False, reason=WaitingForWorker`. The CLI reports that it is waiting for a worker.
3. The server retries after 1 second, then 2 and 4 seconds, with later delays capped at 5 seconds. Once capacity is available, the task moves to `Running`.

The shorter default cap helps waiting tasks use newly freed workers promptly. Operators can tune both delays with ax-server flags:

```bash
ax-server --schedule-retry-interval=1s --schedule-retry-max-delay=5s
```

The interval must be positive and the maximum must be at least the interval. Invalid settings fail at startup. These settings control retry pacing, not how long a task may wait for capacity.

Waiting tasks remain in the existing store, so they survive a server restart. Each retry checks the latest task state under its resource lock: suspending or deleting a waiting task cancels its pending resume. Other errors still follow the existing failure behavior.

The change adds the retry loop, regression tests, and a live test runnable with `make test-e2e-scheduling`. Setup instructions are in [test/e2e/README.md](https://github.com/erain/ax/blob/fix/367-wait-for-worker/test/e2e/README.md).

### End-to-end test

The test uses a real AX server, Redis, and Substrate. It creates an isolated pool with one worker and four tasks whose actors each need the worker's full CPU capacity.

- Start all four: one should run and three should stay `Pending` across retries.
- Suspend one waiting task and delete another: neither should start later. Restart AX: the remaining task should still be waiting.
- Delete the running task: the remaining task should start automatically and successfully write and read a file inside its sandbox.
- Resume the suspended task and scale the pool to two workers: that task should also start.

All scenarios passed. The fixture pre-creates actors to pin them to the test pool; generated-template compatibility is outside this test's coverage.

![Worker exhaustion and recovery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erain/ax/65c02584e0ab883b45fec611046788dbe68a66b9/test/e2e/recordings/scheduling.gif)

`make test`, targeted race tests, `go vet ./...`, the build, and ShellCheck passed. Tests cover the default and custom retry timings, invalid configuration, and the actual retry loop. The live scenarios above also passed with the new defaults. Module files are unchanged.

Implemented with AI coding assistance.

title: [RFC] Shared golden snapshots: canary goldens, anchored Tasks, and Task clones
body:
## Summary Let Tasks with the same shape share one golden snapshot. A **canary golden** is a one-off boot that exists only to warm the shared environment and produce the golden snapshot. **Anchored Tasks** then start from that golden, each with its own data snapshot and per-task input supplied at runtime. A related **Task clone** primitive starts a new Task from the data of an existing suspended Task, using Substrate tags. Today every Task gets its own ActorTemplate, and so its own golden boot and warmup, even when the only thing that differs between Tasks is one input value (a PR URL, an issue number). For pool-style agent workloads, that makes every Task pay a full cold start. This RFC feeds into #433, which says "AX doesn't need golden images". The point here is that whether AX uses goldens should be decided by workloads like the one below, where most of the cost is shared setup. ## Motivation: a pool of code review agents A team wants every PR reviewed by an agent. Every review needs the same environment: the repo cloned at `main`, dependencies installed, linters and MCP servers ready, and review skills loaded. Only the PR differs. **Today:** ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant GH as GitHub participant Q as Queue (outside AX) participant D as Dispatcher participant AX as ax-server participant S as Substrate GH->>Q: PR opened webhook Q->>D: next PR D->>AX: CreateTask(review-pr-1234, env PR_URL) AX->>S: CreateActorTemplate("review-pr-1234-tmpl-hash") Note over S: New template for every task:
task name and per-task env feed the name S->>S: Golden boot in ate-golden:
clone, install deps, start spec.command (see issues 427, 428) S->>S: Golden snapshot AX->>S: CreateActor, ResumeActor S-->>D: Review posted D->>AX: DeleteTask ``` The full setup runs on every PR, nothing is reused, and the golden boot hits the egress and command problems in #427 and #428. **Proposed:** ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant Op as Operator participant GH as GitHub participant Q as Queue (outside AX) participant D as Dispatcher participant AX as ax-server participant S as Substrate participant R as Runner (in actor) rect rgb(235, 245, 255) Note over Op,S: Once per TaskTemplate revision (and on refresh) Op->>AX: apply TaskTemplate "code-review-base" AX->>S: CreateActorTemplate (named from shape, not task) S->>S: Canary boot: clone main, install deps,
start MCP servers (warmup egress allowed) S->>S: Golden snapshot, canary actor deleted AX-->>Op: TaskTemplate Ready (revision 3) end rect rgb(240, 255, 240) Note over GH,R: Per PR GH->>Q: PR opened webhook Q->>D: next PR D->>AX: CreateTask(from code-review-base, input PR_URL) AX->>S: CreateActor(shared template), ResumeActor S->>R: Restore golden + fresh data snapshot (seconds) R->>AX: Fetch own Task input and credentials (actor JWT) R->>R: git fetch PR, run review, post comments R-->>D: Review posted D->>AX: DeleteTask end ``` The dispatcher and queue still live outside AX, but there's no per-PR setup, and nothing carries over between PRs, which matters because PR code is untrusted. How the resources relate: ```mermaid flowchart LR TT["TaskTemplate
code-review-base r3"] -->|canary boot| G[("Golden snapshot
shared, read-only")] G -->|anchored| T1["Task review-pr-1234
own data snapshot"] G -->|anchored| T2["Task review-pr-1235
own data snapshot"] G -->|anchored| T3["Task review-pr-1236
own data snapshot"] T2 -. "suspend + CreateTag" .-> Tag[("Tag")] Tag -. "clone: from.task" .-> T4["Task review-pr-1235-retry
copy of T2's data"] ``` ## Why sharing doesn't happen today In `internal/controller/reconciler.go` and `internal/substrate/client.go`: 1. **The task name is in the template name.** `taskTemplateName` returns `"-tmpl-"`, so two identical specs still produce two templates. 2. **Per-task data goes into the template env.** `AX_TASK_YAML` (which contains `metadata.name`), `spec.env` and `GEMINI_API_KEY` are all template env vars, so they feed the hash and get baked into the golden. 3. **The golden boot is implicit.** The runner treats the golden boot as an ordinary first boot. It clones workspaces where egress is blocked (#427), starts `spec.command` (#428), and snapshots whatever state results. 4. **Credentials are baked into the golden.** Because the model key is a template env var, rotating it means rebuilding templates. ## Proposal ### 1. Canary golden: a resource keyed on shape A new resource, tentatively called `TaskTemplate`, describes the shared shape and the warmup. AX builds one Substrate ActorTemplate per `TaskTemplate` revision. Its name comes from the shape (image, workspaces, resources, sandbox config), never from a task. ```yaml apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1 kind: TaskTemplate metadata: name: code-review-base spec: image: gcr.io/acme/review-agent@sha256:… resources: requests: { cpu: "2", memory: 4Gi } workspaces: - name: acme-monorepo # cloned at main during warmup goal: "install the Go and Node toolchains and run `make deps`" warmup: egress: { gateway: warmup-egress } # the canary needs network access (#427) timeout: 20m status: phase: Ready # Building | Ready | Failed revision: 3 golden: tag: ate-golden/code-review-base-r3 builtAt: "2026-10-14T09:12:00Z" conditions: [...] ``` The canary boot runs workspace setup and then signals that it's ready to snapshot. It **never** runs a Task's `spec.command` (#428). ### 2. Anchored Tasks: shared golden, new data snapshot ```yaml apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1 kind: Task metadata: name: review-pr-1234 spec: from: template: code-review-base # pin with `revision: 3`, or follow the latest Ready revision input: # supplied at runtime, never baked into a template or golden env: - { name: PR_URL, value: "https://github.com/acme/monorepo/pull/1234" } command: ["review-agent", "--pr", "$(PR_URL)"] ``` - The actor restores from the template's golden and gets its own fresh data snapshot and durable volume. - **Input is delivered at runtime.** On first boot the runner fetches its Task from ax-server, authenticating with `MintActorJWT`, and serves it through the metadata server. Model credentials are fetched the same way instead of being baked in. - Per-task setup, such as `git fetch` of the PR branch, runs after the input arrives and before `spec.command` starts. ### 3. Task clones: start from an existing Task's data ```yaml spec: from: task: review-pr-1234 # must be Suspended ``` This maps to Substrate's `CreateTag` on the source actor, then `CreateActor` with `source_tag`. Uses include forking a Task whose environment was prepared by goal-driven setup, speculative branches of one task (the roadmap's "Stateful Task Branching"), and retrying from a known-good point. ## Implementation sketch | Area | Change | |---|---| | API (`ax.proto`) | `TaskTemplate` resource and RPCs. Add `Task.spec.from` (template or task) and `spec.input`. | | Reconciler | Shape-keyed ActorTemplate per `TaskTemplate` revision. Anchored tasks call `CreateActor` against that template. Clones go through `CreateTag` and `CreateActor(source_tag)`. Stop putting task data and credentials in the template env. | | Runner | Tell canary boot and real boot apart. Run warmup only in the canary. Fetch input and credentials at runtime with the actor JWT. Start `spec.command` only on the real actor's first boot. | | ax-server | An endpoint where a Task fetches its own input and credentials, authenticated by actor JWT. | ## Open questions 1. **What Substrate supports, and where the limit is.** A new actor's first boot from a shared golden is Substrate's default: every Actor of a template is first restored from its golden, which is a `Full` capture that includes the golden boot's `/workspace`. So anchored Tasks need no Substrate change; the blockers are on the AX side. The limit is resume after suspend. With `Data` snapshots, resume cold-boots over the Task's own data: `onResume.fromData: Golden` was `microvm`-only, and AX runs on gVisor, and agent-substrate/substrate#2105 (#443) removed `on_resume`. Is warm resume from the golden needed for long-running Tasks, or is `Full` scope the answer there? (Based on the Substrate docs at the version AX pins, `944abe3`; to be confirmed against current Substrate.) 2. **How does this fit #433?** #433 proposes dropping goldens and revisiting `ActorTemplate`. Is a shape-keyed `TaskTemplate` the right abstraction, or should the canary be expressed as an ordinary Task that is suspended and tagged, with anchored Tasks being clones of it? 3. **Tag scope.** Can a tag be used across atespaces (`TagScope`)? Can one shared base serve tasks in many atespaces? 4. **Refresh and rollout.** How does a template follow `main`? Options: scheduled rebuilds, `revision` pinning, and how long old revisions are kept for in-flight Tasks. Old revisions and their goldens also need a cleanup rule, for example deleting them once no Task is anchored to them. 5. **DATA vs FULL.** Clones inherit files only with DATA scope. Should `spec.from.task` allow FULL-scope clones that carry process memory, for agents that need conversational continuity? 6. **Naming.** `TaskTemplate` vs `Golden` vs `TaskClass`. ## Related - #433: Revisit the API server and Task lifecycle - #427: workspace clones run in the golden boot, where egress is blocked - #428: `spec.command` also runs in the golden boot - #443: `snapshot_config.on_resume` was removed in Substrate `6a35150` - #451: suspend sends no signal; only `/workspace` survives - #378: redundant ActorTemplates from status in `AX_TASK_YAML` (closed) - Roadmap: "Stateful Task Branching"

title: Retry and waiting policy for Substrate errors
body:
Several open PRs add handling for Substrate errors at different layers: #457 (adapt to Substrate v0.4, retries in the Substrate client), #463 (transient Substrate unavailability) and #464 (propagate SuspendActor errors). This issue sets one policy so they fit together.

_Updated 14 Oct: #465 (wait for worker capacity) and #367 are closed. AX won't run its own queue; Substrate will own queuing (agent-substrate/substrate#2059) and AX will use it._

**Policy**

- Substrate client (`internal/substrate`): retry only errors where the call is known not to have taken effect, for a few seconds with jittered backoff. That is `Aborted` (busy actor) and `Unavailable` (Substrate not reachable). Use the single retry helper from #457.
- `DeadlineExceeded` is not retried in the client, because the call may have succeeded. It is treated like `Unavailable` at the task level below, and the next attempt goes through the idempotent ensure calls.
- Task level: when client retries run out on `Unavailable` or `DeadlineExceeded`, the task stays `Pending` with `Ready=False, reason=SubstrateUnavailable`, and the error is returned so the caller can retry. It is not marked `Failed` for these.
- `ResourceExhausted` (no free worker) is returned to the caller. AX does not queue or retry it (#367, working as intended).
- ActorTemplate creation errors (`InvalidArgument`, `FailedPrecondition`) are not retried and do not fall back to another template. The task fails with Substrate's reason, so problems like #366 (misleading "actor template not found") don't come back.
- A failed suspend is returned to the caller, and the stored task keeps its previous state (#464).

**Why this split**

- Where a retry lives depends on whether the call could have taken effect. Errors that are safe to repeat and clear in seconds (`Aborted`, `Unavailable`) are retried quickly in the client, where the caller never sees them. Anything that can take minutes (`ResourceExhausted`) or may already have taken effect (`DeadlineExceeded`) moves to the task level, where the state is stored and visible.
- A task hit by a Substrate outage shows `Pending` with a reason, so `ax get` and `ax watch` say why it isn't running, and re-running the resume picks it up.
- No queue in AX. Waiting for capacity belongs in Substrate, the only place that knows when a worker frees up, and anything AX built here would not be forward compatible with it.
- No template fallback while the Substrate API is alpha. A silent fallback runs the task with settings it didn't ask for (for example, it would drop #405's resource limits) and replaces the real error with a misleading one (#366).

**Alternatives considered**

- Retry everything in the Substrate client. Simplest, but a capacity wait can take minutes, which blocks the caller past the 30s resource-lock lease, and repeating a call that may have succeeded is unsafe.
- A background retry loop in AX (#465). Clean, but it is a queue, and Substrate will own queuing. Closed in favour of waiting for that.
- Let each PR handle its own errors. That's what happened, and it produced the stacked retries above and different states for the same failure.
- Chosen: Substrate queues resumes, and AX uses it when it lands (agent-substrate/substrate#2059). Until then, `ResourceExhausted` goes back to the caller.

**Per PR**

- #457: drop the `InvalidArgument` fallback to the base template, and retry `ResumeActor` on `Aborted` only.
- #465: closed, see the note at the top.
- #463: rebase after #457. Add `Unavailable` to #457's retry helper, keep the task `Pending` with `SubstrateUnavailable` and return the error, and keep re-apply of a `Pending` task limited to an unchanged spec.
- #464: as is, plus a test or a note for a failed suspend on the create path.

**Merge order:** #457, then #464, then #463, then #405 (Task resource limits, rebased onto #457).

**Out of scope for now:** queuing for capacity (Substrate will own it), and automatic retry of `Pending` tasks.

If you see a problem with this, comment here by end of Thursday. Otherwise this is the plan.
