title: Task budgets: add spec.budget (active deadline, token ceiling) and populate the unused status.usage
body:
## Problem

AX has no way to bound how long a Task runs or how many tokens it spends. The README names this risk ("can burn money in a loop if nobody is watching"), and `docs/roadmap.md` lists "token/timeout budgets" under Stabilize Core Specs. Today:

- `TaskSpec` (`pkg/apis/v1alpha1/ax.proto`) has no deadline or budget field. A Task stays `Running` until someone runs `ax suspend` or `ax delete`.
- `TaskStatus.usage` (`UsageStats`) and `TaskStatus.pending_approval` are declared, but nothing in `internal/` or `runner/` ever sets them. `ax get task` always shows them empty, which suggests features that don't exist. (`pending_approval` looks like a leftover from the earlier harness architecture, see #111.)
- `internal/workspace/planner.go` calls `model.Client.Generate`, and the response carries `Usage` (`internal/model/client.go:141`), but the value is discarded. AX doesn't count its own platform model spend either.
- `UsageStats` uses `int32`. A long-running agent can pass 2^31 prompt tokens.

## Why this matters

- **Every unattended Task is unbounded.** The only stop today is a human or an external watcher. That works against AX's goal of running very large numbers of tasks, where nobody watches each one.
- **Worker capacity.** A Task stuck in a loop holds its worker indefinitely. On a pool with fewer workers than Tasks, new Tasks fail with `ResourceExhausted` (same symptom as #420, but for Tasks that never exit rather than Tasks that already have).
- **Cost.** Agents call metered model APIs. Without a ceiling, a stuck tool loop is open-ended spend.
- **It's already on the roadmap**, and the status fields already exist in the API. This fills them in rather than adding a new concept.

Example workload: an unattended agent that places outbound calls and holds long conversations against a metered LLM API (for example, candidate screening). A call that never ends or a retry loop is direct cost, and the operator needs AX to enforce a hard limit.

## Proposal

Phased; each phase is useful on its own.

### 1. Active deadline

```yaml
spec:
  budget:
    activeDeadline: 30m   # counts Running time only; Suspended time is excluded
```

When the deadline is exceeded, the runner stops the command (SIGTERM, then the grace period from #446). The Task gets condition `Ready=False, reason=DeadlineExceeded` and then follows `spec.onCompletion` from #420, or moves to `Failed` if #420 hasn't landed.

### 2. Usage reporting

The harness owns model calls; AX doesn't proxy them. So:

- The metadata server gets `POST /metadata/v1alpha1/ax/usage`, which accepts token deltas from the harness.
- The planner's own `Generate` usage is added to the same totals.
- The control plane copies the totals into `status.usage` when it reads task status, next to the exit status proposed in #420 (`/metadata/v1alpha1/ax/status`).
- `UsageStats` fields change to `int64` while the API is still v1alpha1.

### 3. Token ceiling

`spec.budget.maxTokens`. When reported usage crosses it, the Task is stopped the same way as phase 1, with `reason=TokenBudgetExceeded`.

This is cooperative enforcement, since it relies on the harness reporting usage. Strict enforcement would require routing model egress through an AX-controlled gateway, which overlaps with #449 and is probably a separate decision.

### 4. `pending_approval`

Until an approval policy is designed, either remove this field or mark it reserved in v1alpha1, so the API doesn't advertise a feature that isn't there.

## Open questions

- **Where the deadline clock lives.** #451 shows the command restarts after resume, so a runner-side timer would reset every time. Accumulated running time probably needs to live in the Task record (updated on suspend/resume), with the runner told the remaining budget when it starts.
- **Enforcement point.** Since ac23328 there is no background controller. Options are runner-side enforcement only, or reusing the retry loop proposed in #468 as a sweep.
- **Timing relative to #433.** If the lifecycle rework will change how status is stored and reported, phase 1 could land first and phases 2–3 after.
- **Naming.** `budget.activeDeadline` vs. a Kubernetes-style `activeDeadlineSeconds`.

## Related

#420 (completion policy and exit reporting), #346 (status after command exit), #446 (stop grace period), #433 (Task lifecycle revisit), #468 (background loop), #449 (egress), #111 (earlier approval-policy work)

I'm happy to implement phases 1 and 2 once external contributions open (#448). In the meantime I can share a fork branch with the change and tests if that helps the design discussion.

title: fix(controller): fail task when ActorTemplate creation fails
body:
When Substrate rejects the per-task ActorTemplate (most commonly because spec.image is referenced by tag instead of digest), the reconciler only logged a warning and fell back to the default template. In a stock deployment that template does not exist, so the task failed later with a misleading "ActorCreationFailed: actor template not found" and the real cause was only visible in the controller log.

Treat the template error as terminal for the reconcile: set Ready=False with reason TemplateCreationFailed and the Substrate error as the message, set phase Failed, and return. Falling back to a template that carries a different image is never what the user asked for.

Also document the digest requirement under Task in docs/manifests.md and add a regression test that reproduces the tag-referenced image case.

Ref: https://github.com/ericcurtin/ax/tree/fix/terminal-template-creation-failure

title: server,controller: bound task reconciliation deadline under the task lock TTL
body:
## Problem

Follow-up from [#463 (review)](https://github.com/google/ax/pull/463#pullrequestreview-2372947284) and #468.

In `internal/substrate/client.go`, `retryOnCodes` retries `codes.Unavailable` and `codes.Aborted` for up to `defaultRetryAttempts = 10` (`defaultRetryInterval = 200ms`, `maxRetryInterval = 2s` with jitter), meaning a single Substrate RPC can take up to ~6s–20s before exhausting retries.

Meanwhile, in `internal/lock/lock.go`, `NewRedisLocker` acquires the per-task lock with a fixed `30s` TTL (`ttl = 30 * time.Second`) and no renewal. Because `Reconcile` performs multiple sequential Substrate RPCs (`EnsureAtespace`, `EnsureActorTemplateWithImage`, `EnsureActor`, `SuspendActor`/`ResumeActor`, plus `defaultWorkspaceReadyTimeout = 15s`), if Substrate flaps mid-request across more than one step, a single reconciliation can outlast the 30s task lock TTL while still mutating Substrate and task status in the store.

## Proposed Solution

Enforce a per-request / reconciliation context deadline bounded under the task lock TTL (e.g. deriving a `context.WithTimeout` after acquiring the task lock in `CreateTask`, `ResumeTask`, `SuspendTask`, and `DeleteTask`, or bounding the reconcile budget relative to the lock TTL) so that an in-flight reconcile cannot continue operating on a task after its lock has expired.

title: test: add Kind-based E2E test suite and CI workflow
body:
Adds an end-to-end test suite that runs AX against a real Substrate install in a local Kind cluster, plus a GitHub Actions workflow to run it.

### What's included
- **Test suite** (`test/e2e/`): Go tests covering the Workspace/Model CRUD, the task lifecycle and its sync with Substrate Actors/ActorTemplates,
  suspend/resume persistence, `ax ssh` and the in-sandbox metadata server, multi-workspace + git setup, WatchTask, and atespace isolation. The tests are skipped by
  `go test ./...` unless `--e2e` / `AX_E2E=true` is set.
- **Scripts** (`hack/`): `setup-e2e-kind.sh` provisions Kind + Substrate (at `SUBSTRATE_REF`, defaulting to the version in go.mod) + AX; `run-e2e.sh`, `run-
  e2e-kind.sh` and `cleanup-e2e-kind.sh` run the tests and tear the cluster down.
- **Make targets**: `test-e2e`, `test-e2e-head` (Substrate `main`), `e2e-setup`, `e2e-run`, `e2e-cleanup`.
- **CI** (`.github/workflows/e2e.yml`): PRs and pushes run against the Substrate version in go.mod, so unreleased Substrate changes never block PRs. A nightly
  run tests Substrate `main` to catch incompatibilities early. Manual runs accept any ref.

### Small production changes
- `AX_DEFAULT_TASK_IMAGE` overrides the default task image (used to point E2E at a locally built image), via `substrate.DefaultTaskImage()`.
- `Dockerfile.task-runner` takes a `TARGETARCH` build arg.
- The `ax suspend` / `ax resume` CLI timeout goes from 15s to 60s.

### Testing
- `make test-e2e`: 8/8 tests pass against Substrate at the go.mod version (`f6a1dc72`).
- `make test-e2e-head`: the 5 task tests fail against Substrate `main`. This is expected: substrate#2586 changed `sandbox_class` from enum to string. this e2e test is designed to catch that. A separate PR to bump the version will fix that.

title: Credentials via egress injection: keep real keys out of tasks (rotation + multi-tenant)
body:
## Summary

I think we're going to need a proper story for credentials in tasks. Ideally the agent never holds the real key at all. Substrate already has the pieces for this with [egress credential injection](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/blob/main/docs/egress-credential-injection.md): the agent sends a placeholder header, and the egress gateway swaps in the real credential on the way out. AX should lean on that.

This builds on #449, since AX needs to be creating egress policies first.

## What it could look like

Tasks, Models and Workspaces reference secrets instead of carrying values:

```yaml
kind: Model
spec:
  provider: gemini
  model: gemini-2.5-pro
  secretKey: { name: gemini-credentials, key: api-key }
---
kind: Workspace
spec:
  git:
    - repo: https://github.com/acme/private-repo
      credentialRef: { name: github-acme, key: token }
---
kind: Task
spec:
  env:
    - name: STRIPE_API_KEY
      secretRef:
        name: stripe
        key: api-key
        inject: { host: api.stripe.com, header: Authorization, prefix: "Bearer " }
```

AX turns those into rules on the actor's egress policy:

```yaml
rules:
- https:
    hostnames: ["generativelanguage.googleapis.com"]
    effects:
      replaceHeaders:
      - header: x-goog-api-key
        credentialUri: ate-secret://k8s.io/default/team-a/gemini-credentials/api-key
```

Inside the sandbox the agent just sees `GEMINI_API_KEY=ax-placeholder`, so SDKs still work. Git over HTTPS works the same way with a placeholder `Authorization` header.

## Key rotation

Since everything is a reference, rotating a key should just be updating the secret. No template rebuilds, nothing baked into snapshots. Substrate's Kubernetes provider looks like it reads the Secret per request, so a rotation should take effect pretty quickly. Worth confirming whether the gateway caches anything.

## Multi-tenant / many keys to many tasks

- Tenants define their Models and secrets in their own atespace. The same Model can be shared by lots of tasks, and one task can pull in several keys.
- Substrate's provider already scopes atespace → secret namespace, so `team-a` can't resolve `team-b`'s secrets even if it names them.
- AX should check that mapping up front when a Task is created, rather than letting it fail on the first request.

A few things we'd probably want to raise with Substrate:
- The namespace policy only reloads on a provider restart, which gets painful with lots of tenants.
- One task can't use two different credentials for the same host (say two GitHub tokens for different orgs).

## Limits

- HTTP(S) headers only. SSH git, raw TCP databases, signing keys etc. would need something else, probably short-lived scoped tokens.
- The golden boot doesn't get the actor's egress policy (#427), so setup that needs credentials has to happen on the real boot.

## Rough phases

1. #449: AX creates the egress policy
2. Model credentials through the gateway
3. Workspace git credentials
4. `env[].secretRef` for arbitrary APIs
5. Rotation and multi-tenant polish

## Open questions

- Does AX own the egress policy outright, or merge its rules into one the user provides?
- Default to the Kubernetes provider, or make it a per-cluster choice (k8s, Secret Manager, Vault)?
- A built-in table of header/prefix for common providers (Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub), with an override?

Related: #449, #427, #467, #454

title: Controller fails open in two places: a failed custom ActorTemplate falls back to the default template, and any secret-lookup error falls back to the server-wide API key
deploy: cluster-wide `secrets` get/list/watch for ax-server, unauthenticated Redis, and a personal dev-project bucket as the snapshot default
body:
**Version:** `main` at 0cbfc3d (#469). All three items are visible from the committed manifests and defaults; I have not deployed them to a cluster, so effects that depend on cluster-side policy are marked as such.

### 1. ax-server's ClusterRole can read every secret in the cluster

`deploy/ax-server.yaml:27-45` binds the `ax-server` service account to:

```yaml
kind: ClusterRole
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["secrets"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
```

The only secret access I find in the code is a single GET of a fixed-name secret plus a `kubectl get secret` fallback: `internal/model/client.go:345` (`/api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/secrets/<name>`) and `:372`, called through `TaskReconciler.SecretResolver` with `gemini-api-secret` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` (`internal/controller/reconciler.go:42-43,89`). Nothing lists or watches secrets. `list` returns secret data, so as written a compromise of the ax-server process or any request-driven path that reaches the API with its token exposes every secret in every namespace.

Suggested direction (untested): `verbs: ["get"]` with `resourceNames: ["gemini-api-secret"]` (still cluster-scoped because atespaces map to namespaces, but only that name), or a per-atespace `Role`/`RoleBinding` created with the atespace. If Model `secretKey` names are meant to be resolved by the server later (docs/manifests.md shows `anthropic-api-secret`), the names would need to be listed or the design stated.

### 2. The Redis deployment has no authentication, TLS or network restriction

`deploy/redis.yaml`: `redis:7-alpine` with no `--requirepass`/ACL, a ClusterIP Service on 6379, and no NetworkPolicy anywhere in the repo (`grep -ri networkpolicy` is empty). `deploy/ax-server.yaml` passes no password: `--redis-password` defaults to `""` (`cmd/ax-server/main.go:53`) and the manifest sets neither the flag nor `REDIS_PASSWORD`.

Redis is the task/workspace/model store and the lock backend (`internal/store`, `internal/lock`), and the reconciler acts on what the store returns. So any pod that can reach `ax-redis.ax-system.svc.cluster.local:6379` can read task specs (including `spec.env` values) and write or alter them. If the cluster has default-deny network policies or a mesh in front, this is mitigated outside the repo; the manifests as committed don't say so.

Suggested direction: set a password from a Secret in both manifests, add a NetworkPolicy allowing only ax-server to reach Redis, or label `deploy/redis.yaml` as dev-only if that is the intent.

### 3. A developer's project bucket is the compiled-in snapshot default

- `internal/substrate/client.go:211`: `DefaultSnapshotsBucket = "gs://dberkov-gke-dev3/ate-env/"`, used in `BuildActorTemplate` whenever `snapshotsBucket` is empty and `AX_SNAPSHOTS_BUCKET` is unset (`:274-282`).
- `deploy/ax-server.yaml:83-84` sets `AX_SNAPSHOTS_BUCKET` to the same value.
- `demo.sh:39` defaults the task image to `gcr.io/dberkov-gke-dev3/ax-task-runner@sha256:...`.

`docs/runner.md:26` says Substrate snapshots `/workspace` on suspend, and the roadmap mentions checkpointed memory. So a deployment that follows the repo and doesn't override the variable points its suspend snapshots at that bucket. What happens depends on the bucket's access policy, which I can't see: either the writes fail, or they succeed into a project the deployer doesn't control. It also exposes an internal dev project name in a public repo.

Suggested direction: no compiled-in default (fail with a clear error when the bucket isn't configured), a placeholder in the manifest, and `AX_IMAGE_REPO` required or defaulted to the public image already named in `v1alpha1.DefaultTaskImage` for `demo.sh`.

### Not checked

Actual cluster behaviour (RBAC effect, NetworkPolicies outside the repo, the bucket's IAM), whether Substrate itself constrains the snapshot location, and whether any of this already has an issue. Related but separate: the API server itself has no authentication (#TODO link if filed).

I'm glad to split this into separate issues or send small patches if you prefer.

title: Document the current trust boundary (the API has no authN/authZ and atespaces are not an isolation boundary), and add a SECURITY.md
body:
**Version:** `main` at 0cbfc3d (#469). I know the README warns about heavy development and `docs/roadmap.md` §4 lists SPIFFE identity and governance as future work. This is not a request to ship that now. It is a request to state, in the docs, what the boundary is today, because the code and the docs together leave it easy to get wrong, and because I could not find a place to report security issues.

### What the code does today

- **No authentication or authorization on the API.** `internal/server/server.go:69` builds `grpc.NewServer()` with no options, and there are no interceptors anywhere in `cmd/` or `internal/`. The repo's own `TestServerGRPC` (`internal/server/server_test.go:60`) creates a Workspace, a Model and a Task and then deletes them, all with `insecure.NewCredentials()` and no token.
- **Clients don't present credentials either.** `cmd/ax/main.go:200` and `internal/guest/client.go:49` both dial with `insecure.NewCredentials()`. The only thing sent to the router is the routing header `ate-target-actor: <atespace>/<task>` (`internal/guest/client.go:50-57`; `docs/networking.md`).
- **Atespace is a free, client-chosen string.** `ValidateObjectMeta` only checks it is an RFC 1123 label; `ListTasks` with an empty atespace lists every atespace (`internal/server/server.go`, `ListTasks`). The server resolves `gemini-api-secret` in whatever atespace the task names (`reconciler.go:153-155,353-366`).
- **`ax ssh` takes everything from the unauthenticated API.** It reads the task and worker IP via `GetTask`, then runs commands through the guest services directly or via a port-forward to `atenet-router` (`cmd/ax/main.go:962-1060`). The `spec.debug` flag that enables guest services (`internal/metadata/server.go:71`; `docs/sandbox.md` says they allow arbitrary process execution) is set by whoever creates the Task.

### Why it matters (by code reading; not run on a cluster)

Put together, a caller who can reach `ax-server:8080` (or who may `kubectl port-forward` to it) can:

1. create a Task with `spec.debug: true` in any atespace they name;
2. have ax-server read `gemini-api-secret` from that atespace with its service account (and fall back to the server-wide key otherwise) and inject the key into the task's environment;
3. `ax ssh` into the task and read it.

Each step is in the code above; I have not executed the chain end to end. If that's right, atespaces don't separate tenants from each other, and Kubernetes RBAC on the Service and port-forward is the only access control. That may well be the intended alpha posture. It just isn't written anywhere that I could find: `grep -ri "auth\|tenant\|trust boundary" *.md docs/` finds only the roadmap's SPIFFE item and an unrelated `:authority` header note.

### Request

1. A short "Security model / current limitations" section (README or `docs/`) stating: who can reach the API, that there is no authN/authZ yet, that atespaces are naming scopes and not isolation, and that `spec.debug` gives interactive execution in the sandbox to anyone who can create the task.
2. A `SECURITY.md` with a reporting channel (the repo has none; `.github/` contains only `workflows/`).
3. Optionally, a minimal interim control before SPIFFE lands, such as a bearer-token or Kubernetes TokenReview interceptor on ax-server with atespace-scoped authorization. Whatever you prefer; I'd rather not guess at the design.

Related: the deploy manifests give ax-server cluster-wide read on secrets and leave Redis unauthenticated (separate issue, link to follow). A related fail-open fallback in the reconciler is in a separate issue as well.

title: feat(runner): serve metadata endpoints on loopback only
body:
The /metadata/v1alpha1/ax/* endpoints share port 80 with the probes. Port 80 is what Agent Substrate's router forwards to, so anything that can reach a task through the router can read its
  metadata, including its Task spec with spec.env values and its Workspace specs. Suspended tasks are also resumed to serve those requests. The metadata endpoints are only meant for the task's
  own command, so there's no reason for them to be reachable from outside the sandbox.

  What changed

  - The runner now runs two listeners:
    - :80 serves only /healthz, /readyz, and the guest services when spec.debug is set.
    - 127.0.0.1:8099 (loopback only, --metadata-port to change) serves /metadata/v1alpha1/ax/task and /workspaces.
  - AX_METADATA_URL points at the loopback listener, so agents that use it need no changes.
  - Runner contract docs (docs/runner.md, docs/sandbox.md) now say to serve metadata on loopback. The docs/networking.md router example uses /readyz instead of metadata.
  - New test: the metadata paths return 404 on the probe port, and the metadata port refuses connections on non-loopback addresses.

  Notes

  - Port 8099 was chosen to avoid ports agents commonly use (8080/8081). Happy to change it.
  - Custom runners that serve metadata on port 80 keep working. The updated contract asks them to move it to loopback.
  - Follow-ups, not in this PR:
    - drop spec.env values from the metadata response
    - authorization at the router level, since probes on :80 can still wake a suspended task

title: docs: add SECURITY.md with reporting process and current trust boundary
body:
Adds a repo-level SECURITY.md so the reporting process is visible in the repo itself, not only through the google org default. The reporting text is the same as the org's.

It also states the current trust boundary, as asked in #478: the API has no authentication or authorization, atespaces are not a tenant isolation boundary, and anything inside a task's sandbox is untrusted.

Docs only.

title: Name the mascot
Workspace git clones fail because egress waits on the /readyz wakeup probe
body:
Workspace git clones never work on Substrate with egress enabled. The task still comes up `Ready`, just without its repo.

**Why**

Substrate turns on an actor's egress only after its wakeup probe passes (`ateom-gvisor` calls `tunnel.Activate` after `wakeupprobe.WaitAll`). AX sets the wakeup probe to `/readyz`, which returns 503 until workspace setup is done, and setup is what clones the repos. So the clone always runs before the actor has any network. atunnel closes the connection and git fails:

```
fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/chalk/chalk.git/': GnuTLS, handshake failed: The TLS connection was non-properly terminated.
```

After five retries `SetupWorkspace` gives up but returns nil, so the runner marks the workspace ready anyway. The probe passes, egress comes up, and the command starts. `ax describe` shows `WorkspaceReady=True` with nothing checked out. A `git ls-remote` from `ax ssh` a few seconds later works with the same egress policy, so it's not the policy.

**Repro**

kind with Substrate f6a1dc72 (the version in go.mod), a Workspace with any public repo in `spec.git`, and an egress policy on the task's actor allowing `github.com` (`tlsPassthrough`, port 443). Resume the task and check the runner logs for `git fetch error (continuing setup)`.

**Fix**

I have a fix on my fork: https://github.com/zlareb1/ax/commit/1daf54afb1defbee33e6b2c2433eb7fc14c615d2 (branch [`fix-workspace-egress`](https://github.com/google/ax/compare/main...zlareb1:ax:fix-workspace-egress)). It's small:

- the wakeup probe uses `/healthz`, so egress is up during setup. The reconciler already polls `/readyz` itself for `WorkspaceReady`, so that condition is unchanged;
- `SetupWorkspace` returns an error when a repo fails to fetch, so a failed clone isn't reported ready. The marker is still skipped, so the next boot retries;
- the readyz poll in `Reconcile` stops 2s before the caller's deadline. Without this, resuming a task whose workspace stays unready fails with `updating task status: getting task from redis: context deadline exceeded`, since the poll takes the full 15s `ax resume` allows.

With it, the repo clones on the first try and the task is `Ready`. A repo that doesn't exist leaves `WorkspaceReady=False` (the command still starts), and `ax resume` returns normally in both cases. `go test ./...` passes and each new test fails without its fix.

I'd have opened a PR, but external PRs aren't accepted right now (#448), so I'm raising it here instead. Happy to open the PR once contributions are open, or feel free to pick up the commit directly.

title: server,controller: bound task reconciliation deadline under the task lock TTL
body:
## Summary

Follow-up from [#463 (review)](https://github.com/google/ax/pull/463#pullrequestreview-2372947284) and #468.

Because `retryOnCodes` in `internal/substrate/client.go` can retry `codes.Unavailable` and `codes.Aborted` for up to ~6s–20s per RPC, a single task reconciliation that encounters Substrate flapping across multiple sequential RPCs (`EnsureAtespace`, `EnsureActorTemplateWithImage`, `EnsureActor`, `SuspendActor`/`ResumeActor`, plus workspace polling) could exceed the fixed 30s Redis task lock TTL (`lock.DefaultTTL`) while still mutating Substrate and store state.

## Changes

- **`internal/lock/lock.go`:** Export `lock.DefaultTTL = 30 * time.Second`.
- **`internal/server/server.go`:**
  - Define `server.DefaultReconcileTimeout = lock.DefaultTTL - 5*time.Second` (`25s`, configurable via `server.Options.ReconcileTimeout`).
  - Derive `context.WithTimeout(ctx, s.reconcileTimeout)` for `Reconcile` and `ReconcileDelete` in `CreateTask`, `ResumeTask`, `SuspendTask`, and `DeleteTask` after acquiring the task lock so an in-flight reconciliation aborts with `context.DeadlineExceeded` before the 30s lock expires, leaving headroom to persist the resulting task status while the lock is still held.
- **`internal/controller/reconciler.go`:**
  - When `SuspendActor` fails transiently (or hits `context.DeadlineExceeded`) during initial task creation, record `Phase: Pending` and `Ready=False (Reason: SubstrateUnavailable)`.
  - Exit the `deleteTaskTemplates` retry loop immediately when the context is canceled or expires.
- **`internal/server/server_test.go` & `internal/controller/reconciler_test.go`:**
  - Add `TestServer_ReconcileTimeoutBoundedUnderLockTTL` covering reconcile timeout behavior across `CreateTask`, `ResumeTask`, `SuspendTask`, and `DeleteTask`.
  - Add reconcile deadline coverage in `TestTaskReconciler_TransientSubstrateUnavailable`.

Fixes #473

title: Clean up v1alpha1 field names and drop unused fields
body:
- ModelSpec: drop the reserved ranges left over from the typed generation settings and renumber secret_key (6 -> 3) and parameters (7 -> 4).
- TaskStatus: remove pending_approval and usage, along with the PendingApproval and UsageStats messages. Nothing set or read them.
- Rename ResourceReqs to ResourcesSpec.
- Rename Condition.last_transition_time to update_time and ObjectMeta.creation_timestamp to create_time, following the AIP timestamp naming. update_time also matches what the controller does: setCondition refreshes it on every update, not only when the status changes.
- Add a TODO to reconsider WorkspaceRef.goal.

This is a breaking change. The ModelSpec renumbering changes the wire format, so the ax CLI and ax-server must be upgraded together. The JSON/YAML keys lastTransitionTime and creationTimestamp become updateTime and createTime; records already stored in Redis load without those timestamps, and the server re-stamps the creation time on the next update.

title: Let a Task choose its snapshot scope, and document what survives a suspend
body:
## Problem

AX hardcodes the snapshot fidelity for every Task (`PreferredFidelity: SNAPSHOT_FIDELITY_VOLUMES` in `internal/substrate/client.go`). With Substrate main, a resume from a volumes-only snapshot starts the containers fresh from the image and restores only the durable directories. Anything running at suspend time is gone: an agent comes back with its files under `/workspace`, but the tool call it was running shows as interrupted.

A plain Substrate actor with full fidelity keeps its processes across suspends, including a wake on another node. AX tasks can't ask for that, and the docs don't say which behavior a Task gets.

#457 described volumes fidelity as equivalent to the previous behavior. On Substrate main it isn't: since agent-substrate/substrate#2105, the golden snapshot's memory no longer comes back on a data resume either. Combined with #428, the task command also starts again on every resume.

## Reproduce

Apply a Task whose command is `sleep 60`, suspend it 20 s in, wait, and resume it. The command is not running after the resume.

## Ask

- Document what survives `ax suspend` and `ax resume` today: files, memory, processes.
- Add a snapshot scope on the Task (volumes or full), passed to the ActorTemplate, defaulting to today's behavior.

The Substrate v0.5 bump (#484) changes the snapshot fields, so this should build on that.

title: Release hygiene: publish images with each release and state which Substrate release AX works with
body:
## Problem

Getting a working AX install today means building images and pairing versions by reading both codebases:

- No ax-server or ax-task-runner images are published with releases. The manifest references ax-server with a `ko://` path, and the default task image isn't public (#424).
- Nothing states which Substrate release an AX commit works with. AX's latest release is v0.3.1, main has since moved to the Substrate v0.4 API (#457) against an untagged Substrate commit, and #484 moves to v0.5.0. Pairing them wrong fails with a misleading error (#443, #366).
- `go install github.com/google/ax/cmd/ax@latest` installs the v0.3.1 CLI, which calls an RPC the server on main no longer has (#398).

## Ask

- Publish ax-server and ax-task-runner images for each release, referenced by digest in the install manifests.
- Add a compatibility table to the installation docs (linked from the README and CONTRIBUTING): AX release to Substrate release.
- Cut AX releases against Substrate releases, and tag a release whenever the CLI and server stop matching.

title: Add labels or an owner field to Tasks, with label filtering on ListTasks
body:
## Problem

`ObjectMeta` holds only a name, an atespace and a creation time. A platform that runs Tasks for many users has no way to record who a Task belongs to, so it can't find a user's Tasks after a restart, cap Tasks per user, or split cost per user, without encoding ownership in env values or names.

Env values are a poor place for it: they end up in the ActorTemplate and in the runner's metadata, so anything sensitive put there leaks.

## Ask

Labels on `ObjectMeta` (or an owner field), stored by ax-server and not passed into the sandbox, and a label selector on `ListTasks`.

This touches the v1alpha1 API, so it should line up with the field cleanup in #485.

title: Suspend running Tasks when their worker is evicted, instead of stopping the command
body:
## Problem

When a worker pod is evicted (node drain, node upgrade, worker pool change), Substrate sends the actor SIGTERM and gives the harness a window to suspend it before the actor is killed. Everything since the last snapshot is lost after that.

AX's runner treats SIGTERM as a shutdown: `cmd/ax-task-runner/main.go` cancels on SIGTERM, and the runner then stops the task command (SIGTERM, a grace period, SIGKILL) and exits. Nothing in ax-server suspends the Task. A node drain therefore stops every running Task's command and loses its work since the last snapshot. On the next resume, AX reverts the crashed actor to that snapshot.

This is from reading the code on main. An eviction hasn't been run against it.

## Ask

Keep the runner alive on SIGTERM, and have ax-server suspend the Task within Substrate's eviction window, as Substrate's eviction guidance asks of a harness.

Related: #446 (SIGTERM grace period) and #451 (what suspend does to the command).

title: lock,cli: renew Redis lock leases and lengthen suspend/resume timeout
body:
## Summary

Split out from #474 per review discussion (https://github.com/google/ax/pull/474#issuecomment-6203360157).

Suspend/resume hold the per-task lock across Substrate snapshot/restore, which for microVM sandboxes can exceed both the CLI's 15s deadline and the 30s Redis lock TTL. Once the TTL lapsed, another request could take the lock while the first was still mutating the task.

- **Redis lock renewal:** `RedisLocker` now renews a held lease every TTL/3 (token-checked via Lua script) until unlock, so the TTL only bounds how long a crashed holder's lock lingers. The rationale for renewal over a single long TTL is documented on `RedisLocker`.
- **CLI timeout:** Raise the CLI suspend/resume RPC timeout to 5 minutes (`lifecycleRPCTimeout`).
- **Tests:** Add a Redis-backed renewal test (`TestRedisLocker_RenewsLeaseWhileHeld`), skipped unless `REDIS_ADDR` is set.

Relates to #483.

title: Allow creating a task from an actor template
body:
Add an optional `template` field to `TaskSpec` that references a Substrate ActorTemplate. A task sets at most one of `image` and `template`:

- If `image` is set, the task runs from that image, as today.
- If `template` is set, the task runs from the referenced template.
- If neither is set, keep today's default (`DefaultTaskImage`).

The API server rejects a Task that sets both `image` and `template`. It also rejects `command` together with `template`, because the template defines what runs.

## Example

```yaml
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Task
metadata:
  name: lint
  atespace: default
spec:
  # The actor is created from this ActorTemplate.
  template:
    name: node-agent
    atespace: ax-system  # optional, defaults to the task's atespace
  workspaces:
    - name: default-workspace
```

Rejected at apply time:

```yaml
spec:
  image: gcr.io/ax-substrate/ate-images/ax-task-runner:latest
  template:  # error: set image or template, not both
    name: node-agent
```

```proto
message TaskSpec {
  // ...existing fields 1-6...

  // template references the Substrate ActorTemplate to run the task from.
  // It can't be combined with image or command.
  ObjectRef template = 7;
}

// ObjectRef references a resource by name.
message ObjectRef {
  string name = 1;
  // atespace defaults to the referencing resource's atespace.
  string atespace = 2;
}
```

title: Rename ax ssh to ax exec, introduce ax cp
body:
`ax ssh <task> [-- command...]` doesn't open an SSH session. It starts a process in the task's container through the Agent Substrate guest process service and streams the process's stdout and stderr back, which is what `kubectl exec` does. The `ssh` name suggests keys, an sshd in the sandbox, or an interactive login, and none of those apply.

It isn't interactive either. The README describes `ax ssh task123` as an interactive shell, but `guest.ExecOptions` has no stdin or TTY, so the `/bin/sh` that runs when no command is given can't read anything you type.

There's also no way to copy files into or out of a sandbox, which `kubectl cp` covers for pods.

## Proposal

### `ax exec`

Rename `ax ssh` to `ax exec` and follow `kubectl exec` conventions:

```sh
ax exec task123 -- ls -la /workspace
ax exec -a my-atespace task123 -- python3 main.py
ax exec task123 -- sh -c 'cd /workspace && git status'
```

- `--` is required between the task name and the command, as with `kubectl exec`. Today it's optional.
- A command is required, as with `kubectl exec`. Today a missing command defaults to `/bin/sh`, which isn't useful without stdin.
- The existing checks stay: the task must be `Running` and have `spec.debug: true`.

### `ax cp`

Add `ax cp`, following `kubectl cp`: one argument is a local path, the other is `<task>:<path>`, and it copies from the first argument to the second.

```sh
ax cp task123:/workspace/report.json ./report.json  # from the sandbox
ax cp ./config.yaml task123:/workspace/config.yaml  # into the sandbox
ax cp my-atespace/task123:/workspace/out.log .       # atespace/task, like kubectl's namespace/pod
```

title: Prebuilt images
body:
Once TaskSpec is finalized, publish prebuilt Task images for common workloads, so running one doesn't require writing and maintaining a Dockerfile:

- **Antigravity**: runs a program that uses the Antigravity SDK.
- **Claude Code**: Node.js and the `claude` CLI (`@anthropic-ai/claude-code`).
- **Codex**: Node.js and the `codex` CLI (`@openai/codex`).
- **Jupyter**: Python with Jupyter installed, so a task can run notebooks, for example with `jupyter nbconvert --execute`.
- **Browser**: Playwright with headless Chromium, for web-browsing agents and end-to-end tests of web apps.

The images take care of the plumbing: MCP servers, skills, and other configuration declared in the task's Workspaces are set up in each harness automatically, so users don't have to configure every agent themselves.

```yaml
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Task
metadata:
  name: fix-tests
spec:
  image: gcr.io/ax-substrate/ate-images/claude-code  # name to be decided
  command: ["claude", "-p", "Fix the failing tests"]
  workspaces:
    - name: default-workspace
```

## API server

The coding agent images (Antigravity, Claude Code, and Codex) can also expose an API server, so clients can interact with the agent running in a task instead of only passing it a prompt through `command`. The protocol is TBD.

> 

Ask

_Originally posted by @rewalwer89-ship-it in https://github.com/rewalwer89-ship-it/mern-interview-sets-pdf/issues/2#issuecomment-6093943661_

title: Allow only one workspace per task
body:
`TaskSpec.workspaces` is a repeated field right now, so a task can bind several workspaces. Each one is mounted at its own path under `/workspace` (or at a custom path), and the first entry becomes the working directory. We should change this so a task binds **at most one** workspace.

### Motivation

- **Combining filesystems is hard.** Each workspace is its own durable filesystem. Mounting several into one task means handling mount layout, path conflicts, nested paths, and snapshot/restore across all of them. A partial failure while mounting or persisting leaves the task in a state that's hard to reason about.
- **It isn't very useful.** Tasks work against a single working directory, which today is just the first entry. Users who need content from several sources can put it all in one workspace (e.g. via `spec.files`).

### Proposal

- Replace `repeated WorkspaceRef workspaces = 5` in `TaskSpec` with a singular `WorkspaceRef workspace`.
- Leave a task with no workspace working as it does now: it gets an empty working directory at `/workspace`.

title: api,runner: bind at most one workspace per task
body:
Replace the repeated TaskSpec.workspaces field with a singular WorkspaceRef workspace. Mounting several durable filesystems into one task meant handling mount layout, path conflicts, and partial setup failures, and tasks only ever worked in the first entry anyway. Users who need content from several sources can put it all in one Workspace.

- TaskSpec: replace `repeated WorkspaceRef workspaces = 5` with `WorkspaceRef workspace = 5`. The WorkspaceRefs and WorkspacePaths helpers become a single WorkspacePath, and ValidateTask drops the duplicate name and path checks.
- A binding without a path is mounted at /workspace rather than /workspace/<name>. A task with no workspace still gets an empty working directory at /workspace.
- runner: Config.Workspaces becomes Config.Workspace. The runner sets up one workspace and runs the command there.
- controller,server: Reconcile takes a single *Workspace. The bound Workspace is injected as AX_WORKSPACE_YAML, one document, instead of the AX_WORKSPACES_YAML stream.
- metadata: serve the bound Workspace at /metadata/v1alpha1/ax/workspace (404 when none) instead of a stream at .../workspaces.
- ax-task-runner: --workspace-file is no longer repeatable.
- Update docs, README, and examples/task.yaml for the new shape.

This is a breaking change. Manifests using the spec.workspaces list are rejected as an unknown field, and custom runners must read AX_WORKSPACE_YAML. The ax CLI and ax-server must be upgraded together.

Fixes #495.

title: Tasks fail on Substrate after v0.5.0: ActorTemplate.sandbox_config removed, resources and digest-pinned images required
body:
## Summary

AX `8d2ccf3` (current `main`) cannot create tasks on Agent Substrate after `v0.5.0`. With `agent-substrate/substrate@3d3b929` (2026-10-18), every Task fails at template creation. There is also no way to run tasks on a non-gVisor sandbox class such as `microvm`.

## What changed in Substrate

In `pkg/proto/ateapipb/ateapi.proto`, `ActorTemplate` changed in four ways:

1. **`sandbox_config` (field 6) was removed.** The WorkerPool now decides the sandbox class, and templates choose a pool through `worker_selector`.
2. **`resources` is required.** cpu and memory limits are both mandatory.
3. **Container images must be pinned by digest.**
4. **The Go module moved** from `github.com/agent-substrate/substrate` to `go.ate.dev/substrate`. `WakeupProbe` and `HttpGetAction` were renamed.

## Repro

- GKE 1.36; Substrate `3d3b929` installed with `hack/install-ate.sh --deploy-ate-system`.
- AX `8d2ccf3` deployed with `make deploy`.
- Apply a minimal Task:

```yaml
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Task
metadata:
  name: smoke1
  atespace: default
spec:
  resources:
    limits:
      cpu: "2"
      memory: "4Gi"
```

`ax-server` logs:

```
could not create custom ActorTemplate, falling back to default template
  error="creating actor template default/smoke1-tmpl-49b5e690: rpc error: code = InvalidArgument
  desc = actor_template: Invalid value: unknown field with protobuf tag 6"
direct reconcile error on create task task=smoke1
  error="ensuring actor: creating actor default/smoke1: rpc error: code = FailedPrecondition desc = actor template not found"
```

Once field 6 is gone, Substrate rejects the template again unless `resources` is set and the image has a `@sha256:` digest. The default `gcr.io/ax-substrate/ate-images/ax-task-runner` is tag-only.

## Related

- #484 bumps to `v0.5.0`. That release still has `sandbox_config`, so this break comes with the next bump.
- #405 copies Task limits onto the template. That covers point 2.
- #487 asks AX to state which Substrate release it supports; this issue is an example of why.
- #372 (hard-coded snapshot bucket) and #437 (quick start never creates a WorkerPool) came up on the same install.

## Possible fix

`BuildActorTemplate` in `internal/substrate/client.go` would:
- drop `SandboxConfig`;
- set `Resources` from the Task's limits;
- set `WorkerSelector` from configuration, so an operator can route tasks to a pool of a given class (for example, `ax.dev/pool=microvm`).

We're running a minimal version of this against Substrate `3d3b929`: https://github.com/gethamster/ax/commit/43fd8d53538e7f1e7cb6e96d647f59b2558a15a5. It uses an `AX_WORKER_SELECTOR` env var, falls back to requests and then 2 CPU / 4Gi for limits, and passes `go test ./...`.

We'd be glad to send a PR, either on top of #405/#484 or as a standalone change, once you confirm the direction. In particular: should the worker selector be a server flag, a per-Task field, or both?

title: feat(api): add egress, secret-backed env vars, and SecretStore to the API
body:
First step for #475: the API for egress hosts and secret-backed env vars, with no behavior change yet. Splitting this up so the API shape can be reviewed on its own before anything acts on it.

## What's in here

**`TaskSpec.egress.hosts`**: the outbound hosts a task may reach (TLS on 443, `*.` prefix for subdomains).

**`EnvVar.secretRef`**: an env var backed by a secret instead of a literal value. The task gets a placeholder, and the secret is meant to be injected into outbound requests by Substrate's egress gateway. `inject` mirrors Substrate's `CredentialHeader` (header + prefix), plus the host it applies to:

```yaml
env:
  - name: STRIPE_API_KEY
    secretRef:
      name: stripe
      key: api-key
      # store: default
      inject:
        host: api.stripe.com
        header: Authorization
        prefix: "Bearer "
```

**`SecretStore`**: a new atespace-scoped resource for where an atespace's secrets live, so tasks just name a secret and the atespace decides the backend. v1 has a Kubernetes Secrets backend only (`spec.kubernetes.namespace`, defaulting to the atespace name). Get/List/Update/Delete RPCs are defined.

Validation covers hostnames, header names, mutually exclusive `value`/`secretRef`, URI-safe secret names and keys, and the same header injected twice for one host.

## Nothing acts on it yet

- `CreateTask` returns `Unimplemented` for tasks that set `egress` or `secretRef`, so nothing runs without the network or credentials it asked for.
- The `SecretStore` RPCs are unimplemented.

## Coming next

The rest of the stack is tracked on #475:

1. **This PR**: API
2. SecretStore storage, server CRUD, CLI, and the Substrate credential provider setup docs
3. Actor egress policies from `egress.hosts` plus the egress trust bundle (#449)
4. Credential injection for `secretRef`

## Notes

- `ax_grpc.pb.go` was regenerated with protoc 5.28.2 to match `ax.pb.go`, so its header version line changes.
- `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` pass.

title: A task can't serve its own API to anything outside its sandbox
body:
### What happens

A lot of agents are servers. They accept chat sessions, A2A calls, MCP requests or webhooks. When an agent like that runs as an AX Task on Agent Substrate, nothing outside the sandbox can reach it.

The reason is that Substrate's router only delivers requests to the runner, on port 80, and the runner only answers its own health checks. A request meant for the agent reaches the runner and stops there. The agent is running and listening, but only inside the sandbox.

### Example

We run [mast](https://github.com/go-steer/mast), an agent harness, as a Task. It serves its session API on `127.0.0.1:8484` inside the sandbox. From another pod in the cluster, a request through the router reaches the runner instead of mast:

```console
$ curl -s -H "ate-target-actor: cred-test/demo-agent-01" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    http://atenet-router.ate-system.svc.cluster.local/sessions
404 page not found
```

The 404 comes from the runner's probe listener, which only handles `/healthz` and `/readyz` (`internal/metadata/server.go`). There is no way to tell the runner that the task has an API of its own.

A second problem shows up once a task can be reached this way. When a request arrives for a suspended task, the router wakes it and waits for `/readyz`. The runner reports ready as soon as it is up, which can be before the agent's server is listening again, so the first request after a wake fails.

### Proposed solution

Add an optional `spec.http.port` to the Task:

```yaml
spec:
  http:
    port: 8484
```

When it's set, the runner forwards every request it doesn't handle itself to that port on localhost. It streams responses as they arrive (agents stream a lot) and passes connection upgrades through. The port can't be the runner's own port (80) or its metadata port (8099). `/readyz` also waits until something accepts connections on that port, so a request that wakes a task is held until the agent can answer it, rather than failing. Requests stay behind the router and whatever auth the agent itself enforces; nothing new is exposed outside the cluster.

We've been running this on our fork for a couple of weeks; it's what lets our triage agents receive incidents and follow-up questions while they scale to zero between them:

- the pass-through: https://github.com/mastersingh24/ax/commit/6b24abae078d161961ff48e40ad5ec651044b775
- holding readiness until the task's server listens: https://github.com/mastersingh24/ax/commit/e29b160f7ead657b26c880c9c94567d59612105c

This is related to #454 and #430, which describe bigger designs for getting traffic into tasks (a gateway in ax-server, interactive clients). A port on the Task would be a small piece either of them could build on.

title: AX keeps saying a task is Suspended after a request wakes it
body:
### What happens

When a request arrives for a suspended task, Agent Substrate's router wakes the task's actor so it can answer. AX doesn't find out. The task keeps running, but AX still records it as `Suspended`, with no worker address. Anything that trusts AX's view then gets it wrong: `ax ssh` refuses to connect, and dashboards built on AX show the task as asleep while it runs and holds worker capacity.

The same thing happens the other way round. If the actor is suspended outside AX, for example with `kubectl ate suspend actor`, AX keeps showing the task as `Running`.

### Example

We ran into this before we patched our fork. To reproduce it:

1. Create a task and resume it, then suspend it with `ax suspend task demo-agent-01`. `ax get task demo-agent-01` shows `Suspended`.
2. Send any request for it through the router, from a pod in the cluster:

   ```console
   $ curl -s -H "ate-target-actor: cred-test/demo-agent-01" \
       http://atenet-router.ate-system.svc.cluster.local/healthz
   ```

   The router wakes the actor and the runner answers.
3. `kubectl ate get actors -a cred-test` now shows the actor as `ACTOR_STATE_RUNNING`, but `ax get task demo-agent-01` still shows `Suspended` with no worker IP, and stays that way.
4. `ax ssh` refuses the task:

   ```console
   $ ax ssh demo-agent-01 -- uname -a
   Error: task "demo-agent-01" is in phase "Suspended" (must be Running to ssh)
   ```

AX only updates the phase when it suspends or resumes a task itself, so a wake by the router is invisible to it until something else reconciles the task.

### Proposed solution

Have ax-server check the actor's real state from time to time and bring the task's phase in line with it. `GetActor` on Substrate's control API is safe for this, because it never wakes an actor. For a task recorded as `Running` or `Suspended`:

- if the actor is running but the task says `Suspended`, record `Running` with the actor's worker address, and set the `Ready` condition with a reason like `ResumedByRequest`, so it's clear AX didn't do it;
- if the actor is suspended but the task says `Running`, record `Suspended` and clear the worker address;
- keep the worker address current while the task runs, since a woken actor can land on a different worker;
- leave other states (resuming, crashed, reverting) alone until the next pass.

On our fork this runs as part of a periodic check in ax-server (every 30 seconds) that we added for automatic suspension (#420), so a router wake shows up in AX within one interval:

- the state sync, in `CheckIdle`: https://github.com/mastersingh24/ax/commit/7fc344529eb7a0963acb8700064f191a555ba9e4
- running the check periodically in ax-server: https://github.com/mastersingh24/ax/commit/379013f81f93a87476ed360b89a15cfb5f10d284

Upstream it would make sense to run the sync for every task, not only the ones that suspend themselves.

title: Adding a field to Task breaks every runner image built before it
body:
### What happens

The task runner ships inside each agent's container image, so images in use carry runners of different ages. ax-server passes the whole Task to the runner in `AX_TASK_YAML`, and the runner refuses any field it doesn't recognise. So when ax-server gains a new Task field and a Task sets it, every task whose image has an older runner fails at startup, even though the runner has no use for the new field.

That makes adding to the Task API risky: each new field forces everyone to rebuild their agent images, at the same moment they upgrade ax-server.

### Example

We added `spec.egress` to Task on our fork (for #449). Every task built on an image with the previous runner then died as soon as it started. The runner logged that it couldn't parse the Task, ending in `unknown field "egress"`, and exited before starting the agent.

The runner decodes `AX_TASK_YAML` with `Task.UnmarshalYAML` (`cmd/ax-task-runner/main.go`), which goes through `protojson.UnmarshalOptions{}` in `pkg/apis/v1alpha1/types.go`. That decoder is strict on purpose ("unknown fields are errors"), which is right for manifests that people write, but not for a document the server hands to the runner.

### Proposed solution

Two small changes, both in our fork:

1. Have the runner ignore fields it doesn't know when it reads `AX_TASK_YAML` (decode with `DiscardUnknown`). Manifests applied with `ax apply` are still checked strictly, so typos are still caught.
2. Leave fields the runner never uses out of `AX_TASK_YAML`, so even today's runners don't see them.

Commit: https://github.com/mastersingh24/ax/commit/4363c253effeeb9deb118385f2061579058215d6

It would be worth doing before the next field is added to TaskSpec.

title: runner: ignore unknown fields in specs from the control plane
body:
Fixes #503.

The task runner ships inside each task image, so a newer ax-server often talks to an older runner. The runner decoded `AX_TASK_YAML` and `AX_WORKSPACE_YAML` strictly, so adding any Task or Workspace field broke every runner image built before it, even when the runner had no use for the field.

This is part 1 of the fix proposed in #503, based on https://github.com/mastersingh24/ax/commit/4363c253effeeb9deb118385f2061579058215d6 by @mastersingh24.

### Changes

- `pkg/apis/v1alpha1`: add `UnmarshalYAMLLenient`. It runs the same per-kind normalizers as `UnmarshalYAML` and decodes with `protojson.UnmarshalOptions{DiscardUnknown: true}`. The `UnmarshalYAML` methods are unchanged and still strict, so `ax apply` still rejects typos and unknown fields.
- `cmd/ax-task-runner`: use it in `loadSpec`, which reads `AX_TASK_YAML` / `--task-file` and `AX_WORKSPACE_YAML` / `--workspace-file`. Blank or null YAML is still treated as no spec.

Part 2 of the proposal (leaving fields the runner never uses out of `AX_TASK_YAML`) has nothing to apply to upstream yet, because `spec.egress` only exists on the fork.

### Known gaps

- Runner images built before this change are still strict. Only images rebuilt after it get the benefit.
- If the runner is supposed to act on a new field (e.g. `WorkspaceSpec.files`), an older runner now starts without the feature instead of failing. See the table in https://github.com/google/ax/issues/503#issuecomment-6323960913.

### Testing

- `TestUnmarshalYAMLLenient_IgnoresUnknownFields`, `TestUnmarshalYAMLLenient_NormalizesWorkspace`
- New `cmd/ax-task-runner/main_test.go`: a Task carrying `egress:` loads, a Workspace with an unknown field loads, and blank YAML is treated as no spec.
- `go test ./cmd/... ./pkg/... ./runner/... ./internal/...` passes.

title: server: log Substrate actors that have no Task record at startup
body:
A Redis restart drops every Task record while the Substrate actors keep running, so ax no longer knows about sandboxes that still hold worker slots (#442). Make the divergence visible: at startup, list all actors and all tasks and log a warning for each actor with no matching atespace/name. The check only logs, is bounded to 30s, and a failure does not stop the server.

Tasks are read in one call rather than paged by offset, because a delete between pages would shift the list and could skip a live task.

Carried in from rkb32/ax:orphan-check at the maintainer's request on the issue; implementation and tests are rkb32's.

Part of #442

title: build: replace ko with `make images` using podman or docker
body:
Remove ko from the build and deploy flow. The new `make images` target cross-compiles ax-server and ax-task-runner for linux/$IMAGE_ARCH, builds their container images with podman (falling back to docker), and pushes them to $AX_IMAGE_REPO. AX_IMAGE_REPO is required, and IMAGE_TAG overrides the default `latest` tag.

`make deploy-server` now fills in the ax-server image in deploy/ax-server.yaml. It also sets AX_DEFAULT_TASK_IMAGE, so the server runs the task-runner image you pushed for tasks that do not set spec.image. Since the default tag is `latest`, imagePullPolicy is now Always.

Other changes:
- Delete .ko.yaml.
- Move Dockerfile.server from test/e2e/ to the repo root so the e2e setup and `make images` share it.
- Remove redundant Makefile targets (all, build-binaries, build-task-runner, push-task-runner, push).
- Update README, CONTRIBUTING, and docs to use `make images`.

title: Per-Task custom configuration (`spec.config`)
body:
Add a free-form `config` field to the `Task` spec. AX stores it and passes it
to the runner unchanged, without interpreting it. This gives runners a
structured, typed way to receive per-task settings without overloading
`spec.env` or baking settings into the image.

## Motivation

Today a task can tell its runner only three things beyond the workspace:
`spec.image`, `spec.command`, and `spec.env`. In practice this means:

- **Settings get flattened into env vars.** Nested or list-valued settings
  (allowed tools, a list of eval cases, per-model parameters) have to be
  stringified into `spec.env` and parsed back by hand.
- **Custom runners have no extension point.** [Runners](docs/runner.md)
  invites users to replace `ax-task-runner`, but a custom runner has nowhere
  to read runner-specific settings from except env vars or a forked image.
- **The same image can't be reused with different settings** without one
  env var per knob, and every new knob is just another string.

A per-task config lets one runner image serve many tasks that differ only in
their settings.

## Proposal

### API

Add an optional `config` field to `TaskSpec`. It is an arbitrary YAML/JSON
object:

```proto
message TaskSpec {
  string image = 1;
  repeated string command = 2;
  repeated EnvVar env = 3;
  ResourcesSpec resources = 4;
  WorkspaceRef workspace = 5;
  bool debug = 6;
  // config is free-form, runner-defined configuration. AX stores it and
  // hands it to the runner as-is; it is not validated or interpreted by
  // the control plane.
  google.protobuf.Struct config = 7;
}
```

### Semantics

- **Opaque to the control plane.** AX checks only that `config` is a valid
  object and fits within a size limit (see open questions). The runner owns
  the schema.
- **Immutable after creation**, like the rest of the launch spec. Changing
  the config means creating a new task.
- **Not for secrets.** `config` is stored in plain text and shown by
  `ax get task`. Credentials should keep going through secrets (e.g.
  `Model.spec.secretKey`).

### Delivery to the runner

Use the channels runners already rely on, so it works without new plumbing:

| Channel | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `AX_TASK_YAML` | Already contains the full launch spec, so it includes `spec.config` automatically. |
| `/metadata/v1alpha1/ax/task` | Same: the returned `Task` includes `spec.config`. |

The default `ax-task-runner` would only pass the config through to the
command as part of the Task; it would not interpret it.

### CLI

- `ax get task <name>` shows `spec.config` as part of the YAML.
- `ax describe task <name>` shows a `Config:` section (possibly collapsed to
  its top-level keys).

## Examples

### 1. A custom runner with its own settings

A team ships its own runner image for a code-review agent. Each task picks
the repo, the review policy, and where results are posted, all in one place:

```yaml
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Task
metadata:
  name: review-pr-1234
spec:
  image: us-docker.pkg.dev/acme/agents/reviewer:v3
  workspace:
    name: acme-backend
  config:
    pull_request:
      repo: acme/backend
      number: 1234
    policy:
      severity_threshold: medium
      checks: [security, performance, style]
    output:
      format: github_review
      dry_run: true
```

### 2. Eval or benchmark harness

The same harness image runs different eval slices, with structured
parameters that would be awkward as env vars:

```yaml
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Task
metadata:
  name: swe-bench-shard-07
spec:
  image: us-docker.pkg.dev/acme/evals/harness:2026.10
  command: ["python3", "-m", "harness.run"]
  config:
    suite: swe_bench_verified
    shard: { index: 7, total: 32 }
    models:
      - provider: google
        model: gemini-3.8-flash
      - provider: google
        model: gemini-3.8-pro
    limits:
      per_case_timeout: 15m
      max_cost_usd: 25
    report:
      bucket: gs://acme-evals/results/
```

Inside the task, the command reads its config with:

```bash
curl -s "$AX_METADATA_URL/metadata/v1alpha1/ax/task" | yq .spec.config
```

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep using `spec.env`.** It works for scalars, but every structured
  setting has to be encoded and decoded by hand, and there's no place for
  nested data.
- **A config file in the Workspace (e.g. a Git repo).** This ties settings
  to the workspace rather than the task, and doesn't let two tasks on the
  same workspace behave differently.
- **A separate `TaskConfig` kind referenced by name.** Useful for reuse, but
  more API surface. It could be added later on top of an inline `config`
  (e.g. `configRef`).

## Open questions

1. **Size limit.** What maximum size should `config` have, given it is
   stored in Redis and passed through an env var? 64 KiB?

title: Reuse authorized existing atespaces without global creation permission
body:
AX’s Substrate API identity with editor access to an operator-created atespace still calls
`CreateAtespace` through `EnsureAtespace`. That operation requires global
creation permission even when the scope already exists, so task reconciliation
can fail despite the identity having sufficient access within its own scope.

Reproduction: precreate a scope, grant the AX identity editor access only there,
and reconcile a task in that scope. The current client attempts the global create
operation. The fix reads the scope first, creates only after `NotFound`, and
preserves permission and other read errors. A concurrent `AlreadyExists` remains
successful.

Branch: https://github.com/eren23/ax/tree/fix/reuse-authorized-atespace

Compare: https://github.com/google/ax/compare/main...eren23:ax:fix/reuse-authorized-atespace

The branch changes the client and its test fixtures on AX `0f085aa`, without an API
module upgrade. Tests cover existing/editor access, missing scopes, denied reads
and concurrent creation. In the earlier combined-stack live validation, AX used
editor access on precreated scopes and all eight e2e tests passed against
Substrate `173cd071`. Independently, scope branch `849035e` passed the full
Go unit suite and race tests for `internal/substrate` and `internal/controller`
on native Linux amd64 with Go 1.27.1. A negative control reproduced the exact
missing-controller-mock failure, followed by passing corrected tests. This branch also passed `go mod tidy` without changing `go.mod` or `go.sum`,
and built `ax`, `ax-server` and `ax-task-runner`. This standalone batch did not
run live e2e tests.

Would a collaborator be willing to open the focused PR from this branch while
external PR creation is restricted?

title: Support authenticated router TLS in readiness and SSH
body:
With AX tasks running against Substrate `173cd071`, its router exposes an
authenticated TLS endpoint on port 443. AX's legacy readiness and SSH paths
cannot connect through that endpoint using the router's required client identity.

Branch: https://github.com/eren23/ax/tree/fix/router-mtls

Compare: https://github.com/google/ax/compare/main...eren23:ax:fix/router-mtls

The change uses the projected AX Pod identity and service-DNS trust bundle for
readiness and SSH. It adds CA-file, client-bundle and server-name configuration,
reloads credential files for each new TLS handshake, and refuses invalid or
partial TLS configuration without downgrading the router connection to plaintext.
The controller retains its existing direct HTTP worker-readiness probe before
trying the router; this change does not encrypt that path. Explicit legacy
router transport remains available in client configuration. The supplied
manifests require pod-certificate projection, its configured signer, and router
TLS on port 443; they are not unchanged legacy deployment manifests. The router
allowlist stays enabled.

Reproduction: enable the current router's ingress authorization, allow the AX
ServiceAccount identity, and exercise task readiness plus `ax ssh`. The branch's
networking documentation gives the credential projection and configuration.
The October 22 ARM64/gVisor live checks rejected the wrong CA, wrong DNS name,
unauthorized identity and plaintext; a separate command witness verified that
rejected connections did not execute. Separately, the October 23 native amd64
combined-stack validation passed all eight e2e tests against Substrate `173cd071`.
Independently, router branch `9a072872c6bafc38019cce2455e2d40c3956fff4` passed
its full Go unit suite and race tests for `internal/routerclient`,
`internal/controller`, `internal/guest` and `cmd/ax` on native Linux amd64 with
Go 1.27.1. `go mod tidy` left both module files unchanged, and `ax`, `ax-server`
and `ax-task-runner` built successfully.

The added tests reuse the same HTTP and guest gRPC clients across valid client
certificate replacement, then CA/server replacement via stable symlink paths.
The gRPC test executes a real guest command and verifies actor metadata on both
the unary request and output stream. Four deliberately broken variants—cached
HTTP credentials, cached gRPC credentials, missing unary metadata and missing
stream metadata—each failed the intended assertion; the unchanged implementation
passed both normal and race suites.

This standalone batch did not exercise live Kubernetes issuance, actual router
policy, the CLI port-forward lifecycle, or interruptions of active commands.
It does not establish compatibility with Substrate revisions beyond the frozen
`173cd071` combined-stack evidence.

This is separate from #498's API/selector migration. Would a collaborator be
willing to open the transport PR from the branch?
