title: server: remove the `Reconciler` interface
body:
`internal/server` defines a `Reconciler` interface that `Server` uses to drive
task lifecycles on Agent Substrate:

```go
// Reconciler coordinates sandbox/actor lifecycles on Agent Substrate directly.
type Reconciler interface {
	Reconcile(ctx context.Context, task *v1alpha1.Task, ws *v1alpha1.Workspace) (*v1alpha1.Task, error)
	ReconcileDelete(ctx context.Context, atespace, taskName string) error
}
```

The interface doesn't buy us anything, and is poorly designed.

## Proposal

- Delete `server.Reconciler` and `Options.Reconciler`.
- Make `Server` depend on `*controller.TaskReconciler` directly. Another option
  is to build it inside `NewServer` from a `*substrate.Client`. It should also
  act as the `tasks.Observer`, so that one value is wired up in one place.
- Remove the `s.reconciler != nil` branches in `server.go`.
- Make a failure to create the Substrate client in `cmd/ax-server` fatal,
  instead of logging it and continuing without reconciliation.
- Change `server_test.go` to use a real `TaskReconciler` against the fake
  Substrate gRPC servers that `internal/controller` tests already use, instead
  of `fakeReconciler`.

## Affected code

- `internal/server/server.go`: interface, `Options`, `Server`, and the call
  sites at the `Reconcile` / `ReconcileDelete` calls
- `cmd/ax-server/main.go`: wiring
- `internal/server/server_test.go`: `fakeReconciler`,
  `TestServer_DirectReconcilerLifecycle`

title: server, store: move to Postgres and read actor state from Substrate
body:
Replace the Redis store with PostgreSQL, and stop storing the parts of a
task's status that belong to its actor on Agent Substrate.

Storage:
- internal/store/postgres holds resources as protojson JSONB documents.
  Open creates any missing tables. Locks are leases in a locks table,
  renewed while held.
- Watches and lock waiters poll. There is no LISTEN/NOTIFY, so any
  connection pooler works. WatchTask is removed from store.Store.
- The memory store is now test-only and no longer tracks save order.
  Newest-first ordering is covered by a Postgres-specific test.

Task status:
- The store keeps only what AX owns: spec, metadata, the Pending, Failed
  and Terminating phases, and WorkspaceReady. The actor, worker IP, live
  phase and Ready condition are read from Substrate on every get, list
  and watch.
- Only a few helpers in server.go (getTask, listTasks, saveTask,
  updateTask, deleteTask) touch task storage, and a test enforces it.
- Phases, condition types and condition reasons are now constants in
  pkg/apis/v1alpha1. Ready is derived from one rule in the server
  instead of being written in several places.
- Ready reasons visible to clients change: TaskSuspended, ActorResuming,
  ActorSuspending, ActorCrashed, ActorDeleting and UnknownActorState
  become the phase name (Suspended, Resuming, Suspending, Failed,
  Terminating, Unknown).

This work revealed major problems in the server, storage and controller
implementations. Among them:
- Task status was copied from Substrate into storage and could drift
  from the actor it described.
- The controller wrote Ready conditions and phases that the server then
  discarded, or that disagreed with what clients saw.
- Handlers pass the desired action to the reconciler by overwriting
  status.phase, mixing intent with observed state.
- Phase and reason strings were spread across packages as literals. The
  server and CLI checked for a "Completed" phase that nothing produced.
- The shared store tests encoded one backend's list ordering as a
  contract.

This change fixes some of these, but the server, store and controller
need further stabilization. @rakyll is taking ownership of that work.

title: Support multiple model providers, custom endpoints, and Kubernetes Secret references for API keys
body:
I would like AX to support model providers beyond Google, including OpenAI, Anthropic, etc., and services exposing compatible APIs.

The provider configuration should support:

- Selecting the provider and model.
- Configuring a custom API endpoint or base URL, including OpenAI-compatible services and self-hosted model gateways.
- Reading the provider’s API key from a specified Kubernetes Secret.

AX already exposes a secretKey reference in its Model configuration. It would be useful to support an explicit Secret namespace and ensure the selected provider, endpoint, model, and credentials are used consistently throughout model execution, including workspace bootstrap.

For example, the following illustrates the desired configuration; the exact field names are open to discussion:

apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Model
metadata:
  name: default-model
  atespace: default
spec:
  provider: openai
  model: my-model
  baseURL: https://api.example.com/v1
  secretKey:
    namespace: kagent
    name: kagent-my-provider
    key: PROVIDER_API_KEY

The Kubernetes namespace containing the Secret should be independent of the AX/Substrate atespace. In this example, the Model belongs to atespace default, while its credentials come from the kagent Kubernetes namespace. Secret access should use the AX server’s Kubernetes identity and respect RBAC permissions.

Expected behavior:

- Existing Google provider configurations continue to work.
- OpenAI, Anthropic, and compatible custom endpoints can be configured through Model resources.
- API keys are resolved from Kubernetes Secrets without embedding them in manifests.
- Unsupported providers, invalid endpoints, and missing or inaccessible credentials produce actionable errors.

This would allow AX to work with existing enterprise model providers and credential management setups while keeping task execution configuration declarative.

title: chore(substrate): bump substrate to v0.6.0 and update control/dataplane integration
body:
## Summary

Upgrades `agent-substrate` from `v0.5.0` to `v0.6.0` (`go.ate.dev/substrate v0.6.0`) and updates AX's Substrate client, controller, CLI, deployment manifests, and E2E suite for the breaking changes in `v0.6.0`.

## Why Substrate v0.6.0 Mandates These Changes

1. **Canonical module path rename (`github.com/agent-substrate/substrate` -> `go.ate.dev/substrate`)**
   - **Upstream change**: Substrate `v0.6.0` moved its module path to `go.ate.dev/substrate` and removed `pkg/sandboxclass`.
   - **AX update**: Updated `go.mod`, `go.sum`, and all `ateapipb` imports across `internal/substrate`, `internal/controller`, and `test/e2e`.

2. **`ActorTemplate` resource schema and removed proto fields**
   - **Upstream change**: Substrate `v0.6.0` replaced `repeated ResourceLimit` on `ActorTemplate` with `ResourceRequirements{Limits: Resources{CpuMillicores: int64, MemoryBytes: int64}}`, added `ate-api-server` validation requiring both `cpu_millicores != 0` and `memory_bytes != 0` on every `ActorTemplate`, and removed `ActorTemplate.SandboxConfig` and `DeleteActorRequest.AnyState`.
   - **AX update**: Added `v1alpha1.ParseCPUMillicores` and `v1alpha1.ParseMemoryBytes`, updated `substrate.ResourceLimits`, `BuildActorTemplate`, and `EnsureActorTemplateWithImage` to populate `*ateapipb.ResourceRequirements` (defaulting unset dimensions to `DefaultCPUMillicores = 1000` and `DefaultMemoryBytes = 512 << 20`), and removed obsolete field references.

3. **Worker binary rename (`cmd/ateom-gvisor` -> `cmd/ateworker-gvisor`)**
   - **Upstream change**: Substrate `v0.6.0` renamed the gVisor worker binary entrypoint from `cmd/ateom-gvisor` to `cmd/ateworker-gvisor`.
   - **AX update**: Updated `test/e2e/manifests/workerpool.yaml` to `ko://go.ate.dev/substrate/cmd/ateworker-gvisor`.

4. **Dataplane (`atenet-router`) mandatory mTLS on port `443`**
   - **Upstream change**: Substrate `v0.6.0` removed plaintext port `80` from `atenet-router` and now serves ingress exclusively over mTLS on port `443`, verifying client SPIFFE certificates issued by `podidentity.podcert.ate.dev/identity` and presenting server certificates issued by `servicedns.podcert.ate.dev/identity`.
   - **AX update**:
     - Mounted the `podidentity.podcert.ate.dev/identity` projected volume into `ax-server` (`deploy/ax-server.yaml` and `test/e2e/manifests/ax-server.yaml`), updated `ATENET_ROUTER_ADDR` to `https://atenet-router.ate-system.svc.cluster.local:443`, and configured the task reconciler's readiness probe HTTP client (`newProbeHTTPClient`) to present the `podidentity` client certificate and trust the `servicedns` CA bundle.
     - Added `guest.DialTargetTLS` and `tunnel.RouterTLSConfig` (which loads the live `servicedns` `ClusterTrustBundle` and issues/caches a short-lived `PodCertificateRequest` for `ax-server`) so `ax ssh` connects to `svc/atenet-router:443` over mTLS.

5. **E2E installer migration to `cmd/ate-setup`**
   - **Upstream change**: Substrate `v0.6.0` replaced the standalone `install-ate-kind.sh` implementation with a wrapper around `go run ./cmd/ate-setup`, requiring the `deploy ate-system` subcommand, `--credential-provider`, `--ateapi-authz-bootstrap-owners`, and `--ingress-allowed-spiffe-ids`.
   - **AX update**: Updated `hack/setup-e2e-kind.sh` to pass the new `ate-setup` flags and ensure `fs.inotify.max_user_instances` is sufficient on the Kind node.

## Verification

- `go test ./...` passes across all packages.
- `./hack/run-e2e-kind.sh` passes all 8 E2E tests against Substrate `v0.6.0`.

title: Workspace maiden-run marker under /ax is lost on volumes-only resume
body:
## Problem

`internal/substrate/client.go` configures every Task with `PreferredFidelity: SNAPSHOT_FIDELITY_VOLUMES` and `DurableDirs: []string{"/workspace"}`. As noted in #486, resuming from a volumes-only snapshot boots the container fresh from the image and restores only `/workspace`.

`docs/runner.md` notes that workspace setup markers must live on the durable volume so resume skips setup:

> Record that setup happened somewhere on the durable volume or in a known location, per workspace, then skip the work on later boots. Resume restarts the container, and re-cloning into a restored workspace would destroy the agent's state.

However, `internal/workspace/setup.go` sets `DefaultAXDir = "/ax"` on the root filesystem and writes the maiden-run marker to `/ax/initialized-<path>`. Because `/ax` is outside `/workspace`, a volumes-only suspend and resume loses the marker file. On resume, `SetupWorkspace` runs a second maiden setup against the restored `/workspace`:

1. `writeFiles` overwrites any inlined `spec.files` (such as `AGENTS.md`) that the agent or user edited.
2. `cloneRepos` runs `git checkout -f FETCH_HEAD`, wiping uncommitted changes in cloned repositories.
3. `runBootstrap` runs `antigravity_bootstrap.py` again if a workspace `goal` is set.

## Suggested fix

Store the maiden-run marker inside the target workspace directory (for example `<targetPath>/.ax-initialized` or under `/workspace/.ax`) or include `/ax` in `DurableDirs` so the marker survives `SNAPSHOT_FIDELITY_VOLUMES` suspend and resume cycles.

title: api,runner: remove the WorkspaceRef goal field and the agent bootstrap
body:
The goal field on Task.spec.workspace handed a plain-language environment description to an Antigravity agent on the sandbox's first boot. Drop the field, without reserving its number, and everything that existed to serve it:

- The runBootstrap path in internal/workspace, with its GEMINI_API_KEY and AX_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT handling. SetupWorkspace no longer takes a goal and SetupResult loses BootstrapRan.
- cmd/ax-task-runner/antigravity_bootstrap.py, its COPY in Dockerfile.task-runner, and the google-antigravity pip install.
- The goal-based environment planner in internal/workspace, which had no callers outside its own test.
- The goal= suffix in `ax describe task` output.

The model client's offline fallback text was written for the planner's prompt; reword it to be neutral. Docs and the README quickstart no longer describe goal-driven setup, and the roadmap item that depended on it is gone.

title: server: ListTasks lists every actor in each atespace it touches
body:
Follow-up from #515.

To fill in actor status, `listTasks` calls `substrate.ListActors` for each atespace on the page. That call pages through every actor in the atespace, so a 50-task page costs as much as listing all actors there. Every page repeats it. This is the same scale concern as #510.

Substrate has no name filter or batch get, so the likely fix is concurrent per-task `GetActor` calls. That keeps the cost bounded by the page size.

title: test/e2e: cache pre-built Substrate images between CI runs
body:
Every E2E run compiled Substrate's images from source, even though PRs and pushes always test the same Substrate version from go.mod. Add an optional SUBSTRATE_IMAGE_CACHE_DIR to hack/setup-e2e-kind.sh. When it is set, the script starts the kind-registry container with its storage on that directory. It publishes Substrate's release image set once, tagged with `git describe`, and then installs those pre-built images through ATE_IMAGE_REPO/ATE_IMAGE_TAG. The ateom-gvisor reference in the WorkerPool is pinned by digest instead of going through ko. If the Substrate checkout is too old to support `publish release-images` or has local changes, the script logs why and builds from source as before.
In CI, the registry storage is restored from and saved to actions/cache, keyed on the Substrate version in go.mod. Before saving, the AX images are dropped and the registry is garbage-collected, so the cache holds only Substrate images. Nightly and custom substrate_ref runs still build from source.

title: api,cli: remove WatchTask and ax watch
body:
Remove the WatchTask server-streaming RPC and the `ax watch task` command built on it.

- api: drop WatchTask and the WatchTaskRequest and WatchTaskResponse messages from ax.proto, and regenerate ax.pb.go and ax_grpc.pb.go.
- server: remove the WatchTask handler and the watchPollInterval it polled on, plus the export_test.go hook that overrode the interval.
- cli: remove the watch command, runWatch, and its usage line.
- test: drop the watch steps from the server tests. The E2E test becomes TestE2E_DescribeAndAtespaceIsolation and still checks atespace isolation and `ax describe` after a plain resume.
- docs: point README, DESIGN.md, docs/concepts.md, docs/runner.md and demo.sh at `ax describe` instead of `ax watch`. The README also now says `make deploy` installs PostgreSQL, not Redis.

This is a breaking change. Clients calling WatchTask get Unimplemented, and `ax watch` is no longer a command. Use GetTask, or `ax describe task`, to read a task's phase and conditions.

title: Add an optional google.protobuf.Struct config field to TaskSpec
body:
AX stores it and passes it to the runner unchanged. The control plane does not interpret it; the runner defines its schema. No new plumbing is needed: AX_TASK_YAML and /metadata/v1alpha1/ax/task already carry the full launch spec, so the config comes along. Like the rest of the spec, it can't be changed after the task is created.
ValidateTask now rejects a config whose JSON encoding is larger than MaxTaskConfigSize (64 KiB). The config travels inside the AX_TASK_YAML environment variable, which Linux caps at 128 KiB, so this leaves room for the rest of the spec. A config that is not an object is already rejected when the manifest is decoded.
`ax get task` shows the config as part of the YAML, and `ax describe task` prints it in a new Config: section. Struct stores every number as a double, so large integers and IDs that must stay exact should be quoted. The config is stored in plain text and shown by the CLI, so it must not hold secrets. docs/manifests.md covers both points and docs/runner.md links to it.

Fixes #509

title: README: use a realistic agent task in the intro example
body:
The intro example only showed a workspace binding, which doesn't look like real use. Replace it with something closer to how AX is used in practice: a coding agent container that gets a goal and works on a cloned repo, with an AGENTS.md file written into the workspace to give it project guidelines.

Depends on #523.

title: README: describe AX as running millions of tasks per cluster
body: Say "millions" instead of "billions" following the Agent Substrate wording, focusing on the scale in a cluster. Billions can be achieved by scaling into multiple clusters.

title: Local development
body:
Trying AX locally takes a lot of setup. You need a Kubernetes cluster with Agent Substrate installed, plus Go, `ko`, a container registry and `make deploy`. That's a high bar for someone who just wants to run a task, and it slows down contributors who want to test changes against real sandboxes.

Our e2e test setup already does most of this on Kind, but it's built for tests. It wipes the database on every run, uses a test runner image, and writes a separate kubeconfig that `ax` doesn't pick up.

## Proposal

Add local cluster management commands:

```bash
ax local start       # create or reuse the cluster, install Substrate and AX
ax local status    # show what's running and whether it's healthy
ax local stop       # stops the cluster
```

After `ax local start`, everything should just work:

```bash
ax local start
ax apply -f examples/task.yaml
ax ssh task123 -- ls /workspace
```

`ax local start` should:

- Check for Kind and a container runtime, either Docker or Podman. Use whichever is available, or the one picked with a flag such as `--runtime=podman`.
- Create or reuse the Kind cluster.
- Install Substrate, Postgres and `ax-server`.
- Keep data between runs.
- Switch the kube context so `ax` finds the server.

title: README: drop command from example Task
body: Runner images can already set their own entrypoint, so the example Task doesn't need to set `command`. Removing it makes the example simpler and shows that `image` alone is enough.

title: store/postgres: test that a restart keeps tasks and releases locks
body:
Opened on behalf of @rkb32 while PR creation is limited to collaborators (#448). The commit is theirs.

Adds a Postgres store test for the restart case from #442: save a task, take a lock, close the store without unlocking, reopen it on the same database, then check the task is still there and the lock can be taken once its lease expires.

Test only.

title: make: deploy the task image by the digest make images recorded
body:
Follow-up to #508. The README deploys with `make images`, then `make deploy`, but `make deploy` never read the digest `make images` records, so tasks without `spec.image` got the `:latest` tag, which Substrate rejects. `AX_DEFAULT_TASK_IMAGE` now defaults to the pinned digest in `bin/ax-task-runner.digest` when it exists, and falls back to the tag otherwise. Setting `AX_DEFAULT_TASK_IMAGE` explicitly still wins.

Checked with `make -n`: no digest file, an empty one, a recorded digest, and an explicit override. Not tested with a real registry push.

title: docs: document default task CPU and memory limits (1000m, 512Mi)
body:
Follow up #517. 

Update the 'Sizing the sandbox' section in docs/manifests.md and the ValidateResources doc comment in pkg/apis/v1alpha1/resources.go to reflect that omitted CPU and memory limits default to 1 CPU (1000m) and 512Mi memory.

If we want to make these configurable, we should consider moving all the configs into a `Config` type and not blow up params passed into `controller.NewTaskReconciler(...)`

title: DONT MERGE: test
server: remove the Reconciler interface
body:
Fixes #514.

`server.NewServer` now takes the `*controller.TaskReconciler` directly and reads actor state through its client, so `ax-server` wires a single value.

- Removes `server.Reconciler`, `Options.Reconciler`, `Options.Substrate`, and the nil checks they required.
- `ax-server` now exits if it can't create the Substrate client, instead of running without reconciliation.
- Adds `internal/substrate/substratetest`, an in-memory Substrate control API. The server and CLI tests now drive a real `TaskReconciler` against it, replacing `fakeReconciler`, `fakeSubstrate` and `fakeMainReconciler`.

Reviewing commit by commit is easiest:
1. The new package.
2. The test migration, still on the old API. It changes only tests, plus a `TaskReconciler.Client` getter.
3. The refactor. Its test changes are mechanical.

title: demo.sh: use spec.workspace and the server's default task image
body:
demo.sh still declared the `spec.workspaces` list that #496 replaced with a single `spec.workspace`, so `ax apply` rejected the demo Task with `unknown field "workspaces"`.

- Bind the demo workspace with `spec.workspace`. The `path: "/workspace"` override is dropped, since /workspace is now the default.
- Stop pinning `gcr.io/dberkov-gke-dev3/ax-task-runner@sha256:c81cfd6e…`. The image can't be pulled anonymously, and its runner predates #496 and exits on the `workspace` field the server now sends in AX_TASK_YAML. The demo now sets `spec.image` only when AX_TASK_IMAGE is given, so by default the server runs its default task image, which `make deploy` and the kind e2e setup set to the ax-task-runner they pushed. AX_IMAGE_REPO no longer affects the demo.

Updates #424.

title: controller: replace Reconcile with explicit Suspend and Resume
body:
Follow-up to #514 ([comment](https://github.com/google/ax/issues/514#issuecomment-6482157243)).

Server handlers tell `TaskReconciler` what to do by setting `task.Status.Phase` before calling `Reconcile`: `Suspended` (or empty) means suspend, and `Running` means resume. As #515 noted, this mixes intent with observed state.

The phase also does two other jobs today, and both need to become explicit:
- A successful call clears a stored `Pending` or `Failed` only because it ends on a phase the store doesn't keep.
- A failed task is marked `Failed` only if its phase isn't already `Pending`.

## Proposal

- Replace `Reconcile` with `Suspend(ctx, task, ws) error` and `Resume(ctx, task, ws) error`. Both first make sure the atespace, template and actor exist, as `Reconcile` does now.
- Rename `ReconcileDelete` to `Delete`.
- Handlers stop setting the phase to pass the action. `CreateTask` calls `Suspend`, so starting suspended is an explicit step.
- On success, handlers clear the phase so reads take it from the actor. On failure, `IsTransientError` alone decides between `Pending` and `Failed`.
- The reconciler records only what AX stores: the task ID, `WorkspaceReady`, and `Pending` or `Failed` with a Ready reason on failure. It stops writing the actor name, worker IP and `Running`/`Suspended`, which the server discards.

Out of scope: skipping the atespace, template and actor checks on every call, and renaming `TaskReconciler`.

## Affected code

- `internal/controller/reconciler.go` and `reconciler_test.go`
- `internal/server/server.go`: `CreateTask`, `SuspendTask`, `ResumeTask`, `deleteTask`

title: chore: add AGENTS.md contract and skills
body:
Add a unified agent contract (`AGENTS.md`) and an initial checked-in skill library (`skills/`) so coding agents working on `ax` share a single source of truth for repository layout, CI gates, invariants, and Agent Substrate integration details.

**Note:** `AGENTS.md` and `skills/` strictly describe the **current codebase as implemented today** — every rule, path, symbol, and command reflects existing code and CI at `HEAD`. Future changes from the proposed roadmap will update the contract and skills as they land (via `/sync-contract`).

Verified all build/test commands documented in `AGENTS.md` locally (`go mod tidy`, `go build ./cmd/ax ./cmd/ax-server
    ./cmd/ax-task-runner`, `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .`, and `internal/store/postgres` against `postgres:17-alpine`).

title: controller: replace Reconcile with explicit Suspend and Resume
body:
Fixes #534.

Handlers no longer set `task.Status.Phase` to tell the reconciler what to do (#515). `TaskReconciler.Reconcile` is replaced by explicit `Suspend` and `Resume`, which share `ensureSubstrateResources` (atespace, template, actor). `ReconcileDelete` is renamed `Delete`.

- `CreateTask` calls `Suspend`, so starting suspended is an explicit step.
- The reconciler no longer writes the phase, actor name or worker IP. On failure it records only the Ready reason. When create or resume fails, the server's `recordFailure` stores `Pending` for a transient error and `Failed` otherwise. The issue left `Pending`/`Failed` to the reconciler; here only the server sets the phase.
- A successful call clears the stored phase, so reads take it from the actor (new test: `TestServer_SuccessClearsStoredFailure`).
- No behavior change: a before/after trace against `main` showed the same Substrate calls, gRPC codes, responses and stored status.
- `AGENTS.md` and the substrate skill describe the new flow. They also fix text left stale by #532: the server and CLI tests use `substratetest`.

title: Add an ADK runner configured from ADK Agent Config
body:
Add `cmd/runners/adk-runner`, a task runner for [Agent Development Kit (ADK)](https://google.github.io/adk-docs/) agents. Users author the agent in `spec.config` using ADK's own [Agent Config](https://google.github.io/adk-docs/agents/config/) schema (the `root_agent.yaml` format). They don't write a `spec.command` or build a custom image.

The runner serves the agent as an A2A server for the lifetime of the task. Clients talk to it with A2A messages through the atenet router, the same way they reach any task.

## Motivation

To run an ADK agent on AX today, a user has to:

1. Build their own image.
2. Copy their agent code into it or clone it into the workspace.
3. Write a `spec.command` that starts it and exposes it somehow.

That's a lot of setup for the framework we most want to show off on AX. ADK already has a declarative way to author agents: Agent Config YAML, covering model, instruction, and tools. ADK also ships A2A support, so it can serve an agent over A2A. If AX accepts that config and serves the agent over A2A, the Task manifest becomes the whole agent definition. Any A2A client, including other agents, can then talk to it with no AX-specific protocol.

A2A also fits the task lifecycle well. The atenet router resumes a suspended task when a request arrives for it. So an idle agent can be suspended and woken up by its next A2A message.

## Proposal

### Authoring

`spec.config` is an ADK Agent Config document, nothing more. The runner should not invent or rename fields. Anything ADK accepts in `root_agent.yaml` is accepted here. The config holds no input. Input arrives as A2A messages.

```yaml
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Task
metadata:
  name: adk-triage
  atespace: default
spec:
  image: "gcr.io/ax-images/adk-runner@sha256:REPLACE_WITH_PUSHED_DIGEST"  # Dockerfile.adk
  # ADK Agent Config (root_agent.yaml) with camelCase keys. The runner writes
  # it out with snake_case keys, e.g. agentClass -> agent_class.
  config:
    agentClass: LlmAgent
    name: triage_agent
    model: gemini-3.8-flash
    description: Triages failing tests.
    instruction: |
      You are a careful engineer. Reproduce failures before fixing them.
      Write a report of what you found to /workspace/adk-output.md.
    generateContentConfig:
      maxOutputTokens: 8192
    tools:
      - name: google_search
  workspace:
    name: my-repo
  debug: true
```

### Talking to the agent

The agent's A2A endpoint is the task's normal address. Send requests to the atenet router with `ate-target-actor: <atespace>/<task>` (see [Networking](../docs/networking.md)):

```bash
kubectl -n ate-system port-forward svc/atenet-router 8001:80

# Send a message (A2A JSON-RPC)
curl -H "ate-target-actor: default/adk-triage" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  http://localhost:8001/ -d '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "message/send",
    "params": {"message": {"role": "user", "messageId": "m1",
      "parts": [{"kind": "text", "text": "Triage the failing tests."}]}}
  }'
```

Later messages that carry the same A2A `contextId` continue the same ADK session.

### Credentials

ADK on Gemini reads `GEMINI_API_KEY` (or `GOOGLE_API_KEY`). A `provider: google` `Model` resource already stores `GEMINI_API_KEY`. Confirm that the control plane injects it into the task container, so the agent needs no secrets in `spec.env`, and document the result. If ADK needs `GOOGLE_API_KEY` instead, the runner should alias it.

title: Add a Genkit Go runner configured from Dotprompt (spec.config)
body:
Add `cmd/runners/genkit-runner`, a task runner for [Genkit Go](https://genkit.dev/docs/go/overview/) agents (`github.com/firebase/genkit/go`). Users author the agent in `spec.config` using Genkit's [Dotprompt](https://genkit.dev/docs/go/dotprompt/) frontmatter schema (`model`, `config`, `tools`, `maxTurns`, `use`, `input`, `output`) plus `instruction` (or a `.prompt` file in the workspace). They don't write a `spec.command` or build a custom image.

The runner serves the agent in-process for the lifetime of the task — exposing both an **A2A server** (`/` and `/.well-known/agent-card.json`) and **Genkit's native HTTP agent routes** (`/agents/<name>`, `/getSnapshot`, `/waitForSnapshot`, `/abort`) through the runner's port 80 listener. Clients talk to it through the atenet router the same way they reach any task.

## Motivation

Like #537 for ADK, running a Genkit agent on AX today requires building a custom image, writing Go boilerplate, and wiring `spec.command`.

Because AX itself is written in Go, a Genkit Go runner fits naturally into `runner.Run` as a single static Go binary (`CGO_ENABLED=0`) with no secondary runtime required:

1. **Declarative authoring via Dotprompt**: Genkit already defines a declarative format for model, generation config, tool loops (`maxTurns`), schemas, and middleware (`use`): Dotprompt frontmatter.
2. **Native durability across suspend/resume**: Genkit Go's `localstore.NewFileSessionStore` persists atomic, `fsync`-backed session snapshots on disk. Pointing it at `/workspace/.genkit/snapshots` means multi-turn conversations (whether driven via A2A `contextId` or Genkit `sessionId`) automatically survive `ax suspend` and `ax resume` across container restarts.
3. **Built-in Workspace integration (Filesystem, Skills, and MCP)**:
   - Genkit's `plugins/middleware` ships `genkit-middleware/filesystem` (`list_files`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `search_and_replace` confined to `/workspace` via `os.Root`) and `genkit-middleware/skills` (which loads `SKILL.md` files from `Workspace.spec.skills.path` / `.agents/skills`).
   - Genkit's `plugins/mcp` (`MCPHost`) connects to `Stdio` and `StreamableHTTP` MCP servers, allowing the runner to automatically wire `Workspace.spec.mcp` servers into the agent's tool registry (just as `claude-code-runner` does).
4. **Dual protocol support (A2A + Genkit HTTP)**: Mounting `a2asrv` (`github.com/a2aproject/a2a-go/v2`) at `/` alongside `genkitx.AllAgentRoutes(g)` at `/agents/<name>` lets any A2A client or orchestrator talk to the task over A2A JSON-RPC, while Genkit clients (`DefineRemoteAgent`, `remoteAgent` in JS, and `@genkit-ai/vercel-ai`) can use streaming, detached background turns, and snapshot inspection against the same session store.

## Proposal

### Authoring

`spec.config` accepts any [Dotprompt frontmatter](https://genkit.dev/docs/go/dotprompt/) field (`model`, `config`, `maxTurns`, `tools`, `use`, `input`, `output`), plus `name`, `description`, and `instruction` (rendered as the system prompt body). If `spec.config.promptFile` is set (or a `<name>.prompt` file exists in the workspace), the runner loads that `.prompt` file directly.

```yaml
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Task
metadata:
  name: genkit-triage
  atespace: default
spec:
  image: "gcr.io/ax-images/genkit-runner@sha256:REPLACE_WITH_PUSHED_DIGEST"  # Dockerfile.genkit
  config:
    name: triage_agent
    description: Triages failing tests.
    model: googleai/gemini-3.8-flash
    instruction: |
      You are a careful engineer. Reproduce failures before fixing them.
      Write a report of what you found to /workspace/genkit-output.md.
    config:
      maxOutputTokens: 8192
    maxTurns: 15
    use:
      - name: genkit-middleware/filesystem
        config:
          rootDirectory: /workspace
          allowWriteAccess: true
      - name: genkit-middleware/skills
  workspace:
    name: my-repo
  debug: true
```

### Talking to the agent

The agent is served on port 80 behind the runner's probe mux (with `/readyz` held at `503` until workspace setup, MCP connections, and Genkit initialization complete). Send requests to the atenet router with `ate-target-actor: <atespace>/<task>`:

```bash
kubectl -n ate-system port-forward svc/atenet-router 8001:80

# 1. Send a message via A2A JSON-RPC
curl -H "ate-target-actor: default/genkit-triage" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  http://localhost:8001/ -d '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "message/send",
    "params": {"message": {"role": "user", "messageId": "m1", "contextId": "ctx-1",
      "parts": [{"kind": "text", "text": "Triage the failing tests."}]}}
  }'

# 2. Or call via Genkit's native agent HTTP endpoint (supports ?stream=true, detach, getSnapshot, abort)
curl -H "ate-target-actor: default/genkit-triage" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  http://localhost:8001/agents/triage_agent -d '{
    "data": {"message": {"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "What did you find?"}]}},
    "init": {"sessionId": "ctx-1"}
  }'
```

Later messages carrying the same A2A `contextId` or Genkit `sessionId` continue the same session from `/workspace/.genkit/snapshots`, even if the task was suspended and resumed in between.

### Workspace MCP & Skills

- **MCP**: Servers declared in the bound Workspace's `spec.mcp` are connected at startup via `mcp.NewMCPHost` (`Stdio` for `command`/`args`, `StreamableHTTP` for `endpoint`) and registered on the Genkit instance so the agent can call them.
- **Skills**: When the Workspace sets `spec.skills.path`, the runner registers `middleware.Skills` pointed at that path.

### Credentials

Genkit's `googlegenai`, `anthropic`, and `compat_oai` plugins read `GEMINI_API_KEY` (or `GOOGLE_API_KEY`), `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment. Today these can be passed via `spec.env` (or egress credential injection once #475 / #516 land).

title: The Ready condition's update time changes on every read, even when nothing changed
body:
### What happens

Every time you read a task, its Ready condition comes back with a new `updateTime`, even though the task and its actor haven't changed. So the timestamp no longer tells you when the task last changed, which is what clients use it for. Anything that polls ax and looks for changes, like a dashboard or a sync loop, sees every task as changed on every poll.

This started with #515, when Ready became derived from the actor's state on each read. The comment on `setReady` says the update time changes only when the condition does, but that's only true within a single call.

### Example

A test against upstream main (f0228f1) creates a task, then calls `GetTask` twice, a second apart:

```go
s1, t1 := ready() // GetTask, then return the phase, Ready status, reason and updateTime
time.Sleep(1100 * time.Millisecond)
s2, t2 := ready()
```

```
first GetTask:  Suspended False Suspended updateTime=2026-10-31T18:40:08.767301281Z
second GetTask: Suspended False Suspended updateTime=2026-10-31T18:40:09.868168323Z
--- FAIL: Ready did not change, but its updateTime did
```

The cause is in `internal/server/server.go`. `storedStatus` drops the Ready condition before saving, for any phase that comes from Substrate. On the next read there's no Ready condition to compare against, so `setReady` appends a new one with `UpdateTime: timestamppb.Now()`.

We hit this in substrate-scope, a visualizer that polls ax. It had to start ignoring Ready's `updateTime` altogether to stop treating every task as changed on every poll.

### Proposed solution

Give the derived Ready condition a timestamp that only moves when its inputs do. Substrate already has one: the actor's `metadata.update_time`, which changes on every mutation of the actor. When Ready is built from the actor's state, use that time (or the later of it and the WorkspaceReady condition's time, since a running task's Ready also depends on workspace setup) instead of `timestamppb.Now()`. Repeated reads of an unchanged task then return the same value, and a real change still moves it.

Another option is to store the last derived Ready condition and keep its time when the new one matches. That works too, but it puts a write on the read path, and the actor's own timestamp already answers the question.

title: tunnel: respect the client certificate's expiry in the router TLS cache
body:
The router TLS cache was marked valid for 30 minutes from when it was written, whatever the certificate's own NotAfter. A certificate that was already expired when cached was reused until the cache expired, and `ax ssh` failed with "tls: expired certificate".

Cache until 30 minutes from now or one minute before the certificate expires, whichever is earlier. Ignore cached certificates that are expired or within a minute of expiring, and return an error instead of caching a certificate that was issued already expired.

title: Tasks: add a session ID for lineage tracking and trajectory collection
body:
A task in AX stands alone. `metadata` has a name, atespace and create time, and `status.id`
identifies one task, but nothing ties together the tasks that make up one piece of work. In
practice, one piece of work often spans several tasks:

- an agent splits a job into subtasks, and those subtasks create more tasks;
- a failed task is retried, or rerun with a different prompt, image or model;
- a pipeline runs stages one after another (plan, implement, test, review), each in its own
  task;
- one user request fans out to several agents that run in parallel.

Without a shared ID:

- **Lineage is lost.** There's no way to answer "which tasks came from this request?" or "what
  produced this task?". Names can carry a convention, but nothing enforces it and every client
  invents its own.
- **Trajectories can't be put back together.** Collecting a trajectory for evaluation, debugging
  or training means joining each task's prompts, tool calls, model responses, commands and
  results in order. Runners and the telemetry backends they send to have no common key to join
  on, so the pieces stay scattered across tasks.
- **Clients can't group tasks.** `ax get tasks` and UIs such as AX Studio can only list tasks
  flat. They can't show one session's tasks together, or clean them up together.

### Proposal

Add a session ID that the creator sets when creating a task. AX stores it and passes it to the
task, but doesn't interpret it.

    message TaskSpec {
      // ... existing fields 1-7 ...

      // session_id groups tasks that belong to one logical piece of work, such
      // as an agent run and the subtasks it creates, or a task and its retries.
      // AX stores it and exposes it to the runner, but does not interpret it.
      // If empty, AX sets it to the task's ID, so every task belongs to a
      // session. Immutable after creation.
      string session_id = 8;
    }

Rules:

- **Set by the creator.** The client that creates the task picks the session, whether that's a
  user, a CLI, a pipeline or an agent inside another task. A task that creates subtasks passes
  its own `session_id` on so they join its session.
- **Defaults to the task's ID.** If it's unset, AX sets it to `status.id`, so a task created on
  its own starts a new session and every task can be grouped.
- **Immutable.** It can't change after creation, so lineage can't be rewritten.
- **Treated as opaque.** AX validates only its length and character set (e.g. at most 128
  characters, `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`), so an external trace or run ID can be used directly.
- **Not secret.** Like `spec.config`, it's stored in plain text and shown by `ax get task`.

#### Passing it to the task

- **Environment:** the runner sets `AX_SESSION_ID` in the task command's environment, next to
  `AX_TASK_YAML` and `AX_METADATA_URL`.
- **Metadata:** the metadata endpoint returns it with the rest of the task.
- **Telemetry:** runners attach it to logs, traces and model calls as `session.id`, the
  OpenTelemetry semantic-convention attribute. Telemetry and trajectory stores can then join
  every task's records on that key.

#### Listing and cleanup

- **Filtering:** `ax get tasks --session <id>` lists one session's tasks; the server API takes
  the same filter.
- **Output:** `ax get task` shows `SESSION` (e.g. in `-o wide`).
- **Cleanup (optional):** `ax delete tasks --session <id>` deletes a whole session.

### Example

An agent in task `planner-1a2b` splits the work and creates two subtasks, passing its session
on:

    apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
    kind: Task
    metadata:
      name: implement-3c4d
    spec:
      sessionId: 9f2e7c1a-planner
      image: ...

    $ ax get tasks --session 9f2e7c1a-planner
    NAME             SESSION            PHASE      AGE
    planner-1a2b     9f2e7c1a-planner   Running    6m
    implement-3c4d   9f2e7c1a-planner   Running    4m
    test-5e6f        9f2e7c1a-planner   Pending    1m

Each runner tags its telemetry with `session.id=9f2e7c1a-planner`, so the full trajectory
across all three tasks can be collected with one query.

### Alternatives considered

- **Name prefixes:** nothing enforces the convention, names are limited in length, and renaming
  breaks the grouping.
- **Putting it in `spec.config`:** the field is runner-specific and AX doesn't interpret it, so
  the server can't filter on it and other runners won't know where to find it.
- **Tracking sessions outside AX:** every client and telemetry pipeline has to keep its own
  mapping from tasks to sessions, which drifts and isn't visible in `ax get tasks`.

title: AX Studio: a desktop app for AX
body:
The hardest part of trying AX is getting a cluster to run it on. Before running a single task, you need three layers working together:

1. **Kubernetes:** a kind cluster, plus a local container registry connected to it.
2. **Agent Substrate:** cloned and checked out at the version in AX's `go.mod`, built from source, pushed to the registry and installed.
3. **AX:** `ax`, `ax-server` and `ax-task-runner` built from source, the server and runner images built and pushed, and the control plane deployed with a pool of gVisor workers.


Once the cluster is up, using AX is still all CLI and YAML, and could be a barrier for early developers:

- **Writing tasks means writing YAML by hand.** A useful task usually needs a Task, a Workspace (repos, files, MCP servers) and often a Model and secrets, all with matching names.
- **There's no overall view.** `ax get tasks` lists tasks one per line. It can't show what's running across an atespace, which workspaces tasks use, or a task's logs and conditions side by side.

### Proposal

Build **AX Studio**, a desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux that takes you from nothing to running tasks, and lets you watch and manage them. A prototype exists at https://github.com/rakyll/ax-studio.

AX Studio should live in its own repo. It can then be released on its own schedule.

#### Features

- **Clusters:** create a local AX cluster from a name and a worker count, or install AX on an existing cluster. Each cluster shows the health of each layer (Kubernetes, Agent Substrate, AX), so you can see which one is broken. Setup shows progress step by step, and the new cluster is ready to use without changing your current context.
- **Activity:** a sortable table of the atespace's tasks, with running tasks on top. You can resume, suspend or delete tasks, inspect their conditions and follow their logs. A second table lists workspaces (repos, MCP servers, files, and the tasks using each), and you can delete them.
- **Designer:** builds a Task, plus an optional Workspace and Model, with a form or raw YAML, shows the manifest, and creates them. It comes with templates for common runners (Gemini, OpenAI, Claude, GitHub Actions).
- **Terminal:** interactive shells into running tasks, in tabs that stay connected while you use the rest of the app.

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Clusters](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rakyll/ax-studio/main/docs/screenshots/clusters.png) **Clusters** | ![Activity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rakyll/ax-studio/main/docs/screenshots/overview.png) **Activity** |
| ![Map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rakyll/ax-studio/main/docs/screenshots/topology.png) **Map** | ![Designer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rakyll/ax-studio/main/docs/screenshots/designer.png) **Designer** |
| ![Task logs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rakyll/ax-studio/main/docs/screenshots/logs.png) **Task logs** | |


### Related AX changes

- **Terminal support in the process API** (PTY issue): needed for proper interactive shells, including window resizing.
- **Session IDs on tasks** (session issue): would let Activity and Map group the tasks of one run, and clean them up together.

### Open questions

- **Dependencies:** ideally, once AX Studio is installed, it needs nothing else on a laptop to create a cluster and run tasks. What does it take to get there?
- **Distribution:** code signing and notarization for macOS, signing for Windows, and potentially auto-update.
- **Remote clusters:** should cluster management cover only local clusters, or remote ones too?

### Not in scope (for now)

- Replacing the CLI: AX Studio is a companion to `ax`, not a replacement.
- Multi-user or hosted (web) use.

title: fix(ssh): honor --namespace in ax ssh and surface router mTLS errors
body:
Fix three small issues related to ssh

1. Pass the resolved system namespace to runSSH (defaulting to $AX_SYSTEM_NAMESPACE and then ax-system) instead of ignoring -n and reading only $AX_SYSTEM_NAMESPACE.
2. Extract dialGuest and dialRouterTLS helpers from runSSH, and surface the mTLS setup or port-443 forward error when the legacy port-80 fallback also fails.
3. Since ax only reads from the kubectl output pipe, close the parent's write end right after cmd.Start() in tunnel.PortForward so pr.Read observes EOF as soon as kubectl exits instead of hanging until the timeout.

title: feat: machine-readable Substrate compatibility metadata, version handshake, and safe snapshot defaults for Coding Agents
body:
## Summary
When autonomous coding agents (and automated CI/CD pipelines) provision and operate Google AX alongside Agent Substrate on Kubernetes/GKE, they frequently encounter silent or cryptic gRPC/proto API mismatches between AX (`ax-server`, `ax` CLI) and Substrate (`ate-api-server`).

For instance, when Agent Substrate upgraded its protobuf definitions in `v1.0.0-rc.1` (moving from `package ateapi;` with gRPC service `/ateapi.Control/*` to `package substrate.ateapi.v1;` with Go module `go.ate.dev/substrate/api/ateapi/v1`), `ax apply` halts with:
```
rpc error: code = Unimplemented desc = unknown service ateapi.Control
```
Additionally, `DefaultSnapshotsBucket = "gs://dberkov-gke-dev3/ate-env/"` in `internal/substrate/client.go` hardcodes a bucket which triggers:
```
rpc error: code = InvalidArgument desc = actor_template.snapshot_config.storage_location: Forbidden
```
under Substrate v1.0.0 preview gating rules (unless `PerTemplateSnapshotLocation` is explicitly enabled and preview headers are passed).

Because this compatibility information is not exposed in a machine-readable format or validated at startup, coding agents cannot autonomously detect or reconcile version drift, leading to workflow halts.

## Proposed Enhancements

### 1. Machine-Readable Compatibility Matrix (`ax-compat.json` / `ax version --compat --json`)
Provide a structured schema or CLI command that autonomous agents and tooling can query:
```json
{
  "ax_version": "v0.4.0",
  "substrate_compatibility": {
    "supported_range": ">=v1.0.0-rc.1, <v2.0.0",
    "proto_package": "substrate.ateapi.v1",
    "go_module": "go.ate.dev/substrate/api/ateapi/v1"
  }
}
```
This enables agent orchestrators to inspect cluster `ate-api-server` version and select or compile the matching AX container/binary without trial-and-error.

### 2. Runtime Version Handshake / Actionable Error Diagnostic
- In `ax-server` startup and `client.go`, perform a lightweight handshake against `ate-api-server`.
- If `ate-api-server` returns gRPC `Unimplemented` for `ateapi.Control` or `substrate.ateapi.v1.Control`, wrap the error with an explicit diagnostic:
  > *"Proto package mismatch: ax-server was compiled with Substrate client [v0.6.0 (pkg ateapi)], but ate-api-server expects [v1.0.0+ (pkg substrate.ateapi.v1)]. Please align AX and Substrate versions."*

### 3. Default `DefaultSnapshotsBucket` to Empty String `""`
- When `snapshotsBucket` is empty string `""`, protobuf omits `actor_template.snapshot_config.storage_location`.
- Substrate automatically uses its cluster-wide `--snapshot-location`, avoiding preview gate failures (`PerTemplateSnapshotLocation: Forbidden`) and removing developer-specific bucket references (`gs://dberkov-gke-dev3/...` / `gs://snapshot-substrate-test-...`).

### 4. Agent Guidance (`AGENTS.md` / `docs/agent-orchestration.md`)
Add concise documentation or an `AGENTS.md` spec outlining standard conventions for AI agents orchestrating AX:
- How to match AX CLI, `ax-server`, and Substrate images by digest/tag.
- Recommended RBAC and NetworkPolicy labels (e.g. `ate.dev/api-access=true` on AX namespaces).
- Recommended environment overrides (`AX_SNAPSHOTS_BUCKET=""`).

## Context & Impact
Autonomous coding agents are increasingly orchestrating full lifecycle workflows (dispatching tasks, monitoring actors, deploying fixes). Providing machine-readable compatibility metadata and self-describing error diagnostics turns opaque gRPC failures into automated self-healing workflows.

title: Epic: Establish rulesets for branching, tagging, and merging
body:
## Objective

Have GitHub, not convention, enforce how code reaches `main`, release branches and tags. Every change should be reviewed against its final commits and validated before it lands, and release refs should only change through the release process.

## Current state

- Two overlapping rulesets target `main`:
  - `main` blocks deletion.
  - `main: require PR review and CI` blocks force-push, requires a PR with 1 approval, and requires the `build-and-test` check.
- Approvals are **not** dismissed when new commits are pushed (`dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push: false`), although CONTRIBUTING.md says a push after an approval needs a fresh approval.
- The ruleset allows the `merge` method, but the repo settings disable merge commits.
- There is no merge queue, and no workflow triggers on `merge_group`.
- `v*` tags and `release-*` branches have no protection.
- Anyone with write access can create branches on the upstream repo (60+ exist today).
- Rulesets are managed only in the GitHub UI, so changes are neither reviewable nor auditable in the repo.

## Minimum bar

- [ ] Approvals are cleared when new commits are pushed
- [ ] Merge queue on `main` (which checks it runs is decided separately)
- [ ] `v*` tags can only be created, moved or deleted by release managers or the release workflow
- [ ] `release-*` branches are protected (no deletion or force-push; changes only through PRs with CI)

## Planned sub-issues

Each one is tracked as a GitHub sub-issue of this epic:

- #547 Manage rulesets as code and protect release tags and branches (also covers branching and tagging rules)
- #548 Combine the `main` rulesets into a single `protect-main`
- #570 Clear approvals on fresh commits
- #571 Set up a merge queue on `main`
- [RFC] Require contributors to work from forks (not yet filed)

## Rollout

New or changed rulesets start in `evaluate` mode. Once the rule insights show they wouldn't block legitimate work, they switch to `active`.

title: Manage rulesets as code and protect release tags and branches
body:
## Summary

Check AX's repository rulesets into the repo, and use that to add the protection that `main` already has to release tags and release branches, and to enforce branch and tag naming. Ruleset changes are then proposed, reviewed and audited as PRs instead of being edited only in the GitHub UI.

This issue combines four items from the epic (#546): rulesets as code, protecting release tags, protecting release branches, and branching and tagging rules. They are one unit of work: each protection lands as a JSON file in `.github/rulesets/` and is applied with the same script.

## Current state (checked 2026-11-12)

- Two rulesets exist, both on `~DEFAULT_BRANCH`: `main` and `main: require PR review and CI` (merged into one by #548).
- No ruleset targets tags or `release-*` branches. Anyone with write access can create, move or delete a `v*` tag.
- Tags `v0.1.0` … `v0.3.1` were created by hand. All of them follow `vX.Y.Z`; there are no stray tags.
- There are 62 branches on upstream. Most (32) were last updated in July 2026. Common prefixes: `readme-*`, `fix-*`, `antigravity-*`, `agy-*`. Because PRs are squash-merged, `git branch --merged` finds only 1 of them, so cleanup has to check PR state instead.
- `delete_branch_on_merge` is `false`.
- There is no `.github/rulesets/` directory and no `release-*` branch yet.

## Proposal

### 1. Rulesets as code

1. **Export** each active ruleset to `.github/rulesets/<name>.json` with `gh api repos/google/ax/rulesets/<id>`. Remove server-managed fields such as `id`, `node_id`, `_links`, `created_at`, `updated_at` and `source*`, so the files contain only the policy: `name`, `target`, `enforcement`, `conditions`, `rules`, `bypass_actors`.
2. **Apply** with `hack/apply-rulesets.sh`, which a repo admin runs:
   - Match local files to live rulesets by `name`.
   - `PUT /repos/google/ax/rulesets/<id>` for existing rulesets, and `POST /repos/google/ax/rulesets` for new ones.
   - Support `--dry-run`, which shows the differences without changing anything.
   - Never delete live rulesets that have no file. List them instead.
3. **Detect drift** with a scheduled workflow, or a step in an existing one, that compares `.github/rulesets/*.json` with the live rulesets and fails or opens an issue when they differ.
   - Reading `bypass_actors` needs admin. Decide whether this check uses a GitHub App or token with admin read, or compares everything except `bypass_actors`.
4. **Document** the flow in CONTRIBUTING.md or `docs/dev/rulesets.md`: open a PR that edits the JSON, get it reviewed, and after merge an admin runs `hack/apply-rulesets.sh`.

### 2. Protect release tags (`protect-tags.json`)

- Target tags matching `refs/tags/v*`.
- Rules: block creation, update, deletion and non-fast-forward, and require names to match `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$`.
- Bypass list: release managers only, or the release workflow's identity once the tag-driven release workflow (Epic 5) lands.
- This must be in place before releases publish images from tags, following Substrate's `docs/dev/releasing.md`.

### 3. Protect release branches (`protect-release-branches.json`)

- Target `refs/heads/release-*`.
- Rules: block deletion and force-push, require a PR, and require the same status checks as `main`.
- **Open:** how many approvals release-branch PRs need. Substrate uses 0 because its cherry-picks are bot-driven.
- **Open:** whether release branches also use the merge queue. Substrate's don't.

### 4. Branching and tagging rules

- **Branches:** only `main` and `release-X.Y` are long-lived on upstream. The format for any other upstream branch depends on the fork RFC in #546 (require forks, allow only prefixes such as `user/<ldap>/…` or `bot/…`, or keep the current setup). If that RFC adds a branch-name ruleset, it lands here too.
- **Tags:** semantic-version `vX.Y.Z[-pre]` only, with no ad-hoc tags on upstream. Enforced by `protect-tags`.
- **Cleanup:** turn on `delete_branch_on_merge`. For the 62 existing branches, delete those whose PR is merged or closed, and contact the owners of the rest.
- Write the rules down in CONTRIBUTING.md (with the Epic 3 docs update).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every active ruleset on `google/ax` has a matching file in `.github/rulesets/`
- [ ] `hack/apply-rulesets.sh --dry-run` reports no differences against the live configuration right after export
- [ ] `hack/apply-rulesets.sh` creates or updates rulesets from the files, matched by name
- [ ] Drift between the files and the live rulesets is reported automatically
- [ ] A user who isn't a release manager can't create, move or delete a `v*` tag, and tags that don't match the semver pattern are rejected
- [ ] A `release-X.Y` branch can only change through PRs that pass CI, and can't be deleted or force-pushed
- [ ] `delete_branch_on_merge` is on, and stale upstream branches are cleaned up
- [ ] The ruleset change process and the branch and tag naming rules are documented

## Rollout

New rulesets start in `evaluate` mode. Once the rule insights show they wouldn't block legitimate work, they switch to `active`. Suggested order: rulesets as code first, then `protect-tags`, then `protect-release-branches`, then branch cleanup.

## Open questions

- Who are the admins who can run the apply script, and who are the release managers on the tag bypass list?
- Should applying stay a manual admin step, or eventually run automatically after merge using a GitHub App with admin rights on rulesets?
- How many approvals do release-branch PRs need, and do release branches use the merge queue?

## Notes

- Later rulesets changes in this epic (#548, clearing approvals on fresh commits, the merge queue) should each land as a JSON change in this directory.
- Reference: [GitHub REST API: repository rulesets](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules).

title: Combine the main rulesets into a single protect-main ruleset
body:
## Summary

Replace the two overlapping rulesets on `main` with one ruleset, `protect-main`, that holds every rule for the default branch.

## Current state

| Ruleset | Target | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | `~DEFAULT_BRANCH` | `deletion` |
| `main: require PR review and CI` | `~DEFAULT_BRANCH` | `non_fast_forward`; `pull_request` (1 approval, merge methods `merge`/`squash`/`rebase`, `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push: false`); `required_status_checks` (`build-and-test`) |

Problems:
- To see the full policy for `main`, you have to read two rulesets.
- The ruleset allows the `merge` method, but the repo settings disable merge commits (`allow_merge_commit: false`). The two disagree.

## Proposal

Create one `protect-main` ruleset on `~DEFAULT_BRANCH` containing:

- `deletion`
- `non_fast_forward`
- `pull_request`:
  - `required_approving_review_count: 1`
  - `allowed_merge_methods: ["squash", "rebase"]`, matching the repo settings
  - Leave `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push` unchanged here. Changing it is tracked in its own sub-issue, "Clear approvals on fresh commits".
- `required_status_checks`: `build-and-test`, unchanged

This change doesn't make the policy stricter, apart from removing the `merge` method that the repo settings already disable. Stricter rules (stale-approval dismissal, merge queue, more required checks) come in later sub-issues of this epic.

## Rollout

1. Create `protect-main` in `evaluate` mode, next to the two existing rulesets.
2. Check the rule insights to confirm it evaluates the same way as the existing rulesets.
3. Switch `protect-main` to `active`, then delete `main` and `main: require PR review and CI`.

If #547 (Manage repository rulesets as code) lands first, this should land as `.github/rulesets/protect-main.json` and be applied with the script.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exactly one active branch ruleset (`protect-main`) targets `main`
- [ ] `protect-main` contains deletion, non-fast-forward, pull request (1 approval, squash or rebase) and the `build-and-test` required check
- [ ] The old `main` and `main: require PR review and CI` rulesets are deleted
- [ ] Merging a PR still works with squash and rebase

title: Add a `Gateway` resource for Task network policy
body:
A Task today has no network access in either direction, and AX gives users no way to change that. As a result, a Task cannot reach its model, its repository, or its tools does nothing useful, so AX cannot be used for real workloads until this is fixed.

## Proposal

Add a fourth primitive, `Gateway` (`ax.io/v1alpha1`), that declares which traffic may enter and leave a Task. A Task binds at most one Gateway by name, the same way it binds a Workspace. Both directions are lists of allow rules, and anything that matches no rule is denied. Without a Gateway a Task behaves as it does today.

```yaml
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: review-bot
  atespace: default
spec:
  ingress:
    rules:
      # The team's frontend may call the agent's HTTP API.
      - from:
          spiffeIds: ["spiffe://cluster.local/ns/team-a/sa/frontend"]
        ports: {numbers: [8080]}
      # A CI service account may reach the agent's gRPC endpoint.
      - from:
          spiffeIds: ["spiffe://cluster.local/ns/ci/sa/runner"]
        ports: {numbers: [9090]}
  egress:
    rules:
      - https:
          hostnames: ["api.anthropic.com"]
---
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Task
metadata:
  name: review-bot
spec:
  image: "ghcr.io/my-org/my-agent-image@sha256:..."
  gateway:
    name: review-bot
```

- **Ingress.** The router checks the caller's SPIFFE ID and the destination port against the target Task's rules, on top of its cluster-wide allowlist. A Task with no `ingress` rules is reachable only by AX itself: readiness checks, and `ax ssh` when `spec.debug` is set. Once Tasks get SPIFFE identities (`docs/roadmap.md`), one Task can allow another by listing its SPIFFE ID in `from.spiffeIds`.
- **Egress.** Rules allow `http`, `https`, or `tlsPassthrough` traffic to the listed hostnames and ports. `https` rules can inject credentials into matching requests, so secrets never enter the sandbox.

The Gateway must be compatible with Agent Substrate. Egress maps onto Substrate's existing per-actor `EgressPolicy`. Ingress needs a per-actor ingress API in Substrate, which we should propose upstream using the example above, rather than enforce ingress in AX and bypass the router.

## Open questions

1. Should a `Model` contribute an `https` rule with credential injection for its provider endpoint automatically, so users don't have to write it?
2. Is `Gateway` the right name, given that Substrate already uses "egress gateway" for its component?

## Definition of done

- `Gateway` defined in `ax.proto`, mapped in `types.go`, validated in `resources.go`, and documented in `docs/manifests.md` and `docs/networking.md`; postgres `schema.sql` and `schema.go` updated.
- `ax apply/get/describe/delete gateway` work.
- E2E: a Task bound to a Gateway reaches an allowed host and is refused for everything else; an allowed caller reaches the Task and any other caller is refused. A Task with no Gateway behaves as it does today.

title: [Feature Request] Blueprint & Reference Architecture: Integrating Google AX with GitHub Projects for Autonomous Backlog Management
body:
# Feature Request: Blueprint & Reference Architecture for Integrating Google AX with GitHub Projects

**Target Repository**: `google/ax` (https://github.com/google/ax)  
**Issue Type**: Feature Request / Blueprint Proposal  
**Title**: `[Feature Request] Blueprint & Reference Architecture: Integrating Google AX with GitHub Projects for Autonomous Backlog Management`

---

## 1. Summary
Provide an official **Blueprint & Reference Implementation** (documentation, reference webhook dispatcher, and turnkey setup scripts) for using **Google AX** together with **GitHub Projects (v2)** to run an autonomous, laptop-closed backlog management and software delivery workflow on Kubernetes / Agent Substrate.

Connecting Google AX to a project tracking backlog is one of the most common requirements for teams building autonomous agent workflows. However, teams currently face recurring hurdles: webhook recursive loops, Kubernetes/AX manifest naming rejections, silent deadlocks when agents fail, and lack of iteration loops for human playtesting. This blueprint packages production-tested patterns and GitHub best practices into an opinionated starter kit.

---

## 2. Motivation & Real-World Learnings: What We Learned & Mistakes We Made

While integrating Google AX with GitHub Projects and GKE Agent Substrate for an autonomous software engineering pipeline, we encountered several non-obvious failure modes. These friction points serve as the primary motivation for an official blueprint:

### A. The "Todo → Done" Fallacy & The Missing Iteration Loop (`To-be-fixed`)
* **The Mistake**: We initially assumed a simple linear workflow (`Ready` → `In-Progress` → `Done`) would suffice.
* **The Reality**: Autonomous development requires a human-in-the-loop playtesting and review phase once code is deployed. Without a dedicated feedback state, human comments were either ignored or triggered a full re-implementation from scratch that lost prior context.
* **The Solution**: We introduced a five-state Kanban machine: `Backlog` → `Ready` → `In-Progress` → `To-be-fixed` (Human Feedback) → `Done`. When moved to `To-be-fixed`, a lightweight experience reflection step distills the reviewer’s comment into persistent project rules, triggering a targeted fix run without token bloat.

### B. Silent Deadlocks on Agent Failures (Missing `Blocked` Escalation)
* **The Mistake**: When an agent task timed out, hit token budget ceilings (e.g. 400k tokens), or failed self-repair verification after 3 retries, the card remained stuck in `In-Progress` indefinitely with no visibility into why it halted.
* **The Solution**: An explicit failure state transition. On error, the dispatcher removes `In-Progress`, applies a `Blocked Coding Agent` label, tags the issue author/founder (`@user`), posts a collapsible diagnostic log (`<details><summary>Logs</summary>`), and automatically tears down the AX Task resource (`ax delete task`).

### C. Webhook Loop Hazards & Stored Prompt Injection
* **The Mistake**: Listening naively to issue comments or updates caused recursive execution storms: the agent posted a progress comment or PR link, which fired another webhook, re-triggering the AX task. Furthermore, accepting issues from arbitrary public users exposed the system to stored prompt injection.
* **The Solution**: 
  1. Strict bot filtering (`comment.user.type === 'Bot'`) to eliminate self-trigger loops.
  2. HMAC-SHA256 signature verification (`X-Hub-Signature-256`) on all incoming webhooks.
  3. Sender authorization allowlists (`authorizedUsers`) before triggering expensive AX model invocations.
  4. XML prompt encapsulation and input sanitization to strip instruction-override patterns from issue descriptions and feedback comments.

### D. AX Task Manifest & Substrate Validation Pitfalls
* **The Mistake**: Attempting to generate `ax.io/v1alpha1` `Task` manifests directly from GitHub Issue metadata frequently failed with cryptic Kubernetes admission errors:
  * **RFC-1123 Label Rejection**: Raw issue titles contain spaces, uppercase letters, and punctuation. AX `metadata.name` and `metadata.atespace` strictly require lowercase RFC-1123 labels (<= 63 characters).
  * **Image Digest Requirement**: Passing standard tags (e.g., `:latest`) failed in Substrate; Substrate snapshots require images to be pinned by `@sha256:...` digest for reproducibility.
  * **Resource Field Mismatch**: AX Task manifests accept `spec.resources.limits` (CPU and memory) but reject `spec.resources.requests`.
  * **Config Size Ceiling**: Putting large diffs or multi-turn prompt history directly into `spec.config` exceeded the 16 KiB limit.
* **The Solution**: The blueprint should include a reference manifest builder that enforces RFC-1123 sanitization, digest validation, `< 16 KiB` config budgeting, and correct resource schemas.

### E. Ingress & GKE Gateway Health Probing (HTTP 503 Traps)
* **The Mistake**: When exposing an AX webhook dispatcher behind a modern Kubernetes Gateway (`gatewayClassName: gke-l7-global-external-managed`), the load balancer probes `/` over HTTP by default. Because the dispatcher only accepted POST requests on `/webhook/github` and enforced HTTPS, the backend was marked unhealthy, producing continuous `503 Service Unavailable` errors.
* **The Solution**: The blueprint should ship with internal `/healthz` endpoints and an attached `HealthCheckPolicy` manifest out-of-the-box.

---

## 3. Proposed Blueprint Architecture (Aligned with GitHub Best Practices)

Based on [GitHub Projects Best Practices](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/learning-about-projects/best-practices-for-projects), the proposed blueprint would provide a standardized reference implementation across four core areas:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph GitHub["GitHub Ecosystem"]
        Board["GitHub Projects v2 Board\n(Views: Backlog, Telemetry, Triage)"]
        Issue["GitHub Issues & Sub-issues\n(Labels: Ready, In-Progress, To-be-fixed, Blocked)"]
        PR["Pull Requests\n(Refs #123, Auto-merge, Screenshots)"]
    end

    subgraph AXControlPlane["AX & Kubernetes Control Plane"]
        Dispatcher["AX Webhook Dispatcher\n(HMAC-SHA256, Bot-filter, Sanitizer)"]
        AXServer["Google AX Server\n(ax.io/v1alpha1 Workspace & Task)"]
        Substrate["Agent Substrate Runtime\n(gVisor Sandbox, Digest-pinned)"]
    end

    Board <-->|"Sync Status & Fields"| Issue
    Issue -->|"Webhook (labeled: Ready / To-be-fixed)"| Dispatcher
    Dispatcher -->|"Submit Task (@sha256, RFC-1123)"| AXServer
    AXServer -->|"Schedule Actor"| Substrate
    Substrate -->|"Open PR + Post Preview & Logs"| PR
    PR -->|"Squash Merge & Close/Update"| Issue
```

### 1. Communicate Across Issues and Pull Requests
* **Bidirectional Status Sync**: Moving a card to `Ready` or labeling it `To-be-fixed` triggers an AX Task; the dispatcher immediately shifts the card status to `In-Progress`.
* **Rich Completion Telemetry**: When the AX task runner finishes, it opens a linked PR (`Refs #<issue>`), merges it, and posts a rich report to the issue containing:
  * Deployed commit hash and preview URL.
  * Headless browser verification screenshots (mobile and desktop viewports).
  * Consumed token count vs. budget ceiling.
  * Collapsible verification logs (`<details><summary>gVisor Sandbox Verification Log</summary>`).
* **Explicit Blocker Tagging**: If an agent hits a constraint or failure, it removes `In-Progress`, labels the issue `Blocked Coding Agent`, and `@mentions` the assignee with targeted diagnostics.

### 2. Break Down Large Tasks into Manageable Slices
* **Issue Slicing Guidelines**: Guidelines and issue templates instructing users how to structure tasks into small vertical slices (<= 5 files modified per task).
* **Sub-issue Hierarchy**: Leveraging GitHub's sub-issues to break larger epics into independent, testable AX tasks that run within token caps (e.g. 400k tokens per task).

### 3. Customized Views for Different Audiences
The blueprint includes pre-configured GitHub Project views:
* **Product / Reviewer Board (Kanban)**: Focused on delivery: `Ready` → `In-Progress` → `To-be-fixed` → `Done`, with live deployment links and screenshots for playtesting.
* **Engineering / Agent Telemetry (Table)**: Grouped by status, showing custom fields: `Model Route` (e.g., Flash vs. Argon/Pro), `Estimated Effort`, `Token Spend`, `Execution Time`, and `AX Task ID`.
* **Triage / Exception View (Board/Table)**: Filtered exclusively to `Blocked Coding Agent` items to highlight issues requiring human developer intervention.

### 4. Turnkey Setup & Dispatcher Package
* **Reference Webhook Dispatcher**: Lightweight Node.js or Go microservice implementing HMAC verification, bot suppression, sender allowlisting, RFC-1123 task naming, digest verification, and AX task submission.
* **Turnkey Setup Script (`scripts/setup-github.sh` or `ax project setup github`)**: Single CLI command using `gh` to create the GitHub Project board, standard labels, custom fields, and Workload Identity secrets in seconds.
* **Zero-Leak Pre-flight Guardrails**: Instructions for enforcing deterministic gates (`0 tokens`: linting, typechecks, secret scanning) before LLMs are engaged.

---

## 4. Value to the Google AX Community
1. **Accelerated Time-to-Value**: Enables new teams to connect AX to GitHub Projects in 15 minutes instead of spending weeks re-architecting webhook handling, manifest builders, and label state machines.
2. **Standardized Human-in-the-Loop Iteration**: Moves the community beyond simple one-shot script execution to resilient, multi-turn product iteration (`To-be-fixed` and experience reflection).
3. **Hardened Operational Security**: Provides battle-tested patterns for prompt-injection defense, bot loop prevention, and secret isolation.

---

## 5. Potential Discussion Points for Maintainers
* Should the GitHub Webhook Dispatcher live under `google/ax/examples/github-projects` as a reference deployment, or as an optional built-in component/plugin in `ax`?
* Would the team be interested in an `ax project init github` CLI extension that automates the GitHub Project board creation via `gh` CLI?

title: feat: allow creating a task from an actor template
body:
Add optional spec.template field to TaskSpec referencing a Substrate ActorTemplate, allowing tasks to run directly from an existing template.

- Add template (ObjectRef) to TaskSpec in ax.proto and regenerate protos.
- Validate mutual exclusivity of spec.image and spec.template, reject command with template, and require template name.
- Check that the referenced ActorTemplate exists in Substrate at CreateTask time before saving or provisioning, returning FailedPrecondition if not found.
- Reconcile directly against the referenced template without provisioning a per-task ActorTemplate.
- On task deletion, delete only the Actor and skip template cleanup when spec.template is set.
- Update ax describe task to display template name and atespace.
- Add unit tests across types, reconciler, server, and an E2E test exercising the full lifecycle against Substrate.

Refs #491

In the current implementation, a task is rejected at creation time if the referenced ActorTemplate does not exist in Substrate. This is because currently there is no self-healing loop in ax, users would need to delete and recreate the task after the template is created. We will revisit this after reconciliation loop is introduced in the future.

title: chore(substrate): bump substrate to v1.0.0-rc.1 and adapt to Substrate 1.0 changes
body:
### Summary

Upgrade `go.ate.dev/substrate` from `v0.6.0` to `v1.0.0-rc.1` (the published release tag of Substrate 1.0) and adapt AX's client, server, test fixtures, and E2E harness to breaking changes introduced in Substrate 1.0.

### Why & What Changed

1. **Control API Package Migration (`pkg/proto/ateapipb` -> `api/ateapi/v1`)**:
   - **Why**: In Substrate 1.0 (#2996), public APIs were restructured under `api/<api-name>/v1` with Go package `package ateapi`.
   - **What**: Updated imports across `internal/substrate`, `internal/server`, `internal/controller`, and `test/e2e` to `go.ate.dev/substrate/api/ateapi/v1`.

2. **CRD Version Promotion (`ate.dev/v1alpha1` -> `ate.dev/v1`)**:
   - **Why**: Substrate 1.0 graduated `WorkerPool`, `SandboxConfig`, and `CSIDriverConfig` CRDs to `ate.dev/v1` and no longer serves `v1alpha1`.
   - **What**: Updated `test/e2e/manifests/workerpool.yaml` to `apiVersion: ate.dev/v1`.

3. **Per-Template `snapshotConfig.storageLocation` Prohibition & Cleanup**:
   - **Why**: In Substrate 1.0 (#3357), setting `snapshotConfig.storageLocation` on an `ActorTemplate` is forbidden (`InvalidArgument: Forbidden`) unless the `PerTemplateSnapshotLocation` preview gate is enabled. All workloads are intended to use the cluster-wide `--snapshot-location`.
   - **What**: Updated `substrate.BuildActorTemplate` to omit `StorageLocation` by default. Removed the obsolete and unused `DefaultSnapshotsBucket` constant. Updated unit and E2E assertions to verify `SnapshotConfig` presence and `VOLUMES` fidelity without requiring non-empty storage location.

4. **Kind Deployment CLI Migration (`ate-setup --kind`)**:
   - **Why**: In Substrate 1.0 (#3354), `hack/install-ate-kind.sh` was removed in favor of `go run ./cmd/ate-setup --kind`.
   - **What**: Updated `hack/setup-e2e-kind.sh` to call `go run ./cmd/ate-setup --kind` while maintaining fallback support if `hack/install-ate-kind.sh` is present.

5. **Contract & Documentation**:
   - **What**: Updated `docs/installation.md`, `internal/substrate/client.go` (`BuildActorTemplate`), `skills/substrate/SKILL.md`, and `test/e2e/README.md` to explicitly clarify that `snapshotsBucket` / template-level snapshot storage can only be specified when Substrate's `PerTemplateSnapshotLocation` preview feature gate is enabled, otherwise Substrate rejects template creation with `actor_template.snapshot_config.storage_location: Forbidden`.

title: Move AX state out of /workspace into a separate durable directory
body:
Requested by @mayawang on #551, who asked for this as a follow-up to #518. @rakyll may fold it into #551 instead.

#551 merges as-is with the setup marker inside `/workspace`.

The agent and harness modify `/workspace`, so the marker there can be deleted or changed. If that happens, setup reruns on resume and can overwrite the agent's edits.

Proposal: add a second durable volume, mounted at `/ax-state`, alongside the existing `workspace` volume in `internal/substrate/client.go` (around lines 386–396). Move the marker into it.

Done when: the marker survives a volumes-only resume, and the agent can't remove it or prevent setup from being skipped.

Open questions: which path to use, and whether the cost of an extra durable volume is acceptable.
