title: Expose live Substrate actor UIDs in task status and describe output
body:
Task status identifies the Substrate actor by name, but does not expose its UID. Names can be reused when an actor is recreated, so operators cannot reliably match a task to the actor identity in Substrate logs and events (`ate.actor.uid`).

This adds `status.actorUid` to task responses and an `Actor UID` line to `ax describe task <name>`.

### Design and scope

The UID follows the live-read design established in #515: gets and lists read it from the current Substrate actor, and every task store write strips it. A recreated actor's new UID appears on the next read. If the actor is missing or Substrate cannot be reached, the UID is empty and `describe` shows `<none>` rather than a stale identity.

`actor_uid` uses protobuf field 23 to avoid the field numbers in #563's current status schema sketch. Residency and outcome remain with #563. This contributes the actor identity needed for #13; it does not add telemetry events or command-exit detection.

### Tests

- Regression tests fail against the original server implementation and pass with this change. They cover live get/list results, actor recreation, clearing stale UIDs for missing or unreadable actors, and excluding both client-supplied and read-derived UIDs from stored status.
- CLI tests check the current UID, a recreated actor's UID, and the `<none>` display.
- Local `make verify`, builds of the CLI/server/task runner, `go test -count=1 ./...`, and race tests for `./internal/server` and `./cmd/ax` pass. The ordinary local test run skips the opt-in Postgres and E2E tiers.

### Live validation

**Setup:** A separate disposable Kind cluster with Agent Substrate v1.0.0 from its release images, four gVisor workers, PostgreSQL, and AX binaries/images built from this change.

**Actions:** `TestE2E_TaskLifecycleAndSubstrateSync` creates a suspended task, compares its reported UID with the real Substrate actor's nonempty UID, and checks that `ax describe task` prints the same value. It then resumes the task, checks readiness and the worker address, and deletes the task and its Substrate resources.

**Result:** The focused live test passed, and the disposable cluster was removed. The missing/unreachable actor and recreation cases use in-process fixtures in the regression tests. GitHub's [build-and-test job](https://github.com/google/ax/actions/runs/43499320792/job/132140634951), including the Postgres tests, and [full Kind E2E suite](https://github.com/google/ax/actions/runs/43499320682/job/132140634523) also passed on `7a146fb`.

To repeat the focused live test, follow [the E2E setup instructions](https://github.com/google/ax/blob/7a146fb7f5e7945096371fa6ceb31fcb179961c8/test/e2e/README.md) and run:

```sh
make test-e2e E2E_ARGS='-test.run TestE2E_TaskLifecycleAndSubstrateSync'
```

title: ax-server: set up OpenTelemetry tracing, metrics, events, and JSON logs
body:
ax-server has no telemetry. It writes plain-text logs and serves nothing to scrape or collect, so an operator can't see where a slow `CreateTask` spent its time, how often RPCs fail, or which log lines belong together. This PR adds the OpenTelemetry setup that RPC instrumentation and task state events will build on. Part of #13.

The setup follows Agent Substrate's `internal/serverboot`, including its versions (otel v1.45.0, semconv v1.43.0) and its rules for the `OTEL_*` variables. ax-server and Substrate telemetry therefore behave the same way and join on the same attributes.

### What ax-server now does

- **Traces** export over OTLP/gRPC.
  - Sampling: 10% of new traces (`ParentBased(TraceIDRatio(0.1))`), and a caller's sampling decision is followed.
  - Propagation: only W3C trace context; incoming baggage is not trusted.
- **Metrics** are pushed over OTLP, and also served for Prometheus on `:9090/metrics`.
  - `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER` controls only the push: `otlp` (the default) is on; `prometheus` or `none` is off. The new `--metrics-addr` flag controls only `/metrics`, and an empty value turns it off.
  - `/metrics` also serves Go and process metrics. They are not pushed.
  - The SDK's default cardinality limit applies (2000 attribute sets per instrument); `OTEL_GO_X_CARDINALITY_LIMIT` overrides it.
- **Events** go through the new `telemetry.Emit`. With `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER` unset or `none` (the default, as in Substrate), an event is written to stdout as a JSON log line. With `otlp`, it is sent as an OTLP log record instead. With `otlp,console`, it goes to both. An event is never dropped because OTLP is off.
- **Logs** are now JSON on stdout. A line logged while a span is active carries `trace_id`, `span_id`, and `trace_flags`. Log lines are not exported over OTLP.
- **SDK errors** are logged through slog instead of stderr.

**Settings ax-server can't use.** As the OpenTelemetry specification asks, an unknown or invalid value is logged and ignored, which keeps the default. ax-server resolves `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER` itself, because the SDK falls back to sampling every trace. A typo such as `parentbased_traceidratoi`, or a ratio sampler whose argument is missing or out of range, keeps the 10% default. An unknown exporter name keeps the default exporter instead of turning export off.

**Manifests.** Both manifests read the `OTEL_*` settings from a new `ax-otel-config` ConfigMap with `envFrom`. They also set `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` from the downward API: `k8s.namespace.name`, `k8s.pod.name`, `k8s.pod.uid`, and `service.instance.id` set to the pod UID, as Substrate does.
- `deploy/ax-server.yaml` ships with OTLP push off (`OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER: none`, `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER: prometheus`). An install without a collector therefore logs no export errors and loses nothing: metrics stay on `/metrics` and events go to stdout. Connecting a collector means editing the ConfigMap; `docs/observability.md` shows how.
- `test/e2e/manifests/ax-server.yaml` points at the collector that Substrate's kind overlay deploys (`opentelemetry-collector.otel-system.svc:4317`), with `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER: otlp,console`.
- Port `9090` is exposed as `metrics` on the Service; probes and the API stay on `:8080`.

`internal/axattr` fixes the attribute names AX will put on spans and events. For actor identity it reuses Substrate's `ate.atespace` and `ate.actor.uid`, and it keeps those and the other identity attributes off metrics. `docs/observability.md` documents all of this for operators.

Nothing records spans, metrics, or events yet; that starts with the RPC instrumentation and task state event PRs.

**Behavior changes:**
- ax-server's logs change from slog text to JSON.
- ax-server also listens on `:9090`.

### Validation

- **Unit tests:** `go test ./internal/telemetry` (also with `-race -count=3`) covers:
  - spans, a metric, and an event delivered over OTLP to an in-process gRPC collector, with the `ax-server` resource;
  - `OTEL_*_EXPORTER=none` sending nothing, while spans are still sampled and `/metrics` still serves;
  - events written to stdout by default, OTLP only with `otlp`, and both with `otlp,console`;
  - the default sampler: about 10% of 4,000 root spans sampled, and children follow a sampled or unsampled parent;
  - invalid sampler settings (a typo, a missing ratio, a ratio of 10) keeping the 10% default, plus a table of sampler and exporter values;
  - only `traceparent`/`tracestate` propagated;
  - `/metrics` serving an instrument, Go and process metrics, and the resource; 300 attribute sets with no overflow under the default limit, and 100 series with the overflow series when `OTEL_GO_X_CARDINALITY_LIMIT=100`;
  - the log handler adding `trace_id`/`span_id`/`trace_flags` only when a span is active.

  `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, gofmt, and `go mod tidy` pass.
- **Live cluster:**
  - **Setup:** a GKE 1.37 cluster with Agent Substrate v1.0.0-rc.1 and a gVisor worker pool, running ax-server from this branch with the E2E manifest. The ConfigMap pointed it at an OpenTelemetry Collector with a debug exporter, with a 10 s metric push interval.
  - **Result:** the full E2E suite passed (8/8). All 86 log lines ax-server wrote during the run were JSON, with no SDK errors or warnings, while it pushed metrics every 10 s. The downward-API resource reached the SDK:

  ```
  {"time":"2026-11-06T21:14:02.543509374Z","level":"INFO","msg":"tracing initialized","export":true}
  {"time":"2026-11-06T21:14:02.543842658Z","level":"INFO","msg":"metrics initialized","export":true}
  {"time":"2026-11-06T21:14:02.544556911Z","level":"INFO","msg":"OTLP logs export initialized","exporter":"console,otlp"}

  $ curl -s localhost:9090/metrics | grep ^target_info
  target_info{k8s_namespace_name="ax-system",k8s_pod_name="ax-server-5cf64fb5f-lzm9g",k8s_pod_uid="7918ee31-…",service_instance_id="7918ee31-…",service_name="ax-server",telemetry_sdk_language="go",telemetry_sdk_name="opentelemetry",telemetry_sdk_version="1.45.0"} 1
  ```

  Nothing records data yet, so the collector received no data points. OTLP delivery of each signal is covered by the unit test against the in-process collector, not by the live run.

title: [POC-DNS] feat(cli): add ax local, ax install/uninstall, and local installer guide
body:
## Summary This PR adds a self-contained CLI installer and local development stack so developers can stand up AX locally in one command and promote the exact same `Task` manifests to a remote Kubernetes cluster (e.g., GKE) without manual YAML surgery or external setup scripts: - **`ax local `**: Bootstraps a local Kubernetes 1.36+ Kind cluster, Agent Substrate `v1.0.0-rc.1`, and AX in one command (auto-downloading `kind` / `kubectl` into `~/.ax/bin/` on demand without `sudo`). - **`ax install` / `ax uninstall`**: Resolves `@sha256` image digests (via `go-containerregistry/pkg/crane`), idempotently configures AX caller permissions in Agent Substrate (`ate-api-server`, `atenet-router`, and `k8s-credential-provider` gated by `ax.io/credential="true"`), and deploys/removes `ax-postgres` + `ax-server`. - **`ax ctx [name]`**: Lists kubeconfig contexts with live AX tunnel status and switches the active context (`kubectl config use-context`), while isolating cached router mTLS certs by cluster `server + CA` fingerprint. For the full end-to-end user journey (local bootstrap -> task/snapshot verification -> zero-diff promotion to GKE -> cleanup), see **[`docs/local_installer.md`](https://github.com/YoyinZyc/ax/blob/dfbd45da75d7d0c1216fbd20162a98f22054aeba/docs/local_installer.md)**. The installer follows three-layer installation: related issue: https://github.com/google/ax/issues/526 Note: the pr is just for poc. --- ## Dependency Gaps, Trade-offs & Temporary Code Several parts of `internal/install/` exist solely to bridge current packaging gaps in upstream dependencies. They are intentionally isolated behind narrow package boundaries so they can be deleted cleanly once those gaps close: | Current Dependency Gap | Pragmatic Trade-off in This PR | Temporary Code to Delete Later | |---|---|---| | **1. Agent Substrate has no Helm chart yet**
Upstream currently distributes Kustomize overlays + `ate-setup` (requiring a Substrate git checkout, `ko`, and `openssl`). | - **For `ax local`**: Embed pre-rendered Substrate `v1.0.0-rc.1` manifests (synced deterministically via `hack/sync-substrate-manifests.sh` and checked against `go.mod` in unit tests) and generate local CA/JWT keys + Postgres mTLS init in pure Go.
- **For `ax install`**: Reconcile Substrate caller allowlists by patching `ate-system` flags/ConfigMaps via `kubectl`. | Once Substrate ships a Helm chart:
- Delete `internal/install/substrate/` (`manifests/*.yaml`, `bootstrap.go`, `pki.go`) and `hack/sync-substrate-manifests.sh` (~6,300 lines, mostly generated YAML), replacing them with `helm upgrade --install`.
- Delete `internal/install/axdeploy/authz.go` once caller allowlists are exposed via Helm values or declarative config. | | **2. Pre-built AX images (`ghcr.io/google/ax/*`) are not published yet**
Meanwhile, Substrate strictly requires `@sha256`-pinned task images so gVisor snapshots stay valid across nodes. | - Added `--from-source ` to cross-compile, build, and push AX images to a local loopback registry (`127.0.0.1:5001`) or a user's cloud registry.
- Added `crane.Digest` tag-to-`@sha256` resolution so standard registry tags work automatically once images are published. | Once official AX release images are published:
- Normal users will no longer need `--from-source` (or a Go/Docker build environment on `ax install`).
- The local loopback registry setup in `internal/install/cluster/kind.go` (`ensureLocalRegistry`) can be skipped/removed for default `ax local up` runs. | | **3. AX manifests are raw YAML (`deploy/*.yaml`) rather than a chart** | `deploy/embed.go` embeds `deploy/postgres.yaml` and `deploy/ax-server.yaml` as the single source of truth and rewrites namespaces/image placeholders in Go. | If AX adopts a Helm chart, `deploy/embed.go` string rendering can be removed in favor of chart values. | go.mod change: Adds go-containerregistry v0.21.7 (matching Substrate) for OCI digest resolution and Docker keychain auth > **Reviewer tip:** Over half of the line count in this PR (`internal/install/substrate/manifests/01..07-*.yaml`, ~5,460 lines) is deterministically generated from Agent Substrate `v1.0.0-rc.1` by `hack/sync-substrate-manifests.sh` and verified by `TestEmbeddedManifestsMatchGoModVersion` — you can safely collapse those 7 files during review. --- ## Verification - **Unit & contract tests**: `go mod tidy`, `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...` - **End-to-end manual verification**: - Verified full `ax local up --from-source .` -> `Task` apply / `ssh` / `suspend` / `resume` -> `ax local stop` / `up` / `delete` lifecycle on a clean Linux environment. - Verified multi-cluster promotion (`ax ctx` + `ax install --from-source . --image-repo `) and `ax uninstall` against a live GKE 1.37 cluster running Agent Substrate `v1.0.0-rc.1`.

title: New contributors now introduce themselves through a vouch request before opening pull requests
body:
## What changes

First-time contributors will introduce themselves in a "Vouch Request" discussion. A maintainer replies and adds their handle to `.github/VOUCHED.td`. After that they open pull requests as usual. Collaborators with write access and bots are always allowed.

This uses [vouch](https://github.com/mitchellh/vouch), following the First-Time Contributors flow in [Ghostty's CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#first-time-contributors). The goal is a friendly, visible front door for open source developers, and a way to keep reviewer time on contributors who understand their change.

## Contents

- `.github/VOUCHED.td`: the trust list, seeded with past contributors who are not collaborators (collaborators need no entry).
- `.github/workflows/vouch-check-pr.yml`: runs `check-pr` on `pull_request_target`. The action is pinned to the v1.5.0 commit SHA. The workflow never checks out PR code and has only `contents: read` and `pull-requests: write`.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: new "First-Time Contributors" section.
- `AGENTS.md`: one line in rule E.

## Rollout

- The check runs with `dry-run: true`, so it only reports what it would do. A follow-up PR flips it to enforcing (`dry-run` removed) after we have watched it for a week or two.
- Before merging, someone with admin rights needs to create the **Vouch Request** category in Discussions. The `CONTRIBUTING.md` link points to it.

## Not included, and why

- A comment-driven manage workflow (`!vouch` on a discussion). Pull requests opened with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger CI, so a bot PR that edits `VOUCHED.td` could not get the required `build-and-test` check. That needs a token decision (for example a GitHub App) first. Until then, maintainers update `VOUCHED.td` with a normal PR.
- Gating issues. Only pull requests are checked for now.

## Testing

- No Go code changed, so `go test` and `go build` were not run.
- The workflow YAML parses, `git diff --check` is clean, `VOUCHED.td` is sorted, and every listed handle resolves on GitHub.
- The workflow cannot run before merge: `pull_request_target` uses the workflow from the base branch.

Drafted with an AI coding assistant; I reviewed and tested every change.

title: docs: add local development, prebuilt runners, and gateway to the roadmap
chore(substrate): bump to v1.0.0 and install it from release images images E2E
body:
Bump go.ate.dev/substrate from v1.0.0-rc.1 to v1.0.0. AX code is unchanged. Between rc.1 and 1.0 the Control API changed only in comments, plus three stricter validations:
- Capabilities.add takes only an allowlist (AX sets none).
- VolumeMount.mount_path must not be /dev, /proc, /sys or under them (AX mounts only /workspace).
- SnapshotConfig.storage_location segments may contain only [A-Za-z0-9_-] and may not be "atespaces". AX passes snapshotsBucket through unchecked, so Substrate rejects an invalid value at template creation.

E2E now installs Substrate only from its published release images in ghcr.io/agent-substrate/substrate and never builds it:

- hack/setup-e2e-kind.sh stops early unless SUBSTRATE_REF is a release tag (vX.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z-rc.N), the Substrate checkout is clean at that tag, its ate-setup supports --image-repo, and every image the install uses exists under the tag. It installs through ATE_IMAGE_REPO/ATE_IMAGE_TAG and pins the WorkerPool worker image by digest, using an anonymous registry token. The ko source build, the local registry cache (SUBSTRATE_IMAGE_CACHE_DIR) and the older install-ate.sh paths are removed. SUBSTRATE_IMAGE_REPO points at a mirror.
- Makefile: remove test-e2e-head; Substrate main has no published images.
- e2e.yml: remove the Substrate image cache steps. The nightly run (06:00 UTC) now tests the go.mod release instead of Substrate main. The workflow_dispatch input takes a release tag.

go.ate.dev/substrate must therefore stay on a release tag; a pseudo-version fails E2E setup.

Update test/e2e/README.md and skills/substrate/SKILL.md to match.

title: cli: add --trace to trace a command
body:
ax-server cannot join a slow or failed command to the client that issued it, because the CLI sends no trace context. With `--trace`, an `ax` command starts a sampled root span, prints `Trace ID: <id>` to stderr, and sends a W3C `traceparent` on every AX RPC. ax-server (#557) and Substrate sample ParentBased. When ax-server instruments its RPC handlers and its Substrate client, they follow this decision and record the whole request.

- Without `--trace`, the CLI creates no tracer and sends no trace context, so ax-server's own sampler decides for CLI traffic, as with `kubectl ate`.
- RPCs are client spans under the command span, and resolving the ax-server address (which may start a port-forward) is a child span. CLI spans are exported over OTLP only when `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set, in one call when the command ends, with no retry and a 2 s limit. A failed export prints a warning that names the endpoint and gives the error.
- `ax ssh` returns the remote exit code instead of calling `os.Exit`, so the command span ends and the port-forward is cleaned up. The double Ctrl-C exit waits at most 200 ms for the export.
- `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER` and the resource use #557's rules, which move into `internal/telemetry/otelenv` so that ax-server and the CLI share them. Importing `internal/telemetry` into the CLI would add about 1.3 MB of exporters.
- `docs/observability.md` has a CLI traces section.

Pins `otel v1.45.0` as #557 does, and `otelgrpc v0.70.0` as Substrate does. Server spans join these traces once ax-server adds the `otelgrpc` server handler.

Refs #13, #452.

## Testing

- `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go mod tidy` are clean. New tests in `cmd/ax/trace_test.go` and `internal/telemetry/otelenv` cover the header with and without `--trace`, span parents, resource attributes, export and SDK warnings, streaming RPCs, the exporter and resource rules, one export at the end, the export limits, and exit codes. A smoke test of the built binary against a local OTLP receiver and a fake AX server showed one export with the command, resolve, and `ListTasks` spans, and no `traceparent` without `--trace`.

title: Epic: v1alpha1 API updates (Profile, Workspace, Task, Gateway)
api: split ax.proto into per-resource files
body:
First step of #563: split `pkg/apis/v1alpha1/ax.proto` into one file per resource.

- `ax.proto` keeps only the `AX` service; messages move to `common.proto`, `task.proto`, `workspace.proto`, and `model.proto`.
- No wire, JSON, or Go API changes; every message and the service have identical descriptors before and after.
- Most of the diff is regenerated `*.pb.go`. `AGENTS.md` and `docs/runner.md` are updated for the new layout.

title: api: generate and verify protos with buf
body:
There was no `make generate`, and nothing checked that the checked-in `*.pb.go` match the `.proto` files. This adds both.

- `make generate` formats and lints the `.proto` files, then regenerates the Go code. CI (`build-and-test`) runs it and fails on any diff or untracked file.
- `buf.yaml`: STANDARD lint minus four rules AX deliberately differs on (commented). Breaking-change rules are commented out while the API is v1alpha1.
- `buf.gen.yaml`: protoc-gen-go and protoc-gen-go-grpc are go.mod `tool` directives, and buf runs via `go run`, so no protoc install is needed.
- Generated `*.pb.go` change only in their version headers; `ax.proto` loses two blank lines (formatting).
- AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md point to `make generate`.

title: refactor: extract apivalidation, resources, and server workspace handlers
body:
Pure mechanical refactor with no wire, schema, or behavior changes:

- **`pkg/apis/v1alpha1`**: Keep strictly focused on generated protobuf types, constants, and YAML serialization (matching Agent Substrate's `api/ateapi/v1` layout).
- **`internal/apivalidation`**: Extract server-side manifest admission validation (`common.go`, `task.go`, `workspace.go`, `model.go`).
- **`internal/resources`**: Extract Kubernetes CPU/memory quantity parsing (`quantity.go`).
- **`internal/server/workspace.go`**: Split Workspace gRPC handlers out of `internal/server/server.go` for readability ahead of WS5 changes.

title: api: add the Gateway API and manifest validation
body:
API for the `Gateway` resource (part of #549). Nothing is served yet: `ax apply` does not accept `kind: Gateway`, and ax-server rejects a task that sets `spec.gateway`.

- `gateway.proto`, the Gateway RPCs, and `TaskSpec.gateway`. `spec.egress` is Agent Substrate's `EgressRule`, so `make generate` links the Substrate module for buf.
- `ValidateGateway` requires one kind per rule and rejects `*`, `localhost`, IP addresses, credentials outside exact `https` hosts, and passthrough rules without ports. Substrate validates the rest.
- Hostnames inside the cluster are allowed, as in Substrate. A name check cannot tell where a name resolves, so protecting AX's own services is left to a NetworkPolicy and #376.
- Gateway section in `docs/manifests.md`.

Follow-ups: (1) store, server, and CLI; (2) enforcement through the actor's Substrate `EgressPolicy`, with E2E.

title: E2E flaky: `ax resume` fails with "no worker has room for the actor" right after setup
body:
The Kind E2E suite failed once on #566 and passed on re-run:
https://github.com/google/ax/actions/runs/42960996660/job/130327233529

Every task test failed at its first `ax resume` with `ResourceExhausted: no worker has room for the actor`.

**Cause:** the tests start before Substrate's workers are schedulable. A worker pod is Ready as soon as it registers, but the scheduler skips it until atelet has downloaded the gVisor runtimes and the worker has reported them (agent-substrate/substrate#3276). `hack/setup-e2e-kind.sh` only waits for the Deployment rollout.

**Fix (test-only):** wait for schedulable workers, or retry resume on `ResourceExhausted` as Substrate's own e2e does. Also add atelet and worker logs to the failure dump; without them this run cannot show why the workers were slow.

**Follow-up:** ax-server returns this error as `Internal` and marks the task `Failed`. It could be treated as transient, like the errors in #463.

title: server, cli: add Gateway CRUD and ax commands
body:
Store, serve and manage Gateways (part of #549). Their rules are not applied to tasks yet.

- Gateway persistence (memory and Postgres) and the five RPCs; Create fails if the gateway exists, Update if it does not.
- `CreateTask` rejects a task whose `spec.gateway` does not exist.
- `ax apply`, `get`, `describe`, and `delete` for gateways.

Follow-up: enforcement through the actor's Substrate `EgressPolicy`.

title: Clear approvals on fresh commits
body:
## Summary

Dismiss existing approvals when new commits are pushed to a PR, so every change is approved against its final commits. This makes the `main` ruleset match what CONTRIBUTING.md already says.

## Current state (checked 2026-11-12)

The `pull_request` rule in `main: require PR review and CI` has:

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| `required_approving_review_count` | `1` |
| `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push` | **`false`** |
| `require_last_push_approval` | `false` |
| `require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes` | `true` |
| `require_code_owner_review` | `false` |

CONTRIBUTING.md says: "A push after an approval needs a fresh approval." The ruleset doesn't enforce that today, so a PR can be approved, changed, and then merged without anyone reviewing the change.

## Proposal

On `protect-main` (#548):

- Set `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push: true`.
- **Decide** whether to also set `require_last_push_approval: true`. This means someone other than the person who pushed last must approve, which blocks "approve, then quietly push again" by a reviewer.
  - Pros: closes the self-push gap that stale-review dismissal alone leaves open.
  - Cons: a maintainer who pushes a small fix to someone else's PR needs a third person to approve.
- Leave `require_code_owner_review` unchanged. It's tracked separately in Epic 3.

Land this as a change to `.github/rulesets/protect-main.json` (#547). If that isn't ready, apply it in the UI and record it in the issue.

Update CONTRIBUTING.md to tell authors to use "Re-request review" after pushing to an approved PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pushing a commit to an approved PR removes the approval, and the PR can't merge until it is approved again
- [ ] The decision on `require_last_push_approval` is recorded here, and the ruleset matches it
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md describes what the ruleset enforces

## Rollout

Change the rule in `evaluate` mode first if it lands with other changes. On its own, this is low risk, so it can go straight to `active`.

## Dependencies

- Lands on the combined `protect-main` ruleset from #548.
- Ideally lands as a JSON change through #547.

Part of #546.

title: Set up a merge queue on main
body:
## Summary

Add a merge queue to `main`, so PRs land through GitHub instead of being merged by hand, and each PR is validated against the latest `main` (plus any PRs ahead of it in the queue) before it lands.

## Current state (checked 2026-11-12)

- No `merge_queue` rule on `main`. The author merges once the PR is approved and CI is green (CONTRIBUTING.md).
- `allow_auto_merge` is `false` in the repo settings.
- No workflow triggers on `merge_group`:

| Workflow | Job name | Triggers | Required today? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `go.yml` | `build-and-test` | `push` (main), `pull_request` | Yes |
| `e2e.yml` | `E2E (Kind / Substrate ${{ inputs.substrate_ref \|\| 'go.mod' }})` | `push` (main), `pull_request`, nightly `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch` | No |
| `check-binaries.yml` | `check-no-binaries` | `pull_request` | No |

- `strict_required_status_checks_policy` is `false`, so a PR can merge with checks that ran against an older `main`.

## Proposal

1. Add a `merge_queue` rule to `protect-main` (#548). Starting point, copied from Substrate:

   | Parameter | Value |
   |---|---|
   | `merge_method` | `SQUASH` |
   | `grouping_strategy` | `ALLGREEN` |
   | `min_entries_to_merge` | `1` |
   | `max_entries_to_merge` | `5` |
   | `max_entries_to_build` | `5` |
   | `min_entries_to_merge_wait_minutes` | `5` |
   | `check_response_timeout_minutes` | `60` |

2. Turn on `allow_auto_merge`, so a PR can be marked to merge as soon as it is approved and green.
3. Land the rule as a change to `.github/rulesets/protect-main.json` (#547).
4. Update CONTRIBUTING.md: replace "the author merges" with "add to the merge queue" (or enable auto-merge), for both member and external-contributor PRs.

## Dependencies (Epic 2, not yet filed)

The queue only works once CI supports it. These need to land first:

- **Run every PR workflow on `merge_group`.** Add `merge_group:` to `go.yml`, `e2e.yml` and `check-binaries.yml`, and make base-ref logic handle `github.event.merge_group.base_ref`. Without this, required checks never report in the queue and every PR times out. (Substrate #1712.)
- **Stable required-check names.** The e2e job name is dynamic, so it can't be a required check. PR and queue runs should report a fixed name such as `e2e`. (Substrate #2225.)
- **[RFC] Merge queue validation stages.** Decide which checks run before the queue, in the queue, after merge and nightly, especially whether e2e blocks in the queue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PRs to `main` can only land through the merge queue
- [ ] The queue's required checks match the list decided in the Epic 2 validation-stages RFC
- [ ] Auto-merge is enabled in the repo settings
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md describes the queue flow

## Rollout

1. Land the Epic 2 workflow changes, and confirm that `merge_group` runs report the expected check names.
2. Add the `merge_queue` rule with `protect-main` in `evaluate` mode, and check rule insights.
3. Switch to `active` and announce the change to contributors.

## Open questions

- Squash only, or allow rebase too? A merge queue uses one merge method, so this also decides whether the ruleset still needs to allow rebase.
- Batch size and wait time: start with Substrate's values, and adjust once e2e duration and flakiness in the queue are known.

Part of #546.

title: ci: manage repository rulesets as code and combine the main rulesets
body:
## Summary

Moves AX's repository rulesets into the repo, and replaces the two overlapping rulesets on `main` with a single `protect-main`. This is the base of the rulesets stack for #546:

1. **This PR**: rulesets as code + `protect-main` (#548, part of #547)
2. Clear approvals on fresh commits (#570)
3. Protect release tags and release branches (rest of #547)
4. Merge queue on `main` (#571)

## Changes

- **`.github/rulesets/protect-main.json`**: exported from the two live rulesets (`main` and `main: require PR review and CI`) and merged into one. The only change in policy: `allowed_merge_methods` drops `merge`, which the repo settings already disable.
- **`hack/apply-rulesets.sh`**: syncs the files with GitHub. Rulesets are matched by name, and the script never deletes a live ruleset.
  - no flag: create or update (repo admin)
  - `--dry-run`: print the diff
  - `--check`: diff, and exit 1 on drift
  - `--export`: write the live rulesets to the files
- **`.github/workflows/rulesets.yml`**: on PRs that touch the rulesets, prints the `--dry-run` diff. Daily and on manual dispatch, runs `--check`, which fails on drift.
- **`docs/rulesets.md`**: what is enforced, how to change a ruleset, and how drift is reported. Linked from CONTRIBUTING.md. AGENTS.md is updated to match.

## Testing

Run locally against the live repo (read-only, as a non-admin):

```
$ RULESETS_DIR=/tmp/rs hack/apply-rulesets.sh --export && RULESETS_DIR=/tmp/rs hack/apply-rulesets.sh --check
=== main: up to date
=== main: require PR review and CI: up to date
$ hack/apply-rulesets.sh --dry-run
=== protect-main: not on GitHub; would create it from .github/rulesets/protect-main.json
=== main: require PR review and CI: on GitHub (id 25031200) but has no file; not deleting it
=== main: on GitHub (id 16615367) but has no file; not deleting it
```

## After merge (repo admin)

1. Run `hack/apply-rulesets.sh --dry-run`, then `hack/apply-rulesets.sh`. This creates `protect-main`. It is `active`, but it adds nothing stricter than the existing rulesets.
2. Confirm that a PR still merges with squash and rebase. Then delete `main` and `main: require PR review and CI` in **Settings → Rules → Rulesets**.
3. Check that `bypass_actors: []` matches what you want. Non-admins can't see the current bypass list, so it couldn't be exported.

Until step 2 is done, the daily drift check fails, because the two old rulesets have no file.

Fixes #548. Part of #547.

title: ci: dismiss approvals when new commits are pushed to a PR
body:
## Summary

Sets `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push: true` on `protect-main`, so pushing a commit to an approved PR dismisses the approval. CONTRIBUTING.md already says this happens; now the ruleset enforces it.

Stacked on #572. Review only the top commit.

## Changes

- `.github/rulesets/protect-main.json`: `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push: false` → `true`.
- CONTRIBUTING.md: after pushing to an approved PR, use **Re-request review**.
- docs/rulesets.md, AGENTS.md: updated to match.

## Decision: `require_last_push_approval`

This PR leaves `require_last_push_approval` at `false`. Setting it to `true` would also block a reviewer from approving and then pushing their own commit, but a maintainer who pushes a fix to someone else's PR would then need a third person to approve. Comment here if you'd rather turn it on, and I'll add it to this PR.

## After merge (repo admin)

`hack/apply-rulesets.sh --dry-run`, then `hack/apply-rulesets.sh`.

Fixes #570.

title: ci: protect release tags and release branches
body:
## Summary

Adds two rulesets, both in `evaluate` mode, so release refs can only change through the release process. Stacked on #573. Review only the top commit.

## Changes

- **`.github/rulesets/protect-tags.json`**, on **all** tags:
  - Blocks creation, update, deletion and force-push for everyone except **repo admins** (`RepositoryRole` 5). Today that's @rakyll, who has cut every release so far, plus @mayawang and google-admin.
  - Requires names to match `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$`.
  - It targets `~ALL` rather than only `v*`, which also keeps ad-hoc tags off upstream. All 7 existing tags (`v0.1.0`–`v0.3.1`) already match the pattern.
- **`.github/rulesets/protect-release-branches.json`**, on `refs/heads/release-*`: the same rules as `protect-main` (no deletion or force-push, PR with 1 approval, stale approvals dismissed, `build-and-test`), without a merge queue. No `release-*` branches exist yet.
- **`go.yml`** now also runs on `push` and `pull_request` for `release-*`. Otherwise `build-and-test` never reports on release-branch PRs, and the required check can never pass.
- **docs/rulesets.md**: adds the branch and tag naming rules (only `main` and `release-X.Y` are long-lived; tags are `vX.Y.Z[-pre]`). AGENTS.md is updated to match.

## Open questions

- **Release managers:** should anyone besides repo admins be able to create tags? Once the tag-driven release workflow lands (Epic 5), its identity should be added to `bypass_actors`.
- **Approvals on release branches:** this PR uses 1. Substrate uses 0 because its cherry-picks are bot-driven.
- **Who can create `release-*` branches:** this PR doesn't restrict creation. We could add a `creation` rule with an admin bypass.

## After merge (repo admin)

1. Run `hack/apply-rulesets.sh`. The new rulesets are created in `evaluate` mode.
2. Watch **Settings → Rules → Insights** for about a week. Then switch both to `"enforcement": "active"` in a follow-up PR.
3. Branch cleanup (#547):
   - Turn on **Automatically delete head branches** (`delete_branch_on_merge`).
   - Delete upstream branches whose PRs are merged or closed. PRs are squash-merged, so `git branch --merged` finds only 1 of the 62. Check PR state instead.

Part of #547.

title: ci: land pull requests to main through a merge queue
body:
## Summary

Adds a merge queue to `main`, so each PR is tested on top of the latest `main` (plus anything ahead of it in the queue) before it lands, instead of being merged by hand. Stacked on #574. Review only the top commit.

## Changes

- **`.github/rulesets/protect-main.json`**: adds a `merge_queue` rule, starting from Substrate's settings:

  | Parameter | Value |
  |---|---|
  | `merge_method` | `SQUASH` |
  | `grouping_strategy` | `ALLGREEN` |
  | `min_entries_to_merge` / `max_entries_to_merge` / `max_entries_to_build` | 1 / 5 / 5 |
  | `min_entries_to_merge_wait_minutes` | 5 |
  | `check_response_timeout_minutes` | 60 |

- **`go.yml`** now triggers on `merge_group`. `build-and-test` is the only required check, so it must report in the queue, or queued PRs time out after 60 minutes.
- **CONTRIBUTING.md**: the Merging section now describes **Merge when ready** and the queue, for both member and external PRs. docs/rulesets.md and AGENTS.md are updated to match.

## Scope

This PR covers only what the queue needs to work with today's single required check. Out of scope, for follow-up CI work:

- Running `e2e` and `check-no-binaries` on `merge_group`.

title: ci: add make verify with golangci-lint
body:
Adds `make verify` as the one presubmit command, run locally and in CI.

- It runs `make generate`, `go mod tidy`, `go fmt`, and golangci-lint; CI fails on a finding or any diff.
- golangci-lint is pinned in `hack/tools/golangci-lint` with the standard linters.

title: Tasks: bind multiple Models and let the agent discover them (`/v1/models`)
body:
### Problem

Right now a task effectively gets one model. `TaskSpec` has no model field at all, so the model is whatever the runner is told in `spec.config` (e.g. `model` for the Claude Code runner) plus a key in `spec.env`. The proposals we have for fixing that (#348's `spec.modelRef`, and the `Model` changes in #516 and #475) all keep the same shape: one task, one `Model`, one provider + model + key.

I think that is too restrictive. Agents regularly want more than one model in a single task: a cheap model for subagents or summarization and a stronger one for planning, a fallback when a provider is rate limited, or just letting the harness pick. Most harnesses already know how to do this if they can ask "which models do I have?", which is what `GET /v1/models` is in the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs.

### Proposal

Two parts, and the second is more open than the first.

**1. A task binds a list of models, not one.**

```yaml
kind: Task
spec:
  models:
    - name: claude-model
    - name: default-model
```

Each entry references a `Model` in the task's atespace. If we add a singular `modelRef` first, moving to a list later is an API break, whereas a list with one entry covers the single-model case today. So I'd rather start with the list.

**2. The agent can discover what it was given.**

At the very least, the bound models should be readable inside the sandbox, next to the existing metadata endpoints:

```
GET $AX_METADATA_URL/metadata/v1alpha1/ax/models
```

returning name, provider and model ID for each bound `Model` (no credentials).

What I actually want is an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/models` that the agent can point its SDK at, so existing harnesses work without knowing anything about AX. That raises the question of what serves it and whether it also proxies the model calls. Options I can see:

1. Metadata only: the runner serves the list, the agent calls providers directly, and credentials come from egress injection (#475).
2. The runner serves `/v1/models` in the provider's format on loopback, still only a list.
3. A model gateway serves `/v1/models` and proxies the inference calls, which also gives us one place for budgets and usage (#471).

Option 1 is small and doesn't close off 2 or 3, so it seems like the right first step.

### A second axis: `Model` itself holds multiple models

Another way to get at this is to make `Model` one provider with many models, instead of one provider + one model:

```yaml
kind: Model
metadata:
  name: anthropic
spec:
  provider: anthropic
  secretKey: { name: anthropic-api-secret, key: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }
  models:
    - name: claude-opus-5
      parameters: { maxTokens: 16000 }
    - name: claude-haiku-5
```

I like this because it matches what a provider's `/v1/models` already returns: one endpoint and one credential, many models. It also lines up with egress injection, since it is one credential per host, which is the limit #475 calls out. And nothing consumes `Model` today, so changing `spec.model` into a list is cheap now and gets harder once tasks bind it.

The costs are that `parameters` has to move to each entry, and the kind is really a provider at that point, so the name `Model` gets misleading (see #356).

I don't think this replaces the list on the task. A task that wants Anthropic and Gemini still binds two of these, unless each entry carries its own provider and secret, and then `Model` is a catalog and we lose the one-credential-per-host benefit. So I see the two as complementary: `Model` holds many models per provider, and the task binds one or more `Model`s.

### Open questions

- Should a task list models explicitly, or bind by label selector so it sees "everything in the atespace I'm allowed to use"?
- Does the list need a role or alias per entry (`default`, `fast`), or is that the runner's business in `spec.config`?
- Task specs are immutable and gateway rules are copied at create time. Is the model list also fixed at create, or does a later `Model` change show up in a running task?
- How does this line up with #475? With several models, each one needs its own egress rule and placeholder key, and two models on the same host with different keys hit the "one credential per host" limit called out there. A provider-shaped `Model` would mostly avoid that.
- If `Model` holds many models per provider, should it be renamed?

### Related

#348, #516, #475, #471, #563, #356

title: ci: skip E2E when only docs or repo settings change
body:
The Kind E2E job (`E2E (Kind / Substrate go.mod)`) runs on every PR and push to `main`, including changes that can't affect it. This adds a `paths-ignore` filter to the `push` and `pull_request` triggers in `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`.

Skipped when a change touches **only**:
- `**.md`, `docs/**`, `assets/**`, `LICENSE`
- agent skills: `skills/**`, `.agents/**`, `.claude/**`, `.gemini/**`
- repo settings: `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `.github/rulesets/**`, `.github/workflows/rulesets.yml`, `hack/apply-rulesets.sh`

A change that also touches any other file still runs E2E. The nightly schedule and `workflow_dispatch` are unchanged, so `main` is still tested daily.

None of the E2E scripts (`hack/*e2e*`), `test/e2e/manifests`, or Dockerfiles read the skipped paths. `examples/**` is intentionally not skipped.

**Required checks:** E2E isn't a required status check (`protect-main.json` only requires `build-and-test`), so a skipped run doesn't block merging. If E2E becomes required (e.g. for the merge queue), this should become a job-level filter, or skipped runs will leave the check pending.

Also updates `skills/substrate/SKILL.md` to note when PR CI skips E2E.

title: server: trace and measure AX RPCs and Substrate calls
body:
ax-server has a tracer provider (#557) but records no RPC spans, so an `ax --trace` command (#562) ends at the CLI, and a slow `CreateTask` or `ResumeTask` shows no breakdown. ax-server now records a server span for each AX RPC and a client span for each Substrate call, using `otelgrpc` stats handlers in `internal/telemetry`.

- The server span joins the caller's `traceparent`. ax-server does not read or send `baggage`. ax-server records only registered AX methods. `otelgrpc` copies the method name from the client into the span name and `rpc.method`. If ax-server recorded unknown methods, a client could make new span names and metric series.
- Reconciles run inside the RPC, so `CreateActor`, `ResumeActor`, and their retries appear as client spans under the AX server span.
- `rpc.server.call.duration` and `rpc.client.call.duration` use buckets 0.005, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, and 60 s. `otelgrpc`'s default buckets stop at 10 s, and a resume can wait for a snapshot restore and the 15 s readiness timeout. Both histograms have three labels, `rpc.system.name`, `rpc.method`, and `rpc.response.status_code`; the view removes the `server.address` and `server.port` labels that `otelgrpc` sets from the peer IP address.
- The handler reads the known methods from the gRPC server on the first RPC, so a service registered later also gets spans.
- The docs explain that `deploy/ax-server.yaml` exports no spans by default, that a sampled `traceparent` forces sampling, that non-OK Substrate codes show as span errors, and that the old `rpc/dup` histograms keep `otelgrpc`'s buckets.

Refs #13, #452.

## Testing

- `go test -race ./...` and `make verify` pass with 0 lint issues; the new tests pass 200 times with `-race`.
- `internal/telemetry/grpc_test.go`:
  - The server span joins a caller's `traceparent`, and the handler sees no `baggage`.
  - A call to an unknown method gets `Unimplemented`, with no span and no metric point.
  - The client span is the parent of the server span, and no `baggage` is sent.
  - Both histograms use the new buckets and carry exactly the three labels.
  - A service registered after the handler is built (the gRPC health service) gets spans.
  - The tests wait for spans and metric points, because gRPC ends the server span after it writes the status.
- `internal/server/telemetry_test.go`: on the h2c path that `ax-server` serves, a sampled caller gets a `ListTasks` server span and an unsampled caller gets none.
- I ran the `ax-server` binary against Postgres, with an unreachable Substrate endpoint, and an OTel Collector 0.140:
  - `ax --trace apply` produced one trace with `ax apply` (CLI), the `CreateTask` client span, the `CreateTask` ax-server span, and 10 `CreateAtespace` Substrate client spans under it, one per retry.
  - `ax --trace get tasks` produced an ax-server `ListTasks` span under the CLI client span.
  - Without `--trace`, ax-server sampled 1 of 5 `ListTasks` calls as new root traces.
  - `/metrics` served both histograms with `le="15"` and `le="60"` buckets.

title: workspace: align v1alpha1 schema, enforce immutability, and materialize spec.setup
body:
Aligns the `v1alpha1` `Workspace` API schema for snapshot-based workspace setup, makes `Workspace` immutable, and materializes `spec.setup` inside the sandbox.

- **API (`pkg/apis/v1alpha1`)**: Add shared `Profile` (`common.proto`), drop `ResourcesSpec.requests`, move build-time steps under `WorkspaceSpec.setup` (`git` with `ref`, `files`, `skills`, `commands`, `gateway`), add `spec.profile` and `WorkspaceStatus`, replace `UpdateWorkspace` with `CreateWorkspace`, and add `limit`/`offset` pagination to `ListWorkspaces`.
- **Validation & Server (`internal/apivalidation`, `internal/server`, `internal/store`)**: Validate `Profile`, `spec.setup`, and gateway references; make `CreateWorkspace` idempotent on identical specs and reject mutations with `FailedPrecondition`; reject unserved gateway bindings with `Unimplemented`.
- **Sandbox Setup (`internal/workspace`)**: Split git operations into `git.go` and execute `spec.setup` in order (`git` branch/tag/SHA checkout -> `files` -> `skills` -> `commands`).
- **CLI & Docs (`cmd/ax`, `docs/manifests.md`, `test/e2e`)**: Extract `cmd/ax/workspace.go` and update CLI commands, docs, examples, and E2E tests for the new schema.

There are some todo that will be handled in following pr after integration with task and gateway. The pr does not do warm snapshot or setup actor yet.

issue: #563

title: runner: trust the egress CA bundle and give git placeholder credentials
body:
Prepare task sandboxes for Gateway egress (part of #549). A task's network access does not change yet.

- Every task's ActorTemplate mounts Substrate's egress trust bundle at `/run/ate/egress-trust-bundle/trust-bundle.pem`.
- The runner points `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` and `GIT_SSL_CAINFO` at it when it exists, unless `spec.env` sets them.
- The runner defaults `GIT_ASKPASS` to `/ax/git-askpass`, a link to itself; started under that name, the program prints a placeholder from `init` and exits, for a Gateway rule to replace.
- It sets no API key variables: a task sets its own placeholders in `spec.env`.

Follow-up: apply the bound Gateway's rules to the task's actor.

title: Add NetworkPolicies for ax-server and Postgres
body:
NetworkPolicies that keep Task code away from AX's own services (part of #549). A Gateway rule can name a host inside the cluster, and ax-server does not authenticate its callers yet (#376).

- `ax-server`: worker pods and the egress gateway cannot connect; other pods and `kubectl port-forward` still can.
- `ax-postgres`: only ax-server can connect, on port 5432.
- The same policies are in `deploy/` and `test/e2e/manifests/`; the `/substrate` skill lists the two Substrate pod labels they match.

Follow-up: E2E that a task cannot reach ax-server through a Gateway rule that names it.

title: feat(lifecycle): prototype task state machine with inline Substrate c…
body: …alls and session lineage

title: feat(workspace): support pre-warmed workspace snapshots
body:
Track the implementation of pre-warmed Workspace snapshots on Substrate tags so Tasks can start from a materialized workspace snapshot instead of running spec.setup cold on every launch.

This covers eager pre-warming via Workspace.spec.profile, lazy snapshot caching when a Task overrides spec.profile (with single-flight coalescing for concurrent tasks), and workspace snapshot lifecycle management (Preparing / Ready / Failed status)

title: gateway: enforce a task's bound Gateway rules
body:
Enforce `Task.spec.gateway` on Substrate (part of #549): a task that binds a Gateway can reach only what its rules allow.

- `CreateTask` requires the bound Gateway to exist (`FailedPrecondition` otherwise) and copies its rules to the task's actor once, while the actor is suspended.
- Later edits to the Gateway, or its deletion, do not change a task that has its rules; a task without a Gateway makes no egress policy call.
- If Substrate refuses a rule, the task is `Failed` with reason `GatewayBindingFailed` and the gateway's name in the message.

Follow-up: Kind E2E with the Kubernetes credential provider.

title: profile, substrate: add Profile template resolution and snapshot Tag client support
body:
Part of #563

Prepares the **Profile** resolution layer and **Substrate snapshot Tag** client primitives for Workspace pre-warming (will wire Workspace controller change in the next PR):

1. **Profile API Semantics & Validation (`pkg/apis/v1alpha1`, `internal/apivalidation`, `docs/manifests.md`)**
   - Enforce and document that `Profile.ate_actor_template` references an existing `ActorTemplate` directly and is mutually exclusive with `image` and `resources`.

2. **Profile Merging, Template Resolution & Tag Naming (`internal/controller`)**
   - `MergeProfile`: overlays Task-level `Profile` overrides onto a Workspace default `Profile` while respecting `ate_actor_template` mutual exclusivity.
   - `ResolveProfileTemplate`: resolves an effective `Profile` into either the user-supplied `ate_actor_template` name or a deterministic `ax-<hash>` `ActorTemplate` spec (incorporating default image/resources, `runnerImage`, and `SNAPSHOT_FIDELITY_ROOTFS`).
   - `WorkspaceTagName`: generates deterministic, collision-free `ws-<prefix>-<wsHash>-<tagHash>` snapshot `Tag` names per `(workspace, template)` pair.

3. **Substrate Snapshot Tag & Actor Client (`internal/substrate`)**
   - Add `EnsureActorTemplate`, `EnsureActorFromTag` (provisioning an `Actor` seeded from `source_tag`), and `CreateTag` / `GetTag` / `ListTags` / `DeleteTag`.
   - Unify Control API RPC retries on `callWithRetry` (`codes.Unavailable` + `codes.Aborted` on lease-contended mutations).
   - Extend `substratetest` with in-memory `Tag` lifecycle and `source_tag` checks for unit tests.

title: task: update v1alpha1 Task and ObjectMeta schema and update codebase
body:
Part of https://github.com/google/ax/issues/563

I left some fields out like `Budget` and `start_time` because they are not necessary for 0.1 and we can add them incrementally. 

This just updates the proto and make existing codes functional with the changes. Task still creates one template per task. 


- Update ObjectMeta in common.proto with uid, labels, owner, update_time, and delete_time.
- Update TaskSpec and TaskStatus in task.proto to match the v1alpha1 API design (profile, commands, goal, retry, session_id; state, status_detail, outcome, attempt, ate_actor_template, generation, resolved_argv, previous_failure), omitting deferred fields and removing deprecated spec.{image,command,resources} and status.{phase,id,worker_ip}.
- Keep TaskStatusReason minimal (UNSPECIFIED, PROVISIONING_FAILED, SANDBOX_CRASHED) and add buf.build/googleapis/googleapis for google/rpc/status.proto.
- Replace field-level MergeProfile with whole-profile EffectiveProfile so Task.spec.profile is used as-is when set and falls back to Workspace.spec.profile only when omitted; document warm vs. cold startup semantics across protos, Go docstrings, and docs/manifests.md.
- Adapt validation, memory/postgres stores, controller, server, runner, claude-code-runner, CLI, E2E harness, examples, and docs end to end.

title: gateway: add Kind E2E for egress rules and credential injection
body:
Add the Kind E2E for `Task.spec.gateway` (part of #549): a task reaches what its Gateway allows, with the credential injected, and nothing else.

- `TestE2E_GatewayEgress` checks that an in-cluster HTTPS echo server receives the labeled Secret's value instead of the task's placeholder.
- It also checks that a credential from an unlabeled Secret, a host without a rule, ax-server (though a rule names it), and a task without a Gateway are refused, and that editing or deleting the Gateway does not affect a running task.
- The E2E setup enables Substrate's Kubernetes credential provider and runs Substrate's own script that lets the egress gateway trust the echo server's CA.

body:

(#8805, #8834, #8836)
  • Treat overflowing OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL and OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_TIMEOUT values as invalid in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric. (#8800)
  • Prevent a panic in NewFixedSizeReservoir and FixedSizeReservoirProvider when given a negative size in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric/exemplar; negative sizes are now clamped to zero, consistent with a size of zero. (#8832)
  • Preserve exponential histogram ZeroThreshold during OTLP metric export in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric. (#8801)
  • Ensure metric helpers in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.32.0, go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.33.0, and go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.34.0 record measurements only once when no attributes are provided. (#8849)
  • Treat empty OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER and OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG values as unset in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace. (#8873)
  • Normalize global OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT path joining in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploghttp so trailing-slash base URLs do not produce double-slash log export paths. (#8864)
  • Prevent a deadlock when formatting an error passed to RecordError calls back into the span in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace. (#8815)
  • Prevent SimpleSpanProcessor.Shutdown from panicking when constructed with a nil exporter in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace. (#8844)
  • Propagate invalid exponential histogram scale errors to Prometheus exporter self-observability metrics in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/prometheus. (#8839)

  • go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log

See our versioning policy for more information about these stability guarantees.

Added

  • Add String method for KeyValue type in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute. (#8205)
  • Add String method for Set type in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute. (#8347)
  • Add WithMaxExportBatchSize to go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric to configure the maximum export batch size for PeriodicReader. (#8960)
  • Add WithAttributeValueDepthLimit, DefaultAttributeValueDepthLimit, and SpanLimits.AttributeValueDepthLimit in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace to configure the maximum depth of span, event, link, and instrumentation scope attribute values. (#8938)
  • Add WithAttributeValueDepthLimit in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log to configure the maximum depth of log record and instrumentation scope attribute values. (#8938)
  • Add WithMaxResponseSize to go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp, go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp, and go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploghttp. (#8941)
  • Add experimental ProbabilitySampler in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace/x that conforms to the OpenTelemetry specification's threshold-based sampling algorithm. (#8123)
  • Add experimental *Binder extension interfaces in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric/x for instruments that support binding attributes ahead of time. (#8760)
  • Add the experimental Finisher synchronous metric instrument extension interface to go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric/x. (#8906)

Changed

  • Use the OpenTelemetry Attribute Collection representation for non-OTLP protocols for metric data diffs in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric/metricdata/metricdatatest. (#8993)
  • Apply a maximum depth of 64 by default to span, event, link, log record, and instrumentation scope attribute values in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace and go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log. (#8938)
  • Reduce allocations when applying attribute value length limits in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace and go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log by rebuilding composite values only when truncation is needed. (#8912)
  • Decode traceparent using a hex lookup table in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/propagation, which rejects the specification-disallowed upper-case characters without a separate scan of the header. (#8739)
  • Decode all characters at constant indices in TraceIDFromHex and SpanIDFromHex in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace to eliminate bounds checks. (#8740)

Fixed

  • Count valid U+FFFD replacement characters toward attribute value length limits in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace, go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace, and go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log.
  • Truncate string attribute values to empty strings when the configured length limit is zero, including malformed UTF-8, in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace, go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace, and go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log. (#9054)
  • Fix a data race in NewPeriodicReader where r.inst was assigned after the background goroutine was launched in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric. (#9028)
  • Prevent precision loss for large int64 values in Sum, Histogram, and ExponentialHistogram aggregations in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric. (#8981)

(#8805, #8834, #8836)
  • Treat overflowing OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL and OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_TIMEOUT values as invalid in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric. (#8800)
  • Prevent a panic in NewFixedSizeReservoir and FixedSizeReservoirProvider when given a negative size in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric/exemplar; negative sizes are now clamped to zero, consistent with a size of zero. (#8832)
