title: Support running a follow-up turn on the same task workspace (session reuse)
body:
Follow-up from #643 (Step 3 of `hack/hero-demo/run.sh`).

### Problem
Today each `Task` gets its own Substrate `Actor` and its own `/workspace` durable volume. As a result, creating a second `Task` with the same `spec.sessionId` cannot see edits made in Turn 1 or any persisted session state stored under `/workspace/.ax/sessions/<sessionId>` (as implemented for Antigravity in agentexecutor/images#25).

Because of this, `hack/hero-demo/run.sh` currently runs Turn 1 and verifies suspend/resume persistence, while leaving the second turn stubbed (`STUB`) in Step 3.

### Goal
Support running a follow-up turn on the same task's workspace (reusing the same `sessionId` and persisted session state), and wire Turn 2 into `hack/hero-demo/run.sh` Step 3 once supported:

- Allow a follow-up goal/turn to execute against the same task workspace and session state (including updating turn-completion tracking so a new goal runs rather than being skipped by Turn 1's `/workspace/.ax/launcher-done` marker).
- Preserve workspace edits and session state under `/workspace` across turns and across suspend/resume.
- Replace the Turn 2 `mark_stub` in `hack/hero-demo/run.sh` (and update `hack/hero-demo/README.md`) with an end-to-end Turn 2 check verifying both workspace continuity and session reuse.

title: Restrict profile.ateTemplate references to the task's own atespace
body:
Follow-up from #639.

Today `spec.profile.ateTemplate` accepts cross-atespace references (`atespace` different from the task's/workspace's atespace). Until cross-atespace template sharing is settled on the Substrate side, restrict `profile.ateTemplate.atespace` to match the resource's own atespace (or be omitted).

title: ax-server, e2e: enable workspace pre-warming by default and add shared custom-image E2E
body:
## Summary
Enables workspace snapshot pre-warming by default in `ax-server` and adds end-to-end coverage for workspace pre-warming, explicit suspend/resume, completion, and running a plain custom container image against a shared workspace.

## Key Changes
- **`cmd/ax-server/main.go`:** Always wire `SetupCoordinator: runnerSrv` into `WorkspaceManager` when `--runner-addr` is enabled, removing the `--enable-prewarm` / `AX_ENABLE_PREWARM` gate.
- **`test/e2e/launcher_test.go`:** Add `TestE2E_PrewarmAndCustomImageSharedWorkspace` covering:
  1. Applying a `Workspace` with `setup.files` + `setup.commands` and verifying it pre-warms to `Ready`.
  2. Running Task 1 against the pre-warmed workspace to `COMPLETED` with `Outcome.Output`.
  3. Running Task 2 with a plain custom image (`AX_E2E_LAUNCHER_IMAGE`, runner mounted read-only) on the same workspace through `QUEUED → WORKING → SUSPENDED → WORKING → COMPLETED`, preserving `/workspace` across explicit suspend/resume.

## Testing
- `go test ./cmd/ax-server/...`
- `go test -c -o /dev/null ./test/e2e/...`
- Kind E2E suite (running in PR CI)

title: Raise default sandbox memory limit from 512Mi (Antigravity needs 4Gi)
body:
### Problem
When a `Task` omits `spec.profile.resources.limits.memory`, `internal/substrate/client.go` defaults `DefaultMemoryBytes` to `512 << 20` (`512Mi`, also documented in `docs/manifests.md`).

Dogfooding showed `512Mi` is too small for the Antigravity agent image, requiring a bump to `4Gi` to run cleanly.

### Current Mitigations
- `hack/hero-demo/task-starter.yaml` explicitly sets `cpu: "2"` and `memory: "4Gi"`.
- `agentexecutor/studio` starter agent presets also default to `4096Mi`.

Anyone authoring a raw `Task` YAML without `spec.profile.resources.limits` still hits the `512Mi` server fallback.

### Follow-up for Bug Bash
Decide whether to:
1. Raise `DefaultMemoryBytes` in `internal/substrate/client.go` (and `internal/apivalidation/common.go` / `docs/manifests.md`) so starter agent images work out of the box without explicit limits, or
2. Keep `512Mi` as the minimal container fallback and document/surface clear sizing guidance (`4Gi`) for agent images in `docs/manifests.md` and examples.

title: ax ssh can hang and leave the local shell stuck until processes are killed
body:
### Problem
During dogfooding against a `spec.debug: true` Antigravity task sandbox, `ax ssh` hung and left the local shell stuck, requiring manual process termination to recover.

*(Non-blocking for non-debug `Task` goal execution, since interactive `ax ssh` is optional.)*

### Context
- `runSSH` in `cmd/ax/main.go` wires `os.Stdin` and a double `Ctrl-C` interrupt handler (`escalateInterrupts`) into `guestClient.Exec`.
- Interactive PTY support and the `ax exec` rename are tracked separately in #374 and #492.
- Even with the double `Ctrl-C` escape in place, a hung `ax ssh` session was still able to wedge the caller's shell.

### Follow-up for Bug Bash
- Reproduce the hang against a running Antigravity sandbox (`ax ssh <task>` vs `ax ssh <task> -- <cmd>`).
- Verify whether local tunnel/port-forward (`dialRouterTLS` / `tunnel.PortForward`), gRPC stream teardown, or missing PTY raw-mode/EOF handling leaves `ax ssh` or child processes wedged, and ensure interrupts/cleanup release the terminal cleanly.

Related: #374, #492

title: Fix/friction log local install
body:
## TLDR:
1. Print detailed pod error instead of just general "error:timed out waiting for condition"
2. Preflight check the egress by sending a request to `https://ghcr.io/v2/`
3. Improve ax version output
4. Improve the agent prompt for setting ax up.

## Issues:

1. On a clean machine, `ax local start` can wait several minutes and then fail
with only `error: timed out waiting for the condition`. Two cases we hit:
  - The cluster cannot pull an image (a private `--server-image`, for example).
  - Containers on the host have no outbound network (IPv4 forwarding off), so
    every pull from ghcr.io times out.
In both, the reason was in the pod status the whole time, and `ax` did not
  read it. 
2. A source build also printed `ax version dev`, so a report could not
say which commit it came from.

## What changes

**Rollout status** (`internal/install/executil/rollout.go`)

`ax local start` and `ax install` waited with `kubectl rollout status
--timeout`. `executil.WaitRollout` runs the same wait in 15 s slices and reads
the workload's pods between them. It prints what they are waiting for when it
changes, and a timeout error ends with the last status:

    ==> Deploying ax-server (...)...
        ax-system/deployment/ax-server is not ready: pod ax-server-..., container ax-server: ImagePullBackOff: Back-off pulling image "...": ... 403 Forbidden
    Error: waiting for ax-system/deployment/ax-server rollout: timed out after 3m0s: pod ax-server-..., container ax-server: ImagePullBackOff: ...

The status is Kubernetes' own reason and message. `WaitRollout` does not
interpret it and never ends the wait early, so it does not depend on kubelet
wording. A rollout that finishes within a slice prints nothing.

**Egress warning** (`internal/install/cluster/kind.go`)

After the Kind node is ready, `KindProvider.Up` requests `https://ghcr.io/v2/`
from inside the node. If that fails it prints a warning, and names IPv4
forwarding when Docker reports it off. The existing host checks cannot see
this, because the host has network access and its containers do not. It is a
warning, not an error: a cluster that uses a registry mirror still works.

**`ax version`** (`internal/version`)

A build that is not a release prints `dev+<12 hex digits>`, with `-dirty` for
a modified checkout, from the VCS information the Go toolchain records.
Release builds are unchanged. A build without VCS information still prints
`dev`.

**Docs** (`docs/local_installer.md`)

- The agent setup prompt links the guide by URL, runs `~/.ax/bin/ax version`
  to verify the install, and stops on a failed step.
- A local cluster pulls every image anonymously, so images must be public.
- Describes the egress check and the rollout output above.

title: api: paginate list RPCs with page tokens
body:
Paginate the four List RPCs with `page_size`, `page_token` and `next_page_token` instead of `limit` and `offset` ([AIP-158](https://google.aip.dev/158), item 3 of https://github.com/google/ax/issues/563#issuecomment-6987373482).

- `ax get` follows the tokens and prints every row; it used to stop at 50 tasks or workspaces.
- A page holds 50 by default and at most 1000; the token wraps an offset, so the stores are unchanged and a write between two pages can repeat or skip a row.
- An older `ax` against the new server lists the first 50 of each kind, which is new for gateways and models.

Follow-up: page by key in the stores, as Agent Substrate does.

title: Support managed agents (Gemini, Claude)
body:
Track support for vendor managed agents: the Gemini API's Antigravity agent and Claude Managed Agents. The agent loop stays with the vendor and its tool calls run in a sandbox on AX (Gemini calls this a self-hosted environment, Claude a self-hosted sandbox), so images no longer need an agent CLI (`agy`, `claude`) or an `ax-harness` script.



The design is not settled yet. To resolve first:

- [ ] WebSocket egress: the Gemini worker connects over WebSocket, which Substrate v1.0.0 only carries under `tlsPassthrough` rules (agent-substrate/substrate#3885, planned for v1.1).
- [ ] A task runs once and is then finished, but an agent conversation has many turns (#649).
- [ ] Where the vendor API key lives and what talks to the vendor.

Only `README.md` is changed. Not touched here, and possibly worth a follow-up:

title: fix(server): ignore client-supplied uid, timestamps and status
body:
Ignore the `metadata.uid`, timestamps and `status` a client sends on create and update; the server assigns them ([AIP-203](https://google.aip.dev/203), item 1 of https://github.com/google/ax/issues/563#issuecomment-6987373482).

- `CreateTask` kept them, so a manifest copied from `ax get` created a task with the source's uid, and `ax promote` to that target failed with "source and target must differ".
- Workspace, Gateway and Model already ignored a client `uid`; they now ignore the timestamps too and get an `updateTime`.
- The proto comments mark these fields as ignored on input, as Agent Substrate does; `metadata.owner` is unchanged.

title: Zero-flag ax local / Studio UX when DefaultServerImage and DefaultRunnerVolumeImage are unset
body:
Today `internal/install/axdeploy/deploy.go` leaves `DefaultServerImage = ""` and `DefaultRunnerVolumeImage = ""`, so `ResolveImageInputs` errors immediately unless `--server-image` / `$AX_SERVER_IMAGE` is set explicitly. Downstream UI setup (AX Studio) likewise blocks setup until `AX_SERVER_IMAGE` is provided in the UI or environment.

For `v0.4.0-rc.1`, we are keeping image refs explicit to avoid release-branch churn while `ax-runner-volume` rollout (`#625`) settles. Ahead of wider public usage, decide during bug-bash triage between:

1. **Populating release defaults on tagged binaries:** `internal/version/version.go` already exposes `version.IsRelease()` and `version.Image(name)`, which can default `ax-server` (and `ax-runner-volume` once enabled by default) on release builds while still keeping local `dev` builds explicit.
2. **Keeping explicit image configuration with clear copy-paste UX:** Ensure `install.sh` / quickstart docs and release notes prominently surface ready-to-export `AX_SERVER_IMAGE` and `AX_RUNNER_VOLUME_IMAGE` commands and give a clearer prompt in `ax local` / `ax install`.

title: fix(promote): handle a finished task and a workspace's setup gateway
body:
Two fixes to `ax promote`, for cases that did not exist when it was written (#618).

- **Setup Gateway:** ax-server rejected `spec.setup.gateway` until workspace pre-warming was on by default (#651, #663), so promote had only the Task's Gateway to copy. A Workspace can now name one, and the target cannot create the Workspace without it, so promote copies it first, the same way as the Task's Gateway, when the target has to create the Workspace.
- **Finished task:** since #639 a task ends when its command exits, and the source refuses to suspend it, which made `--suspend-source` fail. Such a task is no longer suspended.

title: Emit ax.task.state_changed after committed task writes
body:
Emit `ax.task.state_changed` after each task write that changes the task's phase, so task timelines and cost attribution can join AX tasks with Agent Substrate's `ate.actor.*` events.

Part of #675. Main has no task outcome or exit code now (#707, #756), so the event does not carry them. Related to #13 and #471.

- The task write helpers return a `taskWrite` (phase before and after, write time). Each handler passes the phase that it read under the per-task lock, so a write needs no extra read.
- The caller emits through the new `telemetry.EmitAt`. `CreateTask` and `clearStoredTaskState` emit after `applyActor`, so `Provisioned` gets `ate.actor.uid` with no extra Substrate call.
- Attributes: `ax.task.name`, `ate.atespace`, `ax.task.id`, `ax.task.phase`, `ax.task.previous_phase`, and `ate.actor.uid` (`Provisioned` only).
- Phases: `Provisioned` (the first phase, because #761 stores a task only after its actor exists), `Queued` (after a transient `ResumeTask` error), `Terminating`, `Deleted`. `docs/observability.md` explains each one.
- `substratetest` gets a `GetActor` error and a `GetActor` hook for the tests.

### Validation

`make verify`, `go build`, `go test ./...` (27 packages), and `go test -race` for `internal/server`, `internal/substrate`, and `internal/telemetry`. The tests cover each phase change, failed creates, failed store writes, an unreadable actor, and the write-time timestamp.

Written with help from an AI coding assistant.

title: install: serve localhost registry images to the local cluster
body:
## Problem

`ax local start` cannot start `ax-server` from an image on a `localhost` registry. Before release images exist, that is the only registry a developer has without an external one. The symptom is the one in #648: `ax-server` stays `Pending`, and `ax get tasks` fails with `pod is not running. Current status=Pending`.

### Reproduce

On `main` at de7de90, Linux, Docker 29.8, kind v0.33:

```bash
docker run -d -p 127.0.0.1:5001:5000 --name kind-registry registry:2
make images AX_IMAGE_REPO=localhost:5001 CONTAINER_CLI=docker
export AX_SERVER_IMAGE=localhost:5001/ax-server@$(cat bin/ax-server.digest)
export AX_DEFAULT_TASK_IMAGE=localhost:5001/ax-task-runner@$(cat bin/ax-task-runner.digest)
ax local start
```

It fails after 4 min 46 s. These commands were run before #647 removed the default task image; on current `main`, omit the `AX_DEFAULT_TASK_IMAGE` line. On `main` at 465cbeb, the smoke test that this PR adds runs the same steps and fails in the same way after 5 min. Since #655 the wait shows the reason:

```text
==> Deploying ax-server (localhost:5001/ax-server@sha256:2672...)...
    ax-system/deployment/ax-server is not ready: pod ax-server-7df867bf6-m57vs, container ax-server: ImagePullBackOff: Back-off pulling image "localhost:5001/ax-server@sha256:2672...": ErrImagePull: ... Head "https://localhost:5001/v2/ax-server/manifests/sha256:2672...": dial tcp [::1]:5001: connect: connection refused
Error: waiting for ax-system/deployment/ax-server rollout: timed out after 3m0s: pod ax-server-7df867bf6-m57vs, container ax-server: ImagePullBackOff: ...
```

During the wait, in a second terminal (seen on 212bf13, not run again on de7de90):

```text
$ ax get tasks
Error: kubectl port-forward exited for context "ax-local": error: unable to forward port because pod is not running. Current status=Pending
```

## Cause

In the Kind node, `localhost:5001` is the node itself, and no registry listens there. The host resolves the digest without error, because the registry is on the host's `localhost`.

The Agent Substrate manifests that `ax` embeds are Substrate's kind overlay. In them atelet has `--localhost-registry-replacement=kind-registry:5000`, so actor images on a loopback registry come from a container named `kind-registry`. Substrate's `hack/create-kind-cluster.sh` creates that container, connects it to the `kind` network, and writes `/etc/containerd/certs.d/localhost:<port>/hosts.toml` on each node. `ax local start` creates the cluster in Go and does not do the last two steps. So the node cannot pull pod images from `localhost`, and `ax-server` is the first one. atelet can reach `kind-registry` only when the container is already on that network.

## Change

- `ax local start` reads the registry that serves `localhost` images from the embedded Substrate manifests: `installsubstrate.LocalRegistryEndpoint` returns the value of atelet's `--localhost-registry-replacement`. It gives that endpoint and the image references of the install to the Kind provider (`UpOptions.LocalRegistry`, `UpOptions.Images`). No Go file names the registry.
- For the references on `localhost` or a loopback address, `KindProvider.Up`:
  - checks, before it creates a cluster, that the container that the endpoint names is running, and stops with the command to start it when it is not;
  - connects that container to the network of the nodes;
  - writes `certs.d/<registry>/hosts.toml` on each node, with the endpoint as the host.

  It does not create the registry, because the images must already be in it.
- Test: `make test-local-install` (`hack/test-local-install.sh`) builds the images into a registry on `localhost`, runs `ax local start` with them, and runs a task from a locally built image. No test ran `ax local start` on a cluster before: E2E installs AX with Substrate's own tools. CI runs it as the job `local-install` in `e2e.yml`, with the triggers of E2E. It is not a required check.
- Docs: a "Using Locally Built Images" section in `docs/local_installer.md`, a pointer to it in the README, the new test in `docs/development.md` and `AGENTS.md`, and a row in the address table of the Substrate skill.

The registry container must still have the name and port of Substrate's kind overlay (`kind-registry`, `5000`). The guide gives the command.

## Result

With this change, rebased on `main` at 465cbeb, `ax local start --server-image "$AX_SERVER_IMAGE"` gives:

```text
==> Creating Kind cluster "ax-local" (kindest/node:v1.36.1@sha256:3489...)...
==> Serving images on localhost:5001 from the "kind-registry" container...
==> Installing Agent Substrate v1.0.0 (local profile)...
...
==> AX is ready in namespace "ax-system".

Local environment "ax-local" is ready (active context: ax-local).
```

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| New cluster, registry container not connected to the `kind` network | Ready in 1 min 50 s |
| The task of Step 4 of the guide, with `spec.profile.image` on `localhost:5001` | Resumed in 3 s, `ax ssh` ran in the gVisor sandbox, `/workspace` survived suspend and resume |
| `kind-registry` container stopped | Error in 0.1 s, no cluster created |
| Second run on a healthy cluster | Deployment generation and pod unchanged, 4 s |
| `make test-local-install` with this change | Passes: 2 min 14 s on a workstation, 4 min 23 s as the CI job |
| The same script on `main` at 465cbeb, without this change | Fails after 5 min with the `ImagePullBackOff` reason, exit code 1 |

`make verify`, `go build` of the three binaries, and `go test ./...` pass.

Not verified: Podman as the cluster engine, and macOS. A server image on a remote registry was not run on a cluster; the unit tests cover that no registry is configured for it.

## Not in this PR

A run after a failed run can still fail at once. The `ax-server` Deployment has the default `progressDeadlineSeconds` of 600. After that time, `kubectl rollout status` returns an error immediately, and `kubectl apply` of the unchanged manifest starts no new rollout. An earlier revision of this PR restarted the Deployment in that state. This revision does not.

Measured with the registry code of this PR, before the rebase on #647, on the failed cluster of the reproduction, 10 minutes after the Deployment was created:

1. `ax local start` serves the registry to the cluster, then fails in 4 s with `deployment "ax-server" exceeded its progress deadline`.
2. The kubelet retried the pull 59 s later, and the same pod started. The back-off between retries can be up to 5 minutes.
3. The next `ax local start` is ready in 4 s.

Updates #648. The reproduction gives the error text of that issue, but the report does not show which image was used, so this is possibly not its cause. #655 covers images in a private registry and hosts without egress.

title: fix(controller): let a task recreated under the same name start
body:
A task that is deleted and created again under the same name (`ax delete` then `ax apply`, or `ax promote --replace`) could not start for up to 200 seconds: it stayed in `Working` and its command never ran.

- **Cause:** Substrate's egress gateway reuses an actor's JWT by actor name (agent-substrate/substrate#2208), so the new actor got the old actor's JWT, which ax-server refuses.
- **Fix:** each task's runner egress rule asks for an extra audience that is unique to its policy, so the gateway mints a JWT for the new actor. ax-server still checks only `ax-runner`.
- **What remains:** about 10 seconds, until the gateway reads the new policy. On Kind a recreated task started after 11 seconds instead of 200.

Follow-up: drop the extra audience once agent-substrate/substrate#2208 is fixed; the code has a TODO.

title: docs: add AX Studio to the README and the local installer guide
body: Describe ax studio in the local installer guide (Step 2b), how install.sh decides whether to install ax-studio, and installing ax and ax-studio from source. Link AX Studio from the README.

title: api, controller, server: add ForkTask RPC to branch from a parked task's snapshot
body:
Part 1 of #649 (followed by CLI, E2E, and hero-demo wiring in the stacked PR).

Adds the `ForkTask` gRPC method so callers can start a follow-up turn branched from a parked (`SUSPENDED`, `IDLE`, `COMPLETED`, or `FAILED`) task's durable workspace snapshot without mutating or reopening a terminal task:

- **API (`pkg/apis/v1alpha1/`):**
  - Adds `rpc ForkTask(ForkTaskRequest) returns (Task)` to `service AX`, with `ForkTaskRequest` (`atespace`, `source_task`, `name`, `labels`, `overrides`) and `ForkOverrides` (`commands`, `env`, `goal`, `config`, `session_id`).
  - Adds `parent_task` and `parent_tag` on `TaskStatus` to record lineage and track the snapshot tag owned by the fork.
- **Controller (`internal/controller/reconciler.go`):**
  - Adds `ForkTagName`, `CreateForkTag` (calls `SuspendActorAndWaitForSnapshot` before `CreateTag` so asynchronously parked actors have a completed durable snapshot), and `DeleteForkTag`.
  - Reuses the parent's recorded `ActorTemplate` and seeds the forked actor from `status.parent_tag` via `EnsureActorFromTag`, marking `WorkspaceReady=True`.
  - Cleans up `status.parent_tag` on `DeleteTask` after the forked actor is deleted.
- **Server (`internal/server/fork.go`):**
  - Validates the request, locks the source task while snapshotting, inherits `profile`, `workspace`, `gateway`, `debug`, `env`, and `session_id` (unless overridden), merges `env` and `labels` overrides, creates the forked task suspended, and cleans up the tag on target creation race.
- **Tests:** Adds controller and server unit tests (`internal/controller/fork_test.go`, `internal/server/fork_test.go`) and updates `pkg/apis/v1alpha1/types_test.go`.

Verified:
- `make verify` (`buf format`, `buf lint`, `buf generate`, `go mod tidy`, `go fmt`, `golangci-lint`: 0 issues).
- `go test ./...` passes.

title: cli, e2e, hero-demo: add ax fork task and wire Step 3 Turn 2 session reuse
body:
Part 2 of #649 (stacked on the `ForkTask` API/server PR).

Adds the `ax fork` CLI command, Kind E2E coverage for multi-turn snapshot forking, and Step 3 Turn 2 session reuse in `hack/hero-demo/`:

- **CLI (`cmd/ax/fork.go`, `cmd/ax/main.go`, `cmd/ax/task.go`):**
  - Adds `ax fork task <source-task> <new-task> [--goal] [--session-id] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--label KEY=VALUE] [--no-resume] [-- command...]`, creating the forked task and resuming it by default unless `--no-resume` is set.
  - Prints `Parent Task` in `ax describe task` when populated.
  - Adds unit tests in `cmd/ax/fork_test.go`.
- **E2E (`test/e2e/launcher/ax-harness`, `test/e2e/launcher_test.go`):**

title: hack/hero-demo: redirect stdin from /dev/null in wait_for_file
body:
## Summary
- Redirect stdin from `/dev/null` on the `ax ssh` poll inside `wait_for_file` in `hack/hero-demo/run.sh`.

## Why
When `./hack/hero-demo/run.sh` runs in an interactive terminal, `wait_for_file` runs `AX_TIMEOUT=10 run_ax ssh ...`. GNU `timeout` puts `ax ssh` in a background process group, and `ax ssh` (`Stdin: os.Stdin` in `cmd/ax/main.go`) reads from stdin. Reading from the controlling terminal in a background process group raises `SIGTTIN`, putting `ax ssh` into stopped state (`T`) with `SIGTERM` pending and leaving its child `kubectl port-forward` open indefinitely.

## Verification
- `bash -n hack/hero-demo/run.sh` (exit 0)
- `./hack/hero-demo/run.sh` dry-run (exit 0)
- Controlling-PTY regression test (`pty.openpty()` + `TIOCSCTTY`) with mock `ax` reading stdin (`cat >/dev/null`):
  - Before fix: blocked until 1.5s watchdog kill (`rc=-9`)
  - With `</dev/null`: completed cleanly (`rc=0`, `0.02s`)

title: Emit ax.task.state_changed events for task debugging and Substrate timeline correlation
body:
### Problem

`ax describe` only tells you what a task is doing right now, and once a task is deleted it is just `NotFound`. RPC traces do not fill that gap: they are off by default, sampled at 10% when enabled, and cover gRPC calls only, not runner outcome callbacks or state diffs.

Agent Substrate solves this for actors with `ate.actor.state_changed` and `ate.actor.crashed` events, which go to stdout even without a collector. AX has nothing like that for tasks, so two things are missing when debugging:

1. Why a task stopped: when a command finishes or fails, AX suspends the actor and logs nothing. To Substrate that looks just like `ax suspend`, and once the task is deleted, its outcome and exit code are gone.
2. Task states Substrate does not see: Substrate only tracks the actor, not AX states like `Queued`, `Terminating`, or `Deleted`.

Mapping `ax.task.id` onto Substrate events can live on the Substrate side once immutable actor labels in agent-substrate/substrate#3208 propagate to `ate.actor.*`. Even with that, Substrate still does not know command outcomes or AX-only phases.

### Example

Say a task gets created, resumed, suspended, and resumed again, then gets stuck and someone deletes it. If you join `ax.task.state_changed` with Substrate's `ate.actor.state_changed` on `ate.actor.uid`, one query gives you the whole story:

```text
18:24:14.168Z  ax.task.state_changed   task=t5-fail  none -> Queued                gen=1
18:24:14.358Z  ax.task.state_changed   task=t5-fail  Queued -> Provisioned         gen=2   ate.actor.uid=dbafc5d7...
18:24:14-28    ate.actor.state_changed actor=dbafc5d7... suspended -> resuming -> running -> suspending -> suspended -> resuming -> running
18:28:42.476Z  ax.task.state_changed   task=t5-fail  Provisioned -> Terminating    gen=9   ate.actor.uid=dbafc5d7...
18:28:42.49xZ  ate.actor.state_changed actor=dbafc5d7... deleting -> deleted
18:28:42.710Z  ax.task.state_changed   task=t5-fail  Terminating -> Deleted        gen=10  ate.actor.uid=dbafc5d7...
```

You can tell right away that Substrate ran the actor fine without crashing, `ax-server` got no outcome back before the delete, and `dbafc5d7...` stays tied to this task ID even after the task is gone.

### Proposal

Emit `ax.task.state_changed` (OTLP logs, with stdout JSON as a fallback) whenever a task write commits and changes phase, outcome, or `ate.actor.uid`:

- Only track AX-owned states (`Queued`, `Provisioned`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Cancelled`, `Terminating`, `Deleted`). Live actor states (`Working`, `Suspended`, `Crashed`) stay in `ate.actor.state_changed`.
- Use the commit time as the event timestamp, and include `ax.task.generation`, `ax.task.id`, `ate.actor.uid`, `ax.task.phase`, `ax.task.previous_phase`, `ax.task.outcome`, `ax.task.previous_outcome`, and `ax.task.exit_code`.
- Emit after the write commits, best effort. Failed or no-op writes emit nothing, and telemetry errors do not break task writes.

Related: #13, draft PR in #665.

title: hack: use the ax-runner image in the local install smoke test
body:
## Problem

The job `Local install (ax local start)` fails on `main` since #666 merged: https://github.com/google/ax/actions/runs/44842538569/job/136654239973

```text
==> Building ax and the AX images into localhost:5001...
cat: /home/runner/work/ax/ax/bin/ax-task-runner.digest: No such file or directory
make: *** [Makefile:221: test-local-install] Error 1
```

The guide has the same command in "Using Locally Built Images" (`docs/local_installer.md`), so that step fails for a user too.

## Cause

#677 renamed `ax-task-runner` to `ax-runner`. Since then `make images` pushes `ax-runner` and writes `bin/ax-runner.digest`. `hack/test-local-install.sh`, which #666 added, reads `bin/ax-task-runner.digest`.

Neither PR saw the other:

- The last CI run of #666 was on a base before #677.
- #677 merged at 23:50 UTC, when the script was not on `main`, so the rename could not include it.
- #666 merged at 00:14 UTC without a textual conflict.

## Change

- `hack/test-local-install.sh`: use the `ax-runner` image and `bin/ax-runner.digest`, and clear `AX_RUNNER_IMAGE` (the new name of the Makefile variable).
- `docs/local_installer.md`: the same name in the `AX_TASK_IMAGE` line of "Using Locally Built Images".
- `internal/install/cluster/kind_test.go`: the new name in two sample image references. The test does not depend on the name.
- `hack/test-local-install.sh`: when the script fails before `ax local start` creates a cluster, it no longer prints the state of a cluster. In the failed job, that part was only `kubectl` connection errors to `localhost:8080`.

## Result

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `make test-local-install` on `main` at 7d3ba98 | Fails with the `cat` error above |
| `make test-local-install` with this change | Passes in 2 min 14 s; the task runs from `localhost:5001/ax-runner@sha256:...` |
| A failure before the cluster exists (a registry image that does not exist) | Prints the `docker` error only |

`make verify`, `go build` of the three binaries, and `go test ./...` pass.

Not run again: a failure after the cluster exists. `ax local start` sets the kubeconfig context that the new condition tests, so that case still prints the state of the cluster.

A merge queue (#571, #575) tests each PR on the `main` it merges into, and so finds this kind of break before the merge.

title: lifecycle: never assume tasks resume with memory
body:
AX should never assume that a suspended task resumes with its memory intact. Every resume should be treated as a cold start: the sandbox comes back with the filesystem state the snapshot captured (rootfs/volumes), and with no processes, no in-memory runner state, and nothing written outside the snapshotted paths.

## Why

AX does not create memory-fidelity templates today, and Substrate does not guarantee them either:

- Profile templates use `SNAPSHOT_FIDELITY_ROOTFS` (`internal/controller/profile.go:68`). Nothing changes that default, and every task template comes from `ensureProfileTemplate` (`internal/controller/reconciler.go:202`).
- `BuildActorTemplate` uses `SNAPSHOT_FIDELITY_VOLUMES` (`internal/substrate/client.go:377`).
- `SNAPSHOT_FIDELITY_MEMORY` is a *preferred* fidelity, so a memory restore is not guaranteed even when a template requests it.

All the same, parts of the lifecycle, the runner protocol and the docs still branch on memory restore or imply it.

## Where memory is assumed or implied

Code paths:
- `TaskReconciler.IsMemoryFidelityTemplate` (`internal/controller/reconciler.go:264`) is called from `SuspendTask` (`internal/server/server.go:436,486`). When it returns true, the server keeps `ActiveRunID` across suspend, expecting the same process to keep running after resume.
- `ASSIGNMENT_MODE_RESUME` and `ClaimAssignmentRequest.in_memory_run_id` (`pkg/apis/v1alpha1/runner/runner.proto:34,44`) exist only for "the live child process restored from a MEMORY snapshot". They are handled in `runner/pull.go:278` and `internal/lifecycle/lifecycle.go:207-219`.
- `lifecycle.go:216-218` reads a non-empty `in_memory_run_id` as "the runner process survived", which changes how crash detection works (`restartedSameRun`).

Only the fake memory-fidelity templates in `internal/server/server_test.go` (~1906, ~1943) exercise these paths. Production never does.

Docs and comments:
- `pkg/apis/v1alpha1/workspace.proto:69`: setup results are "persisted on disk/memory in the workspace snapshot".
- `README.md:165`, `DESIGN.md:49`, `cmd/ax/main.go:276`: "checkpoint actor state". This is vague; `docs/local_installer.md:279` states it accurately as a checkpoint of `/workspace`.
- `docs/roadmap.md:23`: forking tasks "including its checkpointed memory".

## Proposal

- Make "resume is a cold start" an explicit invariant in `DESIGN.md` and `docs/concepts.md`. After resume, the runner re-claims and starts a new run (or goes idle), and all state it needs must come from ax-server or the snapshotted filesystem.
- Remove the memory-restore special cases: `IsMemoryFidelityTemplate`, the `!memoryFidelity` branch in `SuspendTask` (always clear run state), `ASSIGNMENT_MODE_RESUME`, and the `in_memory_run_id` handling in `lifecycle.go` and `runner/pull.go`. Also delete the matching memory-fidelity tests. Proto fields are internal (`ax.runner.v1alpha1`), so they can be removed or reserved.
- Fix the wording in `workspace.proto`, `README.md`, `DESIGN.md` and `ax --help` so they say the filesystem (or `/workspace`) is checkpointed, not "actor state" or memory.
- If memory snapshots are ever added on purpose, treat them as an optimization behind the cold-start path. Correctness must never depend on them.

title: telemetry: move internal/axattr to internal/telemetry/attr

\`internal/axattr\` names the OpenTelemetry attributes AX puts on its spans, logs, and events (\`ax.task.*\`, and Substrate's \`ate.*\` for actor identity). It is part of ax-server's telemetry, so it belongs next to \`internal/telemetry\` and \`internal/telemetry/otelenv\` rather than at the top of \`internal/\`.

title: runnerhttp: move internal/runnerhttp under runner/runnerhttp

\`internal/runnerhttp\` holds the runner HTTP protocol (the :8081 handler, paths such as \`assignment:claim\` and events, and the runner token header) that only exists to serve \`ax-runner\`. It lives as a top-level internal package, separate from the runner it serves, and the runner imports it for its path and header constants.

Move it to \`runner/runnerhttp\` so the runner protocol sits next to the runner package, and update the imports in \`cmd/ax-server\`, \`internal/server\`, the runner, and \`AGENTS.md\`'s layout.

title: runner: go back to the push runner
body:
This PR restores the push runner from [241bc4d](https://github.com/google/ax/tree/241bc4d0c682a6898da5f718a9ec84fe7c9197f9/runner) while keeping the later work that doesn't depend on pull. The runner contract needs a rewrite, and this gets us back to a simpler starting point.

**Delivery**

- The reconciler builds a per-task actor template (`<task>-tmpl-<hash>` over the image, the runner volume and the env). The template carries the Task and Workspace as `AX_TASK_YAML` and `AX_WORKSPACE_YAML`, and is deleted along with the task.
- `ax-runner` reads them at startup through `runner.LoadSpec`.
- A gateway applies its egress rules directly to the task actor.

**Removed**

- `internal/runnerhttp` (the `:8081` service and its OIDC/JWT token), `internal/lifecycle`, and `pkg/apis/runner/v1`.
- `internal/substrate/runner_egress.go`, `internal/server/task_applier.go`, `runner/pull.go` and `runner/output_buffer.go`.
- The control state in `store.TaskRow`, which is now `{Task, Generation}`. `schema.sql` drops no columns, so existing databases keep the old ones.
- The `:8081` port in the deploy and E2E manifests, plus the matching text in `skills/substrate`.

**Kept**

- The launcher contract (#621), the egress CA and git-askpass (#581), and `spec.setup`.
- Later changes that don't depend on pull: the `ax-runner` rename (#677), required images (#647), #642 and #663.

**What users lose**

- Workspace pre-warming is dormant. Without a setup coordinator, `PrewarmEnabled()` is false, and the server rejects Workspace `spec.profile` and `spec.setup.gateway` as Unimplemented. Each task runs `spec.setup` in its own sandbox.
- Tasks no longer reach COMPLETED or FAILED with output.
- `docs/manifests.md` and the hero demo now say this.

**Testing**

- [x] `make verify`
- [x] `go build ./cmd/ax ./cmd/ax-server ./cmd/ax-runner`
- [x] `go test ./...`
- [x] Postgres store tests (`postgres:17-alpine`)
- [ ] `make test-e2e`
- [ ] `make test-local-install`

#685 can be closed once this merges, since `runnerhttp` is gone.

title: api: reconsider redundant Task status fields
body:
`TaskStatus` reports how a task ended in several overlapping places. With the push runner (#686), nothing outside the sandbox writes most of them. We don't trust anything an actor reports, so the control plane should only report what it can observe from Substrate.

**Redundant**

- `TaskResult` (`SUCCEEDED`/`FAILED`/`CANCELLED`) maps one to one onto the terminal `TaskState` values (`COMPLETED`/`FAILED`/`CANCELLED`). Non-test code never sets it, and only `ax describe` reads it (`cmd/ax/task.go`).
- `TaskStatusDetail` and `TaskStatusReason` (`PROVISIONING_FAILED`, `SANDBOX_CRASHED`) duplicate the `Ready` condition's reason and message. On a crash, `internal/server/server.go` writes the same message to both. `TaskStatusDetail` also outlives the failure, while conditions are recomputed from Substrate on every read.
- `TaskOutcome.status` (`google.rpc.Status`) is a third place for the same failure.

**Not written with the push runner**

- `TaskOutcome` (`result`, `status`, `exit_code`, `output`). Only the pull runner reported it. `ax promote` uses `Outcome != nil` to decide whether a task finished (`cmd/ax/promote.go`).
- `attempt` is always 1, and `previous_failure` is never set. Both only make sense with `spec.retry`, which is rejected.
- `resolved_argv` is copied from `spec.commands` only, so the documented fallback to the image's `ENTRYPOINT` + `CMD` never happens.

**Proposal**

- Remove `TaskResult`, `TaskStatusDetail`, and `TaskStatusReason`. Terminal `TaskState` plus the `Ready` condition (reasons such as `ProvisioningFailed` and `SandboxCrashed`) become the single answer to how a task ended.
- Remove `TaskOutcome`, `attempt`, and `previous_failure` until something trusted can fill them in. If we want exit codes or output, Substrate should observe them; the runner should not report them.
- Remove `resolved_argv`, or document it as `spec.commands` only.
- Switch `ax promote` to check for a terminal `TaskState`, and update `ax describe` and `docs/manifests.md`.

v1alpha1 is pre-release, so field numbers can be reused, as in #605.

title: all: push tasks to runners and remove the runner pull protocol
body:
Removes the runner pull protocol (`pkg/apis/runner/v1`) and moves task actors to push mode. Workspace setup still runs in a separate setup actor.

## Why

Actors come from profile templates shared by many tasks, so the runner has to learn its task at runtime. Until now the runner pulled it from ax-server's runner endpoint (`:8081`), authenticated by an Actor JWT that the egress gateway injected. That needed a second server, JWT validation, a per-actor egress rule back to ax-server, and run-attempt bookkeeping in the task row.

## What changes

- **Push endpoints on the runner's port 80** (`v1alpha1.RunnerTaskPath`, `v1alpha1.RunnerSetupPath`):
  - `POST /runner/v1alpha1/task`: Task YAML, optionally followed by the bound Workspace as a second document.
  - `POST /runner/v1alpha1/setup`: Workspace YAML, sent to setup actors.
  - Replies: `202` accepted, `200` already holds the same object (atespace, name, uid), `409` holds different work, `400` bad body.
  - `/readyz?check=workspace` returns `503` while pending, `200` when ready, and `500` with the reason when setup failed. Plain `/readyz` returns `200` while waiting, for Substrate's WakeupProbe.
- **ax-server** (`internal/controller/actorhttp.go`) pushes after `ResumeActor` and polls the workspace check. It dials the worker IP `ResumeActor` returned and falls back to `atenet-router` with `ate-target-actor`. The runner never calls ax-server.
  - `TaskReconciler.Resume` pushes the task on every resume. A rejected push (4xx) fails the resume with `ActorResumeFailed`. A runner-reported setup failure sets `WorkspaceReady=False/SetupFailed`.
  - `WorkspaceManager` uses a `SetupRunner` (`HTTPSetupRunner` in production) in place of `SetupCoordinator`.
- **Runner**: `runner.Config.AwaitPush` replaces `PullMode`/`ControlURL`. `ax-runner` and `claude-code-runner` wait for a push when no task is given by env or file. A new `Config.PrepareTask` hook lets `claude-code-runner` rewrite pushed tasks.
- **Removed**:
  - `pkg/apis/runner/v1`
  - `internal/runnerhttp` (the `:8081` server and its JWTs)
  - `internal/lifecycle`
  - `internal/substrate/runner_egress.go`
  - `runner/pull.go` and `runner/output_buffer.go`
  - the `--runner-addr`, `--runner-endpoint` and Actor JWT flags
  - the `ax-server-runner` Service and its NetworkPolicy rule (reverts #631)
  - the run-attempt fields of the task row
- **Egress**: `bindGateway` is back to Gateway rules only. A task without a Gateway gets no egress policy; the runner rule existed only to reach `:8081`.
- **Store**: `TaskRow` is renamed `TaskVersion`. `schema.sql` adds no `DROP COLUMN`.

## Multiple ax-server replicas

The replica that builds a snapshot owns the whole flow:
- It creates a setup actor with a random suffix, resumes it, pushes, and polls that actor directly. State lives in the runner, so replicas share nothing.
- The Workspace lock (Postgres advisory lock and lease) keeps it to one builder.
- If the replica crashes, the setup actor is orphaned. The next attempt uses a new actor, and `WorkspaceManager.Delete` removes leftovers by prefix.

## Known limitations

- ax-server no longer records exit codes or attempts, so `status.outcome` is never set by the runner.
- An actor woken without `ResumeTask` (router auto-resume, container restart) waits for a push until the next `ResumeTask`.
- The push endpoints are first-assignment-wins; a runner never switches tasks.
- Prewarm can no longer be turned off with `--runner-addr`; cmd/ax-server always provides an `HTTPSetupRunner`.
- On resume, an unreachable runner is soft: `WorkspaceReady` stays `False/Initializing` and the resume succeeds.

## Testing

- `make verify`, the three builds, and `go test ./...` pass locally.
- Postgres tier (`AX_TEST_POSTGRES_URL`, `postgres:17-alpine` under podman): 10 tests pass, none skipped.
- New unit tests:
  - the metadata server push endpoints and `readyz` 500
  - runner push mode (task, setup, setup failure)
  - `HTTPSetupRunner` (rejection, no address, router fallback)
  - Resume push rejection and setup failure
- Not run: E2E and `make test-local-install`.

### Local cluster (`make build-local-cluster`)

Built ax-server and ax-runner (linux/arm64) from this branch into the `localhost:5001` registry. `ax local start` rolled the new ax-server out onto an existing `ax-local` Kind cluster (Substrate v1.0.0, podman), with no errors in the ax-server log. Results:

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Workspace `push-ws` with `setup.files` and a `setup.commands` step | `ax apply` took 4.3 s. One setup actor (`ax-ws-setup-…`) was resumed, the Workspace was pushed to `/runner/v1alpha1/setup`, and the snapshot was tagged. `Phase: Ready`, `SnapshotReady=True`. |
| Warm task `push-warm` (binds `push-ws`, no profile) | `ax resume` took 2.1 s. `WorkspaceReady=True` ("seeded from snapshot tag …"), `Ready=True/TaskRunning`. Its command read `hello.txt` and the `built.txt` written by the setup actor, saw its `spec.env`, and ran as UID 1000. |
| Cold task `push-cold` (own profile, no workspace) | `ax resume` took 2.1 s. `Ready=True/TaskRunning`; the command ran with its env as UID 1000. |
| `ax suspend` / `ax resume push-warm` | Resume took 2.1 s. A file written before the suspend survived, the fresh runner accepted the re-pushed task, and the task returned to `Ready=True/TaskRunning`. `ax ssh` works (`spec.debug: true`). |
| Workspace `push-bad-ws` whose setup command runs `exit 7` | The runner's `500` reason reached the user. `ax apply` failed with `FailedPrecondition … running setup.commands[0] ("echo about to fail; exit 7"): about to fail: exit status 7`, and the Workspace showed `Phase: Failed` with `SetupComplete`/`SnapshotReady` `False/SetupFailed` carrying the same message. |

Unchanged from main: a setup failure the runner reports is retried once on a fresh setup actor (`maxSetupAttempts`), so `push-bad-ws` used two setup actors. That can help with a flaky `git clone`, but it is wasted work for a deterministic failure. Marking a runner-reported failure as non-retryable could be a follow-up.

Fixes #685, #681.

title: ax local start takes 3–5 minutes on a fresh cluster
body:
On a machine with no existing cluster, `ax local start` takes 3–5 minutes before the first task can run. A second run against the same cluster is fast because `substrate.Bootstrap` takes its `alreadyHealthy` fast path, so the cost is all in first-time setup. That is a lot of waiting for a first impression, and for `make test-local-install` in CI.

## What a fresh start does

These steps run one after another, and most of them block on a readiness wait:

1. Create the Kind cluster and wait for nodes to be Ready (`internal/install/cluster/kind.go`, `--timeout=120s`).
2. Download kubectl if needed (`executil.EnsureKubectl`).
3. Bootstrap Agent Substrate (`internal/install/substrate/bootstrap.go`):
   1. Create namespaces, apply the CRDs, and wait for them to be Established.
   2. Create the CA pools, apply podcertificate-controller, and wait for its rollout.
   3. Apply the gVisor SandboxConfig.
   4. Deploy the bundled PostgreSQL and wait for `postgres-0` to be Ready, then initialize the schema and roles.
   5. Create the ate-system PKI pools, ConfigMaps and Secrets.
   6. Apply the control-plane bundle and wait for each component's pods to be Ready.
   7. Create the default gVisor WorkerPool and wait for it.
4. Deploy AX (`internal/install/axdeploy`): Postgres and ax-server, waiting for their rollouts (3 minute timeout each).

Each pod in steps 3 and 4 also has to pull its image into the Kind node on first use, unless the image is preloaded.

## What we don't know yet

We have no per-step timing, so we don't know whether the time goes to image pulls, to readiness waits that could overlap, to the WorkerPool coming up, or to the polling intervals of the waits themselves.

## Proposed next steps

- Print or trace how long each step takes during `ax local start` (the CLI already has `ax --trace`), and record a breakdown on a fresh macOS and Linux machine and in the `local-install` CI job.
- Depending on what that shows:
  - Preload or pull images in parallel up front (`kind load` or a pull-ahead DaemonSet) instead of letting each rollout pull its own.
  - Apply the independent manifests together and wait for them at the end, instead of applying and waiting one step at a time. For example, PostgreSQL, the podcertificate-controller, and AX's own Postgres don't depend on each other.
  - Shorten the polling intervals of the readiness waits.
- Show progress during long waits so the command doesn't look hung (see #648).

title: Canonical /ax/STATUS file (JSON) for a task to report COMPLETED, FAILED, or REQUIRES_ACTION
body:
A task's command has no way to tell AX how it ended. `TaskState` has `COMPLETED`, `FAILED` and `REQUIRES_ACTION`, and `TaskStatus.outcome` has `result`, `exit_code` and `output`, but nothing inside the sandbox sets them. A task that finished reads `Working`/`Ready=True` until someone deletes it (#346). With #688 the runner no longer reports exit codes to ax-server either, so today the state is never set.

We should define one canonical status file, `/ax/STATUS`, with structured JSON content. The command (or the image's launcher) writes it, the runner surfaces it, and ax-server turns it into the task's state.

## Proposal

**File.** `/ax/STATUS` holds one JSON object:

```json
{
  "state": "FAILED",
  "message": "tests failed: 3 of 120",
  "details": {"failedTests": ["test_login", "test_logout", "test_refresh"]}
}
```

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `state` | yes | `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, or `REQUIRES_ACTION` |
| `message` | no | A short human-readable summary, shown by `ax describe task` and stored as the outcome's status message |
| `details` | no | Any JSON object, passed through to the task's status for tools and UIs; size-capped like `spec.config` |

How each state maps to the task:

| `state` | Sets |
|---|---|
| `COMPLETED` | `status.state: COMPLETED`, `outcome.result: SUCCEEDED` |
| `FAILED` | `status.state: FAILED`, `outcome.result: FAILED` |
| `REQUIRES_ACTION` | `status.state: REQUIRES_ACTION`; `message` says what the agent needs from a human |

The agent's answer stays in `$AX_OUTPUT_FILE` and is still reported as `outcome.output`. `/ax/STATUS` only says how the task ended.

**Location and durability.** `/ax/STATUS` must survive suspend and resume, but only the workspace volume is snapshotted. The runner therefore backs `/ax` with the workspace volume, for example as a symlink to `<workspace>/.ax`, so the path stays fixed while the data persists. `/run/ax` (`DefaultRunDir`, the launcher's input files) stays separate because it is rewritten on every start. The runner also exports the path as `AX_STATUS_FILE`, like the other launcher-contract variables (`runner/launcher.go`).

**Writing rules.**
- Write atomically: write a temp file in `/ax`, then rename it to `STATUS`.
- `COMPLETED` and `FAILED` are terminal: once the runner has seen one, later writes are ignored.
- `REQUIRES_ACTION` is not terminal. The command can overwrite it with a terminal state, and resuming the task with new input clears it so the agent can continue.
- A file that is not valid JSON, or has an unknown `state`, is reported as `FAILED` with a message naming the parse error. A malformed report shouldn't look like success.

**Defaults when the command writes nothing.** The runner falls back to the exit status and writes `/ax/STATUS` itself: exit 0 gives `{"state": "COMPLETED"}`, and a non-zero exit or a signal gives `{"state": "FAILED", "message": "exit status 3", "exitCode": 3}`. A long-lived command that never exits (an interactive or `ax ssh` sandbox) stays `Working`.

**Getting the state to ax-server.** With #688 the runner never calls ax-server, so ax-server has to read the state from the runner:
- The runner serves the parsed file on port 80, for example `GET /runner/v1alpha1/status`, along with the exit code and `$AX_OUTPUT_FILE` capped at 64 KiB, as `outcome.output` documents.
- ax-server records `COMPLETED` and `FAILED` in the store once it sees them. `store.StoredStatus` already persists these AX-owned states and the outcome, so a later read doesn't need the sandbox, which may be suspended or gone.

Related: #346 (finished task reports `Working` forever), #420 (suspend on completion), #687 (redundant status fields), #688 (push model, which removed exit-code reporting).

title: Versioned Postgres schema migrations with Goose (as Agent Substrate does)
body:
AX has no schema management. `internal/store/postgres/schema.go` runs all of `schema.sql` on every ax-server start, under an advisory lock, and relies on `CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS`, `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, and a hand-written `DO $$` block that rewrites the `locks` primary key. `schema.go` already carries `TODO: Add versioned migrations before the schema first changes after release.`

That only works while every change is additive and idempotent:
- **No removals.** #688 deletes eight runner columns from `tasks` (`actor_uid`, `runnable`, `active_run_id`, `run_seq`, `runner_token_hash`, `runner_token_confirmed`, `claim_nonce`, `last_acked_runner_seq`). Existing databases keep them forever, because a `DROP COLUMN` in an always-run script would run on every start, and older replicas still reading the column would break.
- **No record of what ran.** Nothing records which schema a database has, so we can't tell an up-to-date database from one that a newer ax-server partly upgraded, or refuse to start an older binary against a newer schema.
- **Breaking changes need manual steps.** The `locks` primary-key rewrite asks operators to stop every replica before upgrading (the comment in `schema.go`). Nothing enforces or records that.
- **Data changes have no place.** Backfills and data rewrites need to run exactly once, not on every start.

## Proposal: Goose, as Agent Substrate does it

Agent Substrate already solves this with [Goose](https://github.com/pressly/goose) (`github.com/pressly/goose/v3`, v3.27.3 in its `go.mod`) in `cmd/ateapi/internal/store/atepg/schema.go`. AX already depends on Substrate at v1.0.0 and also uses pgx, so we can copy its approach almost as-is:

- **Embedded, numbered SQL files.** `internal/store/postgres/migrations/NNNNNN_name.sql`, embedded with `//go:embed migrations/*.sql`. `000001_initial.sql` is today's schema without the `IF NOT EXISTS` guards and without the pre-release upgrade blocks.
- **Applied at startup with the Goose provider.**
  - `goose.NewProvider(goose.DialectPostgres, stdlib.OpenDBFromPool(pool), migrations, goose.WithTableName("schema_migrations"), goose.WithSessionLocker(locker))`, then `provider.Up(ctx)`. This replaces `createSchema`.
  - The locker is `lock.NewPostgresSessionLocker`, keyed by `hashtextextended('ax:postgres:migrations:' || current_schema(), 0)`, so several replicas starting at once apply each migration once and AX never contends with Substrate's lock in a shared database.
- **Logging.** Log the starting, current, and latest versions, the number of migrations applied, and the duration, as Substrate's `migrateToLatest` does, and report partial failures through `goose.PartialError`.
- **Refuse an unknown schema.** Before Goose creates its ledger, check for AX tables without a `schema_migrations` table, as Substrate's `rejectUnversionedSubstrateSchema` does. AX has pre-release installs, so instead of refusing outright we can adopt them once: if the tables exist without a ledger, verify they match `000001_initial.sql` and record version 1. Otherwise refuse with a clear error.
- **A verify script, like Substrate's `hack/verify/postgresql-migrations.sh`, run by `make verify`.** It checks:
  - files are named `NNNNNN_name.sql` and numbered without gaps
  - each file has `-- +goose Up` and no `-- +goose Down`
  - no `-- +goose no transaction`, no `IF NOT EXISTS`, no `ENVSUB`, and no `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`, so Goose controls the transaction
  - against the merge base, merged migrations are never changed or deleted
- **Forward-only.** As in Substrate, there are no down migrations; a mistake is fixed by a new migration. Removing a column takes two releases: stop reading it, then drop it in a later migration once no running replica uses it.
- **Tests.** Apply all migrations to an empty database in the Postgres tier (`AX_TEST_POSTGRES_URL`), and check that a database at version N upgrades to latest.

title: Long-running, goal-based tasks with steering (TaskService)
body:
## Problem

A `Task` runs its goal once, and nobody can talk to it while it runs: there is no way to add guidance, answer a question, or interrupt it. The control plane also learns little from inside the sandbox; a task's state reflects its actor, not its agent's progress, and the outcome does not reach the server.

The API already anticipates more. `TaskSpec` has `goal` and `sessionId`, retries are counted per turn, and `TaskState` has `IDLE`, `WORKING` and `REQUIRES_ACTION`, which nothing sets yet. The roadmap lists "Task Communication and Steering Protocols" and "Sessions".

## Goals

- A task pursues its goal over many turns, for as long as it takes, and finishes when the goal is met rather than when a process exits.
- Users, services and other tasks steer a running task: send guidance, answer its questions, and interrupt it.
- An idle task costs no compute: it is suspended and wakes when a message arrives.
- Any CLI agent that can continue a session works without changes.

## Non-goals

- Changing a task's spec. Tasks stay immutable; steering adds to the task's conversation.
- Long-term memory across tasks, and task-to-task identity. Both are separate roadmap items.

## TaskService

A new gRPC service, `TaskService`, sits beside `AX`. `AX` stays declarative CRUD over the four kinds; `TaskService` is the conversation with a running task. The two differ in shape (an append-only, streamed history against get/list/create/delete) and are likely to differ in authorization, so they are separate.

| RPC | Description |
|---|---|
| `Send` | Send a task guidance, an answer to its question, or an interrupt. Resumes the task if it is idle and suspended. |
| `List` | Read the task's conversation: what was sent to it and what it reported. |
| `Watch` | Stream the conversation and the task's state changes as they happen. |

A conversation entry is either sent by a user (a message, an answer, an interrupt) or reported by the task (a state change, a question, progress, the outcome).

## Lifecycle

```
          create / message
QUEUED ────────────────────► WORKING ──── turn ends ────► IDLE ── idle timeout ──► SUSPENDED
                               ▲  │                         │                         │
                               │  └── asks a question ──► REQUIRES_ACTION             │
                               │                            │                         │
                               └──────── message / answer ──┴──── message ────────────┘

WORKING ── goal met ──► COMPLETED        WORKING ── goal abandoned or limit hit ──► FAILED
```

The first turn starts from the goal; each later turn starts from the messages sent since. The agent, not the process, decides when the goal is met. `spec.goal` gains limits on turns, total duration, and how long the task may sit idle before it is suspended.

## Runner contract

The runner owns the turn loop: it hands each turn's input to the agent, and reports turns, questions and the outcome back to the control plane. The control plane keeps the conversation durably, so nothing is lost across suspend, resume, or a server restart.

Agents integrate in one of two ways. By default, the runner starts the agent once per turn and the agent continues its session, which suits CLI agents such as Claude Code. Agent frameworks that keep their own loop can instead receive messages and report events continuously.

Tasks with explicit `spec.commands` keep today's behavior and cannot be steered.

## CLI

`ax send` sends a message, an answer, or an interrupt. `ax attach` follows a task's conversation and sends what you type. `ax describe` and `ax studio` show the conversation.

## Phases

1. **Reporting.** The runner reports turn state and the outcome; tasks show `IDLE`, `REQUIRES_ACTION` and `COMPLETED`, and a real outcome. Useful even for today's one-shot goals.
2. **Steering.** `TaskService`, turn-based execution in the default and Claude Code runners, `ax send` and `ax attach`.
3. **Long-running.** Suspend when idle, resume on message, goal limits.
4. **Streaming agents** and steering from `ax studio`.

## Open questions

- Should tasks without a goal accept messages, making every task chat-capable?
- How long is a conversation kept for tasks that run for weeks?
- Should a message from one task to another identify the sender?

title: all: report how a task ended through AX_STATUS_FILE
body:
Step 1 of #690: a task's command can say how the task ended, and AX records `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`. Fixes #346 for tasks whose command exits; related: #420.

Stacked on #688 (base `run`), which removed exit-code reporting with the pull protocol.

## What changes

**Runner**
- Gives the command `AX_STATUS_FILE` = `<workspace>/.ax/STATUS` (on the workspace volume, next to `AX_OUTPUT_FILE`). The command may write `{"state": "COMPLETED" | "FAILED", "message": "..."}`.
- When the command exits, reads the file without following symlinks, only if the agent owns it, up to 64 KiB. Invalid JSON or an unknown state reads as `FAILED`.
- Without a file, the exit status decides (`0` → `COMPLETED`, otherwise `FAILED` with `exit status N`), and the runner writes the file so it survives a suspend.
- Serves `GET /runner/v1alpha1/status`: `204` until the command exits, then `{"state","message","exitCode","output"}`; `output` is `AX_OUTPUT_FILE` or the end of stdout/stderr.
- Removes a status left by an earlier run before starting the command. A launcher that already finished for the same goal is not rerun; its stored status is reported again.

**ax-server**
- `WatchTaskStatus` polls each `Working` task's runner every 2s, records `COMPLETED`/`FAILED` as state, `status.outcome` and `Ready`, then suspends the actor under the task's lock. Recording is an atomic `Apply` transition, so all replicas may poll.

**Tests and docs**
- Unit tests for the status file; runner tests through the real endpoint; a controller client test (404 from an older runner reads as "no status"); a server test with the substrate fake (`COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, actor suspended, later polls change nothing).
- Restores `TestE2E_PureImageLauncher` and `TestE2E_PrewarmAndCustomImageSharedWorkspace` and the launcher image removed in #688, which wait for exactly this.
- `docs/runner.md` ("Report how the task ended", the endpoint, the checklist) and `docs/sandbox.md` (`AX_OUTPUT_FILE`, `AX_STATUS_FILE`); `AGENTS.md` layout.

## Not in this PR (later steps of #690)
- `REQUIRES_ACTION`: it needs a stored state and a way to give a task new input.
- `details` on `TaskOutcome` (an API change).

## Differences from the proposal in #690
- The file is `<workspace>/.ax/STATUS` rather than a re-pointed `/ax`, which holds the runner's own state (`git-askpass`) and should not become agent-writable. It still survives suspend.
- A terminal status does not stop a later run: a `spec.commands` task suspended between its exit and ax-server's next 2s poll runs again on resume, with the earlier status cleared. This keeps the existing launcher semantics (a failed launcher is retried; a new goal runs it again).

## Testing
- `make verify`, `go build ./cmd/...`, `go test ./...` pass.
- On a local cluster (`make build-local-cluster`): a task writing `AX_OUTPUT_FILE` ended `Completed` with that output; one writing `{"state":"FAILED","message":"tests failed: 3 of 120"}` ended `Failed` with that message; one exiting 3 ended `Failed`, `exitCode: 3`, output from stderr. Each was recorded within ~4s and its actor suspended.
- E2E not run locally (the setup script calls `docker`; this machine has podman). CI runs the restored tests.

title: ax promote: support optional --copy-workspace to transfer /workspace files across clusters?
body:
## Context

`ax promote task <name> --to <context>` (#618, #664) promotes a Task along with its bound `Workspace` and `Gateway` specs to a target cluster, while intentionally leaving the sandbox's runtime `/workspace` files untouched today (`promoteUsage`: *"The sandbox's files and the Secrets a Gateway names are not copied"*).

When iterating on a task locally (`ax local` or another dev cluster) where an agent has already made edits inside `/workspace` that aren't committed/pushed to a remote Git repo yet, promoting the task along with its current `/workspace` files is a common workflow.

## Question Before Prototyping a PR

Would an opt-in **`--copy-workspace`** flag on `ax promote` (for tasks with `spec.debug: true`, streaming `/workspace` sandbox-to-sandbox via `guest.Client` / `FileSystemService` or `tar` over `Exec` before resuming/restarting on the target—preserving read-only `.git/objects/pack` permissions and skipping `.ax/` state files as needed) fit the direction you have in mind for `ax promote`, or are you planning to handle cross-cluster `/workspace` state transfer at the Substrate snapshot/volume layer instead?

Happy to put together a small, focused PR if CLI-side `/workspace` streaming is useful!

cc @yongruilin @YoyinZyc

title: Remove ReasonSubstrateUnavailable: return Substrate failures as errors, not as state
body:
`ReasonSubstrateUnavailable` is a condition reason that records, as task or workspace state, that a call to Agent Substrate failed. A Substrate outage is not a state of the task. It should be returned as an error to the caller that hit it and not stored. `pkg/apis/v1alpha1/types.go` already has a TODO saying so.

## Where it is used on `main`

- **Provisioning** (`internal/controller/reconciler.go`): `ensureSubstrateResources`, `bindGateway`, and `Resume` set `Ready=False/SubstrateUnavailable` and then return the error. `recordFailure` in `internal/server/server.go` stores that condition with state `QUEUED` and returns `Unavailable`. The caller already gets the error; the stored condition only repeats it for a later `ax describe`.
- **Workspace prepare** (`internal/controller/workspace.go`): `SetupComplete` and `SnapshotReady` are set to `False/SubstrateUnavailable`, and the error is returned as well.
- **Reading a task** (`internal/server/server.go`): when the task's actor cannot be read, the task is returned with `Ready=Unknown/SubstrateUnavailable` instead of an error. This is the only place where the reason replaces an error.

## Proposed change

- Return the error in the provisioning and workspace paths without setting the condition. Whether the task is `QUEUED` and the RPC returns `Unavailable` already follows from `substrate.IsTransientError`, not from the condition.
- Decide what reading a task does when Substrate cannot be reached: fail the RPC, or return the stored task without live actor status. Failing makes `ax get` and `ax describe` unusable during a Substrate outage, so this needs a decision before the reason can be deleted.
- Delete `ReasonSubstrateUnavailable` and update the tests in `internal/controller` and `internal/server` that assert on it.

## Related

- The same TODO lists `ReasonAtespaceCreationFailed`, `ReasonActorNotFound`, `ReasonActorCreationFailed`, and `ReasonActorResumeFailed`. They are out of scope here but have the same problem.
- #468 covers the retry and waiting policy for Substrate errors.
- #688 adds one more use of the reason, for a runner that does not accept a pushed task in time.

title: Don't split Workspace into its own actor; apply workspace config when the task starts
body:
## Summary

A `Workspace` should not become its own Substrate actor with its own lifecycle that tasks attach to. A workspace is metadata the runner uses when a task starts. Users who want a long-lived environment to branch from can run a task and fork other tasks from it.

## What a Workspace is for

A `Workspace` describes what a task needs to start, for example:

- which MCP servers to fetch from a registry
- which skills to download
- which repositories to clone, which inline files to write, and which setup commands to run

All of this is task startup configuration. `ax-runner` should read and apply it when it starts the task, inside that task's own actor. A separate actor for the workspace isn't needed.

## Workspace metadata is time sensitive

What a workspace resolves to depends on when it is resolved:

- **Registries change.** The MCP servers a registry returns, their endpoints, and their versions can change at any time. If you resolve them once when the workspace is created, every task that starts later gets whatever was current back then.
- **Skills and repositories move.** A skill's latest version and a branch's head commit change all the time. If setup is baked in ahead of time, tasks run against stale content without anyone noticing.
- **Policy can change.** If an admin removes an MCP server from the registry or revokes a skill, the change should apply to the next task that starts. It shouldn't wait for someone to rebuild the workspace.

Because of this, the runner should resolve workspace metadata when each task starts, so every task gets the current state. A separate workspace actor would freeze the metadata at the time the workspace was set up and copy that frozen state into every task that uses it. If a user really does want a frozen setup, they can say so explicitly by forking from a tagged task. That way it's a choice the user makes, not the default.

## Why not a separate actor

- **Two lifecycles.** A workspace actor has to be provisioned, suspended, resumed, garbage-collected and authorized separately from the tasks that use it. That's more state in the reconciler and the store, and more ways for the two to get out of sync. #453 already shows how hard it is to keep workspace state correct inside one task.
- **Substrate already covers the use cases.** Shared state between tasks is better served by primitives that already exist or are planned:
  - **Shared volumes** for data several tasks read or write at the same time.
  - **Tagging and forking** for "set up once, branch many times": start a task, let its setup finish, tag it, and fork new tasks from that point. You get the pre-warmed behavior without a new resource type.
- **Simpler mental model.** One task, one actor. The workspace is just the startup configuration of that actor.

## Proposal

- Keep `Workspace` as a declarative config resource that tasks reference. Don't back it with an actor.
- `ax-runner` resolves and applies workspace config (MCP servers, skills, clones, files, commands) every time a task starts, against the current state of registries and sources.
- Document forking from a tagged task as the way to reuse an expensive setup, and shared volumes as the way to share data between tasks that are running at the same time.
- Remove or drop any existing or planned code paths that give a workspace its own actor.

## Related

- #563 (v1alpha1 API epic, "Pre-warmed `Workspace`")
- #649 (follow-up turns on the same task workspace)
- #467 (shared golden snapshots and task clones)

cc @yongruilin @YoyinZyc thoughts?

title: ax local start can't recover when the atenet-router envoy sidecar is stuck unready
body:
## Summary

Sometimes `ax local start` fails during the Substrate step because the existing `atenet-router` pod on the local cluster is unhealthy. Once that happens, the cluster can't recover on its own. Every later `ax local start` (and so `make build-local-cluster` and `make test-local-install`) fails the same way until someone restarts the pod by hand.

## What we saw

- `atenet-router` is `1/2` ready. Its `envoy` container had been failing its readiness probe with HTTP 503 for 16 hours (6,978 failures).
- Likely trigger: the pod's `atenet-router` container drained and restarted at 06:35 UTC, and the `envoy` sidecar has reported unready ever since. Its last successful traffic was `hero-demo-custom-task` at 06:13.
- The run that hit this was `make build-local-cluster`. It rebuilt the images and pushed them to the local registry, then `ax local start` gave up in the Substrate step. The new `ax-server` was not rolled out and no tasks were created, so the change under test was never exercised.

The cluster problem existed before the run. Nothing in the change caused it.

## Why `ax local start` doesn't recover

1. `alreadyHealthy` (`internal/install/substrate/bootstrap.go:747`) waits up to 90s for pods labeled `app=atenet-router` to be Ready. The envoy sidecar never becomes ready, so the check fails.
2. `Bootstrap` then re-applies the Substrate manifests. They haven't changed, so the Deployment's pod template is the same and no new pod is created.
3. `rolloutStatus(..., "deployment/atenet-router", ...)` (`bootstrap.go:289-296`) waits for the same stuck pod to become available, and times out.

The result is a timeout that tells the user nothing about the cause or the fix.

## Workaround

Restart the pod:

```bash
kubectl --context ax-local -n ate-system rollout restart deployment/atenet-router
```

## Proposal

- When `ax local start` finds an existing Substrate workload whose pods are stuck unready (for example, a container that has failed its readiness probe for longer than the rollout timeout), run `rollout restart` on it once before waiting on it again.
- If that doesn't help, fail with an error that names the unready pod and container and prints the `kubectl rollout restart` command, instead of a bare rollout timeout.
- Separately, find out why envoy stays unready after the `atenet-router` container restarts. If the cause is in Substrate, file it upstream.

title: CreateTask: do not store a Task until its actor exists
body:
A Task should not exist until its actor exists on Agent Substrate. Today `CreateTask` stores the Task first and creates the actor afterwards, so a failed create leaves a Task behind.

## What happens today

`CreateTask` in `internal/server/server.go`:

1. Stores the Task with state `QUEUED`.
2. Calls `TaskReconciler.Suspend`, which creates the atespace, the ActorTemplate and the actor, suspends the actor, and binds the Gateway.
3. On failure, `recordFailure` keeps the stored Task: `QUEUED` and `Unavailable` for a transient error, `FAILED` with `PROVISIONING_FAILED` otherwise.

The consequences:

- A create that fails for good leaves a `FAILED` Task with no actor. Tasks are immutable, so the name cannot be applied again until the Task is deleted.
- A create that fails transiently leaves a `QUEUED` Task. Nothing retries it: ax-server has no queue and no background work. The client has to apply the same manifest again, and `CreateTask` has a special case that allows this only for a stored `QUEUED` Task with no template and an identical spec.
- `QUEUED` reads as "something will pick this up", which is not true.

## Proposed change

- Provision the actor first, and store the Task only once the actor exists.
- A failed create returns the error and stores nothing. The client retries by applying again, as for any failed RPC.
- Remove the stored `QUEUED` state for creation, the retry special case in `CreateTask`, and the `provisioning` use of `recordFailure`.

## To decide

- **Orphaned actors.** If storing the Task fails after the actor was created, or ax-server dies between the two steps, an actor exists with no Task. `CreateTask` can delete the actor when the store write fails. For a crash, a later create of the same name adopts the actor, because the actor is named after the Task and creation is an ensure; otherwise nothing removes it.
- **Server-assigned fields.** `metadata.uid`, `create_time` and the default `session_id` are assigned before provisioning today. They can stay in memory until the Task is stored, as long as nothing in provisioning needs them to be durable.
- **Resume.** `ResumeTask` also leaves a Task `QUEUED` after a transient failure. That Task already has an actor, so it is a separate question.

## Related

- #695: remove `ReasonSubstrateUnavailable` and return Substrate failures as errors.

title: Rename GetGateway to LoadGateway
body:
Rename the store's `GetGateway` method to `LoadGateway`, per Go naming conventions, which avoid the `Get` prefix.

This is the Go method on `store.Store` and `controller.GatewayStore`, not the `GetGateway` RPC.

body:
ax-server now reaches a task's runner only through atenet-router, as asked in https://github.com/google/ax/pull/688#discussion_r4655802512.

- The task push, the workspace setup push and the readiness check no longer dial the worker IP first.
- Tests give their fake runner as `ATENET_ROUTER_ADDR` instead of as the worker IP.
