body: Move `Locker`, `Key`, and `ErrLockFailed` from `internal/lock` into `internal/store`, and `MemoryLocker` into `internal/store/memory` so both backends implement `store.Locker`. Then delete `internal/lock`. Resolves the TODO in `internal/lock/lock.go`.

title: Dead code: functions no binary reaches
body:
`deadcode` ([golang.org/x/tools/cmd/deadcode](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/cmd/deadcode), v0.52.0) reports two sets of functions on `main` at d5af95e. The lists here leave out `internal/model`, `internal/store/memory`, `internal/substrate/substratetest`, `internal/telemetry` and `internal/version`.

- 1 function that nothing reaches, neither a binary nor a test.
- 8 functions that no binary reaches: the one above plus 7 that only tests reach.

The binaries are `cmd/ax`, `cmd/ax-server`, `cmd/ax-runner` and `cmd/runners/claude-code-runner`.

## Reached by nothing

```text
internal/metadata/server.go:323:18: unreachable func: Server.IsWorkspaceReady
```

## Reached by no binary

By package:

| Package | Functions | What they are |
|---|---|---|
| `client` | 2 | `CurrentContext` and `ListContexts`, exported API of the public Go client. |
| `internal/metadata` | 2 | `ProbeAddr`, which tests use to find the listener, and `IsWorkspaceReady`, which is also in the first list. |
| `internal/substrate` | 2 | `NewClient`, the constructor tests use, and `ResourceLimits`, which only its own test calls. `internal/controller/profile.go` computes the limits in production. |
| `internal/guest` | 1 | `Dial`, a wrapper over `DialTarget` that only its own test calls. |
| `internal/server` | 1 | `storedStatus`, a wrapper over `store.StoredStatus` that only `status_test.go` calls. |

```text
client/client.go:116:6: unreachable func: CurrentContext
client/client.go:122:6: unreachable func: ListContexts
internal/guest/client.go:43:6: unreachable func: Dial
internal/metadata/server.go:190:18: unreachable func: Server.ProbeAddr
internal/metadata/server.go:323:18: unreachable func: Server.IsWorkspaceReady
internal/server/server.go:821:6: unreachable func: storedStatus
internal/substrate/client.go:158:6: unreachable func: NewClient
internal/substrate/client.go:320:6: unreachable func: ResourceLimits
```

## How to reproduce

```bash
skip='^internal/(model|store/memory|substrate/substratetest|telemetry|version)/'
go run golang.org/x/tools/cmd/deadcode@v0.52.0 -test ./... | grep -vE "$skip"   # reached by nothing
go run golang.org/x/tools/cmd/deadcode@v0.52.0 ./... | grep -vE "$skip"         # reached by no binary
```

## What these lists leave out

- `deadcode` reports functions and methods only, so unused constants, variables and types are not here.
- It works from the static call graph, so code behind a branch that `ax-server` never takes is not here either.

title: Delete the Claude Code example
all: remove dead code and rename guest.DialTarget to Dial
body:
Remove six functions that no binary reaches:

- metadata.Server.IsWorkspaceReady and Server.ProbeAddr. The metadata tests move into package metadata and read the probe listener's address from the Server.
- substrate.NewClient. The reconciler tests and substratetest connect with NewClientWithOptions over plaintext.
- substrate.ResourceLimits and its test. The controller resolves profile limits itself.
- guest.Dial, a one-argument wrapper over DialTarget.
- The server's storedStatus, a wrapper over store.StoredStatus, which TestStoredStatus now calls.

With that wrapper gone, guest.DialTarget is renamed Dial and guest.DialTargetTLS is renamed DialTLS. skills/substrate/SKILL.md is updated to match.

Updates #703

title: examples: remove Claude Code example
body:
Delete examples/claude-code, cmd/runners/claude-code-runner, Dockerfile.claude-code, and their Makefile targets, ignore entries, and documentation references. Agent task images are built in agentexecutor/images.

Fixes #704

title: api: remove TaskResult, TaskStatusReason, and TaskStatusDetail
body:
Removes `TaskResult` (`TaskOutcome.result`), `TaskStatusReason`, and `TaskStatusDetail` (`TaskStatus.status_detail`) from `ax.v1alpha1`, since they duplicate `TaskState` and the `Ready` condition:

- **`TaskResult`**: 1:1 with terminal `TaskState` values (`COMPLETED` / `FAILED` / `CANCELLED`). Remaining `TaskOutcome` fields (`status`, `exit_code`, `output`) are renumbered sequentially.
- **`TaskStatusDetail` / `TaskStatusReason`**: duplicated the `Ready` condition's `reason` and `message`. Remaining `TaskStatus` fields are renumbered sequentially, and `ReasonFailed` is renamed to `ReasonSandboxCrashed` for crashed actors.
- **Server & store**: simplified `isExecutionTerminal` for `TASK_STATE_FAILED` to check `st.GetOutcome() != nil` (only `recordFailure` stores `FAILED` without an outcome), and removed `StatusDetail` handling from `internal/server/server.go` and `internal/store/task_apply.go`.
- **CLI & docs**: `ax describe task` drops the `Detail:` line and prints `Exit Code:` without `TaskResult`; removed the `status.statusDetail` mention from `docs/concepts.md` and updated tests.

Fixes #687

title: api: align TaskState with Substrate ActorState and avoid unnecessary extra states
body:
`TaskState` (`pkg/apis/v1alpha1/task.proto`) currently defines its own set of states and remaps Substrate's `ActorState` on read (`internal/server/server.go`, `actorTaskState`):

| Substrate `ActorState` | Current `TaskState` |
|---|---|
| `RUNNING` | `WORKING` |
| `RESUMING`, `REVERTING` | `QUEUED` |
| `SUSPENDING` | `SUSPENDING` |
| `SUSPENDED` | `SUSPENDED` |
| `CRASHED` | `FAILED` |
| `DELETING` | `UNSPECIFIED` (with `Ready=False/Terminating`) |

`TaskState` also defines extra states that don't exist in Substrate (`IDLE`, `REQUIRES_ACTION`, `COMPLETED`, `CANCELLED`, and `QUEUED` for in-flight/transient-error provisioning):

- `IDLE` and `REQUIRES_ACTION` are unused today.
- `QUEUED` is overloaded across in-flight `CreateTask`, transient Substrate failures (with no background queue draining them), and live `RESUMING`/`REVERTING` actors. With #698 and #695, provisioning doesn't need a `QUEUED` state either.
- Renaming `RUNNING` → `WORKING`, `RESUMING`/`REVERTING` → `QUEUED`, and `CRASHED` → `FAILED` adds translation complexity and hides the real actor state.

### Proposal

- Match `TaskState` to Substrate's `ActorState` instead of renaming or collapsing actor states.
- Don't introduce new AX-only states unless strictly required by real behavior (e.g., task-level terminal/action states if #690 lands).

Related: #687, #690, #695, #698

title: api: add repeated models to TaskSpec
body: TaskSpec should take a repeated list of Model references so a task can declare which models it uses.

title: ax-server: take the actor router URL from a flag, not ATENET_ROUTER_ADDR
body:
ax-server reaches every actor through the router, and reads the router's address from the `ATENET_ROUTER_ADDR` environment variable inside `internal/controller`, on every request. Its other Substrate settings are flags (`--substrate-endpoint`, `--substrate-authority`).

Why change it:

- The variable has no default. When it is unset, a resume succeeds without pushing the task to the runner. A flag with a default, as
  `--substrate-endpoint` has, removes that case.
- It is process-wide state, so every test that needs a router sets it with `t.Setenv`.
- More control-plane traffic will go through the router over time (e.g. #692), so the URL should be configured explicitly in one place.

Proposal: add `--router-url` to ax-server (default `https://atenet-router.ate-system.svc.cluster.local:443`), pass it from `cmd/ax-server/main.go` to the controller, and set it under `args` in `deploy/ax-server.yaml` and `test/e2e/manifests/ax-server.yaml`. ax-server stops reading `ATENET_ROUTER_ADDR`; `ax ssh` keeps reading it.

title: Rename the default image launcher from ax-harness to ax-launcher
body:
The runner starts an image's launcher at `DefaultLauncherPath = "/usr/local/bin/ax-harness"` (runner/launcher.go:54) when a task has a goal and no `spec.commands`. `runner.Config.LauncherPath` can override it, but nothing outside tests sets it, so every agent image has to ship its entry point at that exact path.

"Harness" doesn't say what the file is for. AX's own code and docs already call it the launcher (`launcherCommand`, `markLauncherDone`, "launcher contract"). Images then end up naming their real binary after the agent and adding an `ax-harness` symlink just to satisfy the runner. For example, the Gemini API Managed Agents image in agentexecutor/images ships `ax-antigravity` plus an `ax-harness` link.

`ax-runner` would be a poor replacement name: it is already AX's runner binary. It is `DefaultGuestCommand = "/usr/local/bin/ax-runner"` (internal/substrate/client.go:196), and the runner volume mounts it at `/opt/ax/ax-runner`. An image launcher at that path would be started as the runner itself when no runner volume is mounted.

Proposal:
- Rename `DefaultLauncherPath` to `/usr/local/bin/ax-launcher`.
- Update the references in internal/substrate/client.go:399, internal/install/axdeploy/deploy.go:55 and the docs.
- Decide on a migration path for existing images. For example, fall back to `/usr/local/bin/ax-harness` for one release if `ax-launcher` is missing.

title: ax local start should not require Docker
body: `ax local start` effectively requires Docker; it should work with other container runtimes and tools such as Podman (including rootless) on Linux and macOS. Today `executil.ResolveContainerRuntime` only probes `docker` then rootful `podman`, and the macOS error only points to Docker Desktop, OrbStack or Colima.

title: controller: rename TaskReconciler to TaskManager
body: TaskReconciler (internal/controller/reconciler.go) no longer runs a reconcile loop: ax-server calls it directly to provision, suspend, resume, and delete task actors. Rename it to TaskManager to match what it does and to sit alongside WorkspaceManager.

title: store, server: delete TaskApplier
body:
We don't need `TaskApplier`. AX is an imperative system for provisioning — the declarative style is only for task execution, not for provisioning. If an actor cannot be created, we return an error directly to the client rather than driving task-row state transitions through a transactional `Apply` state machine.

## Why

- Task handlers in `internal/server/server.go` already serialize mutations per task with `s.locker.Lock`.
- `TaskApplier` (`Apply`, `GetTaskVersion`, `TaskVersion`, `ApplyFunc`, `DeleteTaskVersion`) maintains a second write path alongside `store.Store` (`SaveTask`, `UpdateTaskStatus`, `DeleteTask`), including row-level `FOR UPDATE` transactions, insert-collision retries, `generation` reconciliation, and the `TaskApplierForStore` fallback adapter.

## Scope

- Remove `TaskApplier`, `TaskVersion`, `TaskKey`, `ApplyFunc`, `DeleteTaskVersion`, and `PrepareTaskVersionForApply` / `OverlayTaskGeneration` (`internal/store/task_apply.go`, `internal/store/task_version_normalize.go`, `internal/store/task_apply_test.go`); keep `StoredStatus` if still needed for scrubbing live actor fields before writes.
- Remove backend implementations and tests: `internal/store/memory/task_apply.go`, `internal/store/postgres/task_apply.go`, and `TestTaskApplier*`.
- Remove `internal/server/task_applier.go`, `server.Options.TaskApplier`, and its wiring in `cmd/ax-server/main.go`.
- Have `internal/server/server.go` use `store.Store` directly under the task lock.
- Update `AGENTS.md`.

## Related

- #698: CreateTask should not store a Task until its actor exists.
- #695: Return Substrate failures as errors, not as state.
- #713: Rename `TaskReconciler` to `TaskManager`.

title: server, controller: don't fall back to NewMemoryLocker
body: NewServer (internal/server/server.go) and NewWorkspaceManager (internal/controller/workspace.go) silently fall back to lock.NewMemoryLocker() when no Locker is passed, which only serializes within one process and is unsafe with multiple ax-server replicas. Require a Locker instead; tests can pass a memory locker explicitly.

title: store, server: delete TaskApplier
body:
Removes `TaskApplier` and uses `store.Store` directly under the per-task lock in `internal/server/server.go`.

## Summary

- **Store contract & backends**:
  - Deleted `TaskApplier`, `TaskVersion`, `TaskKey`, `ApplyFunc`, `DeleteTaskVersion`, and normalization helpers (`internal/store/task_apply.go`, `internal/store/task_version_normalize.go`, `internal/store/memory/task_apply.go`, `internal/store/postgres/task_apply.go`).
  - Moved `store.StoredStatus` into `internal/store/store.go` (with unit tests in `internal/store/store_test.go`).
  - Simplified `MemoryStore.tasks` back to `map[string]*v1alpha1.Task` and dropped the `TASK_STATE_UNSPECIFIED -> TASK_STATE_QUEUED` coercion in `SaveTask` (memory and postgres) so saving a task after clearing `delete_time` preserves `TASK_STATE_UNSPECIFIED`.
  - Removed the unused `tasks.generation` `ALTER TABLE` from `internal/store/postgres/schema.sql`.
- **Server & wiring**:
  - Deleted `internal/server/task_applier.go`, `server.Options.TaskApplier`, and its wiring in `cmd/ax-server/main.go`.
  - Updated `CreateTask`, `DeleteTask`, `SuspendTask`, `ResumeTask`, `clearStoredTaskState`, `recordFailure`, and `deleteTask` to write through `saveTask`, `updateTask`, `getStoredTask`, and `s.store.DeleteTask`.
  - Updated `AGENTS.md` and `DESIGN.md`.

## Verification

- `make verify`
- `go build ./cmd/ax ./cmd/ax-server ./cmd/ax-runner`
- `go test ./...` (Postgres integration tests will run in CI)

Fixes #714

title: all: drop .gemini/skills and fix the CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md claim in AGENTS.md
body: Gemini CLI reads .agents/skills, so the .gemini/skills symlink looks redundant (only .claude/skills is needed, for Claude Code); remove it along with its references in AGENTS.md and .github/workflows/e2e.yml. AGENTS.md also says CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md are symlinks to it, but neither exists; add them or drop the sentence.

title: server: don't lock models in ApplyModel and DeleteModel
body: ApplyModel and DeleteModel (internal/server/server.go) take a "model" lock around a single store write, but a Model has no Substrate side effects to serialize, and ApplyModel reads the existing metadata before taking the lock anyway. Drop the lock and rely on the store.

title: store, server: delete TaskApplier
body:
AX is a simple CRUD system over Agent Substrate: Task/Actor provisioning and lifecycle are handled imperatively (under the per-task lock, returning Substrate failures directly to the client), while task execution is declarative. Because of that, we do not need a transactional `TaskApplier` state machine alongside `store.Store`.

This PR removes `TaskApplier` and has `internal/server/server.go` read and write tasks directly through `store.Store` under `s.locker.Lock`.

## Summary

- **Store contract & backends**:
  - Deleted `TaskApplier`, `TaskVersion`, `TaskKey`, `ApplyFunc`, `DeleteTaskVersion`, `PrepareTaskVersionForApply`, and `OverlayTaskGeneration` (`internal/store/task_apply.go`, `internal/store/task_version_normalize.go`, `internal/store/task_apply_test.go`, `internal/store/memory/task_apply.go`, `internal/store/postgres/task_apply.go`) and removed `TestTaskApplier*`.
  - Moved `store.StoredStatus` into `internal/store/store.go` with unit tests in `internal/store/store_test.go`.
  - Simplified `MemoryStore.tasks` back to `map[string]*v1alpha1.Task` and dropped the `TASK_STATE_UNSPECIFIED -> TASK_STATE_QUEUED` coercion in `SaveTask` (memory and postgres) so saving after clearing `metadata.delete_time` preserves `TASK_STATE_UNSPECIFIED`.
  - Removed the unused `tasks.generation` column migration from `internal/store/postgres/schema.sql`.
- **Server & wiring**:
  - Deleted `internal/server/task_applier.go`, `server.Options.TaskApplier`, and its wiring in `cmd/ax-server/main.go`.
  - Updated `CreateTask`, `DeleteTask`, `SuspendTask`, `ResumeTask`, `clearStoredTaskState`, `recordFailure`, and `deleteTask` to write through `saveTask`, `updateTask`, `getStoredTask`, and `s.store.DeleteTask`.
  - Replaced `failApplyTaskApplier` with a `store.Store` wrapper in `internal/server/server_test.go` and added `TestServer_ResumeAfterFailedDeleteClearsDeleteTime`.
- **Docs & contract**:
  - Updated `AGENTS.md` and `DESIGN.md`.

## Verification

- `make verify` (0 issues, no diff)
- `go build ./cmd/ax ./cmd/ax-server ./cmd/ax-runner`
- `go test ./...`
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/store/... ./internal/server/... ./cmd/ax-server/...`
- Tested with a local cluster
- Postgres integration tests in `internal/store/postgres` run in CI.

Fixes #714

title: runner: workspace setup through a Gateway fails TLS verification
body:
When ax-server pushes a Workspace for setup alone, runPushed (runner/runner.go) calls setupWorkspace without setDefaultEnv, so GIT_SSL_CAINFO and the other CA variables aren't pointed at the egress trust bundle. A Workspace that clones over HTTPS through spec.setup.gateway then fails with "server verification failed: certificate signer not trusted"; set the default env before setup as runTask does.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Apply a Gateway and a Workspace whose setup clones over HTTPS through it:

```yaml
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: github-gw
spec:
  egress:
    - https:
        hostnames: ["github.com"]
---
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Workspace
metadata:
  name: chalk-ws
spec:
  profile:
    image: "<runner image, pinned by digest>"
  setup:
    git:
      - repo: "https://github.com/chalk/chalk.git"
        depth: 1
    gateway:
      name: github-gw
```

```bash
ax apply -f repro.yaml
```

The Workspace fails to prepare:

```
Error: applying document 2: rpc error: code = FailedPrecondition desc = preparing workspace default/chalk-ws: running workspace setup: workspace setup failed: cloning https://github.com/chalk/chalk.git (ref main): git fetch: exit status 128
```

2. git's error in the worker log shows it verified against the system CA file, not `/run/ate/egress-trust-bundle/trust-bundle.pem`:

```bash
kubectl -n ate-workers logs deploy/ax-workers | grep -o 'fatal: unable to access[^\\]*' | sort -u
```

```
fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/chalk/chalk.git/': server verification failed: certificate signer not trusted. (CAfile: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt CRLfile: none)
```

3. A Task bound to the same Gateway works, because runTask calls setDefaultEnv:

```yaml
apiVersion: ax.io/v1alpha1
kind: Task
metadata:
  name: tls-probe
spec:
  profile:
    image: "<same runner image>"
  gateway:
    name: github-gw
  commands: ["sh", "-c", "echo GIT_SSL_CAINFO=$GIT_SSL_CAINFO; curl -sS -o /dev/null -w 'curl=%{http_code}\n' https://github.com"]
```

After `ax resume task tls-probe`, the worker log shows `GIT_SSL_CAINFO=/run/ate/egress-trust-bundle/trust-bundle.pem` and `curl=200`.

title: cli: rename ax apply to ax create
body:
Rename the `ax apply` subcommand to `ax create`.

## Why

We only allow creations and do not allow any mutations. The `apply` name borrows `kubectl apply` semantics (create-or-update reconciliation with `configured` / `unchanged` outcomes), which is misleading when AX resources are create-only.

## Scope

- Rename `ax apply` to `ax create` in `cmd/ax/main.go` (and help text / usage / tests).
- Remove update/mutation paths from the command (`UpdateGateway`, `UpdateModel`, and `applyOutcome`'s `configured`/`unchanged` logic) so `ax create` only creates resources.
- Update references across tests (`test/e2e`), scripts (`demo.sh`, `hack/hero-demo`, `Makefile`), examples, and docs (`README.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/*`, `pkg/apis/v1alpha1/ax.proto`).

title: hack/hero-demo: live steps hang because tasks never reach Completed since #688
body:
## Summary

`RUN_LIVE_STEPS=1 ./hack/hero-demo/run.sh` no longer works on `main`. Steps 3, 4 and 5 hang until they time out, although the work inside the sandboxes finishes. The dry run (without `RUN_LIVE_STEPS`) still passes, so CI does not notice.

## Root cause

#688 (2ede873, "push tasks to runners and remove the runner pull protocol") removed the path by which ax-server learned that a task's command had exited:

- `runner.Config.OnCommandExit` (`runner/runner.go`) is never set by `cmd/ax-runner`, so the exit code is only logged.
- Nothing in `internal/server` or `internal/controller` moves a task to `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` (or to `FAILED` on a non-zero exit) any more, and `status.outcome` (exit code, output) is never filled in.
- The #688 commit message acknowledges this: it removed `TestE2E_PureImageLauncher` and `TestE2E_PrewarmAndCustomImageSharedWorkspace` because "those tasks stay Working and both tests timed out".

`finish_task` in `hack/hero-demo/run.sh` (#671) waits for `ax describe task` to report `Completed` or `Failed` with `Output:`, so it never returns.

Reproduced on an `ax local` cluster at 775f5ad: the starter agent finished (it edited `math_utils.py` and wrote `/workspace/.ax/output`), and the runner logged `task command completed successfully`, but `ax describe task hero-demo-starter-task` still shows `State: Working` with no outcome.

## Related problems found along the way

1. **`launcher-done` marker cannot be written.** After a successful launcher run the runner logs:
   ```
   failed to record that the launcher finished path=/workspace/.ax/launcher-done error="open /workspace/.ax/launcher-done: permission denied"
   ```
   ax-runner runs as root without `CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE` in the sandbox, and `/workspace/.ax` is owned by UID 1000 with mode 0755 (`ensureWritableForUser` / `chownTree`). As a result, a resumed starter task re-runs its one-shot agent (`launcherCommand` in `runner/launcher.go`).
2. **Missing Gateway credential gives an unhelpful failure.** On a fresh cluster without the `hero-demo-gemini` Secret, the agent gets `403 egress denied` from the Gemini API and exits with empty output. The task still shows `Working` / `Ready=True TaskRunning`, so nothing tells the user that the run failed.

title: runner: set $AX_WORKSPACE to the workspace path so tasks stop hardcoding /workspace
body:
## Summary

Task commands, launchers and `Workspace.spec.setup` commands have no supported way to learn where the workspace is. The path is configurable (`Task.spec.workspace.path`, default `/workspace`), but nothing in the environment tells the command what it is, so manifests, harnesses and images hardcode `/workspace`. AX should set **`$AX_WORKSPACE`** to the absolute workspace path in every process it starts in the sandbox, document it as part of the runner contract, and switch our own manifests and docs to use it.

## Current behavior

- `TaskSpec.WorkspacePath()` (`pkg/apis/v1alpha1/types.go`) returns `spec.workspace.path` or `DefaultWorkspacePath` (`/workspace`), and the runner uses it as the command's working directory (`taskWorkspacePath` in `runner/runner.go`).
- `commandEnv` (`runner/runner.go`) passes only the runner's environment, `AX_METADATA_URL`, the launcher files (`AX_GOAL_FILE`, `AX_CONFIG_FILE`, `AX_MCP_CONFIG_FILE`, `AX_SESSION_FILE`, `AX_OUTPUT_FILE`) and `spec.env`. There is no variable for the workspace path.
- `spec.setup` commands (`internal/workspace/setup.go`) run with `sh -c` and get no workspace variable either.
- The working directory is the only signal, and it is unreliable: a command that `cd`s elsewhere, a launcher that changes `HOME`, or a subprocess started from another directory loses it. Even `AX_OUTPUT_FILE` (`<workspace>/.ax/output`) has to be parsed to recover the path.

## Where `/workspace` is hardcoded today

- `hack/hero-demo/workspace.yaml`, `task-custom.yaml`, `task-starter.yaml` (setup commands write to `/workspace/app`, the custom task tests `/workspace/first-run` and runs `unittest -s /workspace/app`, the goal text names `/workspace/app/math_utils.py`), and `run.sh` (`/workspace/.ax/output`, `/workspace/.ax/exit-code`, `/workspace/first-run`).
- `examples/simple.yaml`, `docs/manifests.md` (for example `args: ["--repo", "/workspace"]` for an MCP server, `path: "/workspace/.ax/skills"`), `docs/runner.md`, `docs/sandbox.md`, `docs/concepts.md`, `docs/local_installer.md`.
- Starter images: `ax-harness` in `ghcr.io/agentexecutor/antigravity` derives the workspace from `$PWD` (`${PWD}/.ax/sessions/...`, `${PWD}/.ax/bin`), which breaks as soon as it is started from another directory.

A Task that sets `spec.workspace.path: /src` silently breaks every one of these.

## What needs to be done

- [ ] **Runner:** set `AX_WORKSPACE=<absolute workspace path>` (the value of `taskWorkspacePath(task)`) in `commandEnv`, so it reaches `spec.commands` and the image launcher. Add a constant next to `OutputFileEnv` in `runner/launcher.go` (for example `WorkspaceEnv = "AX_WORKSPACE"`).
- [ ] **Workspace setup:** set the same variable for `Workspace.spec.setup` commands and git clones (`internal/workspace/setup.go`), both in the setup actor (`/runner/v1alpha1/setup`) and in a task that runs setup itself at a non-default path.
- [ ] **Guest services:** set it in processes started through `ax ssh` (`internal/guest`, `internal/metadata`), so `ax ssh <task> -- ls "$AX_WORKSPACE"` works.
- [ ] **Precedence:** decide whether a user's `spec.env` may override `AX_WORKSPACE` (probably not; reject it in `internal/apivalidation` like other reserved `AX_*` names, if there is such a list).
- [ ] **Metadata endpoint:** consider exposing the path from the metadata server too, for agents that read the task from `AX_METADATA_URL` rather than the environment.
- [ ] **Docs:** document `AX_WORKSPACE` in `docs/runner.md` (launcher contract) and `docs/manifests.md` (`spec.workspace`, `spec.setup`, `spec.commands`), and replace hardcoded `/workspace` in examples with `$AX_WORKSPACE` where a shell expands it. `DefaultWorkspacePath` stays the default mount point.
- [ ] **Our manifests:** update `hack/hero-demo/*` and `examples/*` to use `$AX_WORKSPACE`, and make `run.sh` read paths relative to `$AX_WORKSPACE` inside the sandbox.
- [ ] **Starter images:** ask the `agentexecutor/images` owners to have `ax-harness` prefer `$AX_WORKSPACE` over `$PWD`.
- [ ] **Tests:** unit test in `runner/runner_test.go` that the command sees `AX_WORKSPACE` for both the default path and a custom `spec.workspace.path`; same for setup commands in `internal/workspace`.

## Non-goals

- Changing the default mount point (`/workspace`) or the snapshot rules for non-default paths.

title: fix(runner): set the default environment at startup, not in runTask
body:
The runner now sets its default environment when it starts instead of in `runTask`, which a runner that only sets up a Workspace never reaches. Fixes #720.

- `Run` calls `setDefaultEnv` before it takes any work; the call in `runTask` is gone.
- `setDefaultEnv` no longer takes the task: a task's `spec.env` is applied later and overrides the defaults.
- `TestRun_AwaitPushSetsUpPushedWorkspace` checks the CA variable and `GIT_ASKPASS` from a setup command.

title: api: validate manifests with k8s declarative validation
body:
Manifest validation is hand-written in `internal/apivalidation`: each rule is Go code plus test rows, kept apart from the field it checks. Agent Substrate uses Kubernetes declarative validation instead: most of its rules are `+k8s:` tags on the proto fields, and `validation-gen` generates the checks ([guide](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/blob/main/docs/api-validation.md)).

Why change it:

- A simple rule (required, name format, range, list size) becomes one line next to the field. Many input fields have no check today, for example `metadata.labels`, `spec.env`, `spec.commands`, and the MCP and Model fields, and no list has a size limit.
- Gateway egress rules are Substrate's types and already carry its tags, so the rules Substrate declares that way can be generated instead of copied by hand (`TODO: Validate everything that Substrate validates` in `ValidateGateway`).
- A request gets every problem back with its field path, not only the first one.

Proposal: declare validation rules as tags in the `.proto` files and generate the checks with `validation-gen`. Rules a tag cannot express stay hand-written.

Error messages change format, and their field paths use proto names (`ate_template`, not `ateTemplate`).

Related:

- agent-substrate/substrate#3821: the `validation-gen` changes this needs ship in Kubernetes 1.38.
- kubernetes/kubernetes#144385: proposes a small `k8s.io/validation` module for the library the generated code imports.

title: cli: ax apply with multiple -f flags silently ignores all files after the first
examples/workerpool.yaml: 1 CPU / 1 GiB worker limit is too small for agent tasks
body:
## Summary

Following the quick start on GKE with `examples/workerpool.yaml` (`limits: cpu: "1", memory: "1Gi"`) fails to schedule coding-agent tasks (for example a `2 CPU`, `4 GiB` Antigravity task) with `no worker has room for the actor`.

## Observed behavior on `v0.4.0-rc.1` / Substrate `v1.0.0`

When scheduling a `2 CPU`, `4 GiB` task on a GKE `WorkerPool`:

| Worker `limits` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `1 CPU, 1 GiB` (`examples/workerpool.yaml`) | `no worker has room for the actor` |
| `2 CPU, 4 GiB` | `no worker has room for the actor` |
| `3 CPU, 4 GiB` | `no worker has room for the actor` |
| `2 CPU, 6 GiB` | Runs |
| `3 CPU, 5 GiB` | Runs |

A worker needs memory headroom above the task's `spec.profile.resources.limits.memory`.

## Suggested fix

Raise the default resource limits in `examples/workerpool.yaml` (or document the sizing headroom directly in the file comment and quick start) so first-time users running real agent tasks do not immediately hit `no worker has room for the actor`.

title: server: fetchGateway and fetchWorkspace silently drop store errors
body:
`fetchGateway` and `fetchWorkspace` in `internal/server/server.go` return `nil` for **any** store error, not only `store.ErrNotFound`:

```go
gw, err := s.store.GetGateway(ctx, atespace, name)
if err != nil {
	return nil
}
```

Both are used by `SuspendTask` and `ResumeTask` to load the task's bindings before calling `reconciler.Suspend` / `reconciler.Resume`.

## Why it matters

A transient store failure (for example, Postgres unavailable or a context deadline) is swallowed and treated as "the Gateway does not exist":

- If the actor has no EgressPolicy yet, `bindGateway` (`internal/controller/reconciler.go`) reports `gateway "<name>": not available in atespace "<atespace>"` with reason `GatewayBindingFailed`. That error is not a Substrate transient error, so `recordFailure` stores the task as `Failed` instead of `Queued` and the client gets `Internal` instead of `Unavailable`. The real cause never appears in logs or in the task's status.
- `fetchWorkspace` has the same pattern: a store error makes the reconciler proceed as if the task had no Workspace.

By contrast, `CreateTask` distinguishes `store.ErrNotFound` (`FailedPrecondition`) from other errors (`Internal`) when loading the same resources.

## Suggested fix

Return the error from both helpers, map `store.ErrNotFound` to `nil` (or a `FailedPrecondition`), and surface any other error from `SuspendTask` / `ResumeTask` as `codes.Internal` (or `Unavailable`) without touching the actor. Add a test with a store wrapper whose `GetGateway` / `GetWorkspace` fails.

title: controller: rename TaskReconciler to TaskManager
body:
TaskReconciler no longer runs a reconcile loop; ax-server calls it directly to provision, suspend, resume, and delete task actors. This renames it to TaskManager (and reconciler.go to task.go) to sit alongside WorkspaceManager. No behavior change.

Fixes #713

title: api: align TaskState with Substrate ActorState
body:
Fixes #708.

`TaskState` used to rename and collapse Substrate's `ActorState` on read (`RUNNING` → `WORKING`, `RESUMING`/`REVERTING` → `QUEUED`, `CRASHED` → `FAILED`, `DELETING` → `UNSPECIFIED`) and defined AX-only states that nothing set. This PR makes `TaskState` mirror `ActorState` and keeps only the AX states that current behavior needs.

## API (`pkg/apis/v1alpha1/task.proto`)

| # | TaskState | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 1–7 | `RESUMING`, `RUNNING`, `SUSPENDING`, `SUSPENDED`, `CRASHED`, `DELETING`, `REVERTING` | The actor's state; same names and numbers as `ActorState` |
| 8–199 | reserved | For `ActorState` values Substrate may add |
| 200 | `QUEUED` | Stored: actor not provisioned yet (until #698) |
| 201 | `FAILED` | Stored: provisioning or resume failed, or the actor is missing (until #695/#698) |
| 202 | `COMPLETED` | Reserved, `TODO(#690)`; nothing sets it yet |

`IDLE`, `REQUIRES_ACTION`, `WORKING` and `CANCELLED` are removed.

**Breaking:** enum numbers changed. Stored tasks are protojson, so states are stored by name, and the stored names `QUEUED` and `FAILED` are unchanged.

## Server and CLI

- `actorTaskState` maps each `ActorState` to the `TaskState` of the same name.
- `IsAXTaskState` covers `QUEUED`, `FAILED` and `COMPLETED`. `FormatTaskState` prints `Running`, `Crashed`, `Deleting`, and so on.
- `isExecutionTerminal` is removed: it checked `COMPLETED`, `CANCELLED` and `FAILED` with an outcome, none of which the server sets.
- `ax ssh` requires the task to be `Running`.
- New `TestActorTaskStateMirrorsActorState` fails if the enums drift apart or an AX-only state goes below 200. `TestStoredStatus` covers every `IsAXTaskState` state.

## Docs

`docs/concepts.md`, `docs/local_installer.md` and `README.md` use the new state names.

## Not in this PR

The hero demo (`hack/hero-demo/`) still waits for a `Completed` state that nothing sets. Its fix moves to #722, together with the runner's `launcher-done` permission fix.

## Testing

- `make verify`, `go build ./cmd/ax ./cmd/ax-server ./cmd/ax-runner` and `go test ./...` pass.
- E2E not run locally.

title: docs: explain how AX relates to Agent Substrate
body:
Fixes #724.

Adds a short **AX and Agent Substrate** section at the bottom of the README:

- Agent Substrate is the compute runtime layer AX relies on (scheduling, isolation, suspend/resume, snapshots).
- Besides task execution, AX and Agent Substrate are orthogonal projects.
- AX aims to grow into an agentic platform covering session management, memory, multi-task coordination, input steering, registries, models, and trajectory collection, built at Google as a portable platform that runs inside Google, on customer clusters, and on-prem.

Docs only.

title: install: add a liveness probe to the Envoy sidecars of Substrate
body:
Fixes #697

## Root cause:
`ax local start` only re-applies unchanged manifests, which creates no new pod, and then waits on the stuck one. 

https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/issues/3601
The root cause is on substrate end. When only the atenet-router container restarts (the kubelet restarts single containers, not pods), the router's shutdown sequence has already told Envoy to fail its health check (POST /healthcheck/fail). The new router process never undoes that, and Envoy itself never restarted, so it reports DRAINING and 503 on /ready forever. Kubernetes does not repair it: the envoy container has a readiness probe but no liveness probe, and a Deployment does not replace a pod for being unready. atenet-egress has the same problem.

## Fix on Ax
1. Adds a liveness probe on /ready to the envoy container of atenet-router and atenet-egress when it renders the Substrate manifests (RenderSystemBundle, new RenderEgressBundle). The kubelet then restarts a drained Envoy by itself, with no need to run ax local start again. A container that already has a liveness probe keeps it, so this steps aside once Substrate ships its own.
2. Rollout errors name the pod and container that is running but not ready, and print the `kubectl rollout` restart commands.

The probe is ·initialDelaySeconds: 30, periodSeconds: 10, failureThreshold: 6·: Envoy is restarted after 60 seconds of 503. Envoy also answers 503 while it starts, and the window leaves it time for that.

## Test
```
1. kill atenet-router to trigger container recreation
➜  ax git:(fix-697-stuck-rollout) ✗ docker exec $N pkill -TERM -f 'router --mode=ingress'

2. envoy container is not ready
➜  ax git:(fix-697-stuck-rollout) ✗ kubectl --context $C -n ate-system get pod -l app=atenet-router
NAME                             READY   STATUS    RESTARTS        AGE
atenet-router-58db677747-czjsc   1/2     Running   3 (2m19s ago)   72m

3. watch the killing event
➜  ax git:(fix-697-stuck-rollout) ✗ kubectl -n ate-system get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | grep -E 'liveness|Killing'
12m         Normal    Killing     pod/atenet-router-54bb6c897f-vpgvg   Container envoy failed liveness probe, will be restarted

4. both router and envoy sidecar are back to running after restart
➜  ax git:(fix-697-stuck-rollout) ✗ kubectl -n ate-system get pod -l app=atenet-router -w
NAME                             READY   STATUS    RESTARTS      AGE
atenet-router-54bb6c897f-vpgvg   2/2     Running   4 (11m ago)   73m
```

title: fix(server): return store errors on suspend and resume
body:
`SuspendTask` and `ResumeTask` now fail when the store cannot read the task's Workspace or Gateway, instead of treating it as missing. Fixes #729.

- `fetchWorkspace` and `fetchGateway` return the store's error as `Internal`, and both handlers return it before they call the task manager. A Workspace or Gateway that does not exist is still nil.
- A task that has its Gateway's rules can no longer be suspended or resumed while the Gateway cannot be read. A deleted Gateway still does not affect it.
- `TestServer_ResumeAndSuspendWithUnreadableGateway` becomes `TestServer_ResumeAndSuspendWithStoreError` and checks the new behaviour.

Known pre-existing issue: `ensureSubstrateResources` in `internal/controller/task.go` drops the store's error when it reads a Workspace's setup Gateway.

title: hack/hero-demo: detect task completion inside the sandbox
body:
Fixes #722.

`RUN_LIVE_STEPS=1 ./hack/hero-demo/run.sh` hung in Steps 3, 4 and 5:
`finish_task` waited for `ax describe task` to report `Completed` or
`Failed` with `Output:`, but since #688 nothing sets either, and
`COMPLETED` is reserved until #690. Tasks stay `Running` with no
`status.outcome` after their command exits.

This change only touches `hack/hero-demo/`.

## Manifests

- `task-starter.yaml` sets `spec.commands` to a wrapper around the
  image's launcher (`/usr/local/bin/ax-launcher`, or `ax-harness` on
  images from before the rename). Commands still get the goal, config,
  MCP and session files of the launcher contract. The wrapper writes the
  launcher's exit status to `/workspace/.ax/hero-demo-exit-code`, and
  does not run the agent again once a status is recorded. This also
  avoids depending on the runner's `launcher-done` marker, which the
  runner cannot write (root without `CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE` in a UID
  1000-owned `/workspace/.ax`).
- `task-custom.yaml` writes the unit test output to `$AX_OUTPUT_FILE`
  and its exit status to the same file.

## run.sh

- `finish_task` waits for the exit-code file over `ax ssh` (both tasks
  set `spec.debug`), fails on a non-zero status and shows the end of the
  output, and fails when `/workspace/.ax/output` is empty.
- `ax ssh` calls take the global ax flags, so Step 5 reads the sandbox
  on `--context <remote>`.
- Steps 3 and 5 fail fast when `kubectl` reports the `hero-demo-gemini`
  Secret as NotFound, or the Secret lacks the `ax.io/credential=true`
  label, instead of the agent getting `403 egress denied` while the task
  reads `Running`.
- Comments and the README no longer say a finished task refuses
  suspend/resume.

## Not in this PR

- The runner's `launcher-done` permission bug, which still makes a
  resumed task without `spec.commands` run its launcher again: #740.
- Reporting completion from AX itself (#690).

## Testing

- `RUN_LIVE_STEPS=1 AX_TIMEOUT=300 ./hack/hero-demo/run.sh` on an
  `ax local` cluster built from `33b93cf`: Step 2 and Step 4 PASS, Step 3
  runs the agent to completion (it added `subtract` and its test, exit
  status 0, output written); Steps 1, 3 and 5 report their existing STUBs.
- The dry run (no `RUN_LIVE_STEPS`) is unchanged.
- With a fake `ax` CLI: agent failure, empty output, missing Secret,
  failing unit tests, and Step 5 with `--context` each give the expected
  scoreboard line.

title: runner: launcher-done marker fails with permission denied
body:
Split out from #722 before #738 closes it.

After a successful auto-launcher run, `markLauncherDone` logs:

```text
failed to record that the launcher finished path=/workspace/.ax/launcher-done error="open /workspace/.ax/launcher-done: permission denied"
```

`ax-runner` runs as root without `CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE`, and `/workspace/.ax` is owned by UID 1000 with mode `0755` after `ensureWritableForUser` drops permissions. As a result, a resumed starter task re-runs its one-shot agent.

Code path: `markLauncherDone` in `runner/launcher.go` (called from `runner/runner.go`).

title: runner: reply to a push only when the pushed work is complete, and delete the pushes channel
body:
## Today

ax-server hands work to a runner in two steps.

1. It POSTs a Task to `/runner/v1alpha1/task`, or a Workspace to `/runner/v1alpha1/setup` (`pushToRunner` in `internal/controller/actorhttp.go`). The handler in `internal/metadata/server.go` (`handleTaskPush`, `handleSetupPush`) puts the work on an internal channel, `pushes`, and replies `202` at once.
2. `runPushed` in `runner/runner.go` receives the work from `Pushes()`, sets up the workspace and starts the task, and records the result with `SetWorkspaceCheckReady` or `SetSetupFailed`. ax-server learns the result by polling `GET /readyz?check=workspace` every 500 ms (`waitWorkspaceReady`): `503` while the work is pending, `200` once it is done, and `500` with the reason when it failed.

So the reply to a push says only that the work was queued. Its result travels through a second endpoint, and through extra state in the metadata server.

## Proposal

A push should not return until the pushed work is complete: the workspace is set up and, for a task, its command has started. The reply is the result: `200` on success and `500` with the reason on failure, with `409` and `400` as they are today.

The metadata server then has no work to queue:

- Delete the `pushes` channel, `Pushes()` and the `Push` type. The handler runs the work itself, through a function the runner gives the server, or the runner serves these two endpoints.
- `runPushed` loses its receive loop.
- ax-server stops polling `/readyz?check=workspace` after a push. `waitWorkspaceReady` can go, and so can `workspaceCheckReady`, `setupFailure`, `SetWorkspaceCheckReady` and `SetSetupFailed` in the metadata server, if nothing else needs them.

## To decide

- **Timeouts.** ax-server's HTTP client for these calls times out after 2 seconds (`newProbeHTTPClient` in `internal/controller/task.go`). `Resume` waits `WorkspaceReadyTimeout`, 15 seconds by default, and does not treat a runner that is still setting up as an error. Workspace setup can take minutes (git clones, `setup.commands`). A push that blocks needs a longer request timeout, and `Resume` needs a rule for a push that outlives its wait. Check also whether `atenet-router` limits how long a request may take.
- **Repeated pushes.** ax-server retries a push until the runner answers, and pushes the task again on every resume. A push of work that is still in progress should wait for that work's result, not answer `200` at once.
- **The runner contract.** `docs/runner.md` documents the `202` reply and the `/readyz?check=workspace` polling for custom runners, so it changes with this.
- **`assignmentCh`.** The metadata server also holds a guest gRPC call for up to 10 seconds until a task is assigned. Check whether that is still needed once a resume returns only after the push is complete.

Related: #688 (the push protocol), #739 (its other follow-ups).

title: Tasks should be upgradable
body: Running Tasks can't be upgraded today; changing a Task's spec (e.g. image or runner version) means deleting and recreating it, which loses its state. AX should support upgrading a Task in place, so a suspended or running Task picks up the new spec and keeps its workspace.

title: runner, server: report COMPLETED and FAILED from the status file (#690)
body:
Updates #690 for `COMPLETED` and `FAILED`; `REQUIRES_ACTION` is not handled yet.

A task's command now says how the task ended by writing one JSON object, at most 16 KiB, to `$AX_STATUS_FILE` (`<workspace>/.ax/status`):

```json
{"state": "COMPLETED", "message": "...", "output": "..."}
```

**Runner**
- Exports `AX_STATUS_FILE` to the command and creates `<workspace>/.ax`.
- Serves the file on `GET /runner/v1alpha1/status`, reading it on each request; the runner keeps no status in memory.
- A file that can't be read, isn't JSON, is over 16 KiB or has an unknown state is served as `FAILED` with the error. With no file, the task has not ended.
- The exit status is not a report. A command that exits without writing the file leaves the task `Running`.
- Removes `AX_OUTPUT_FILE`; `output` in the status file replaces it.
- Push endpoints are always served (`AcceptPushes` removed).

**ax-server**
- `Server.ObserveStatus` (`internal/server/observe.go`) runs every 5 s. It lists running actors and asks each runner whose task has no stored state, 16 at a time. It stores the first `COMPLETED`/`FAILED` under the task lock: `status.state`, `status.outcome.output`, and `Ready=False` with `TaskCompleted`/`TaskFailed`.
- `GetTask`/`ListTasks` never call the runner.
- `COMPLETED` and `FAILED` stay through suspend and resume.
- `substrate.Client.ListActors` takes optional states and filters client-side, since Substrate's `ListActors` has no state filter.
- `ax ssh` also connects to a task that has an outcome.

**Docs**: `DESIGN.md`, `docs/{runner,manifests,concepts,observability}.md`, `skills/substrate/SKILL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `hack/hero-demo` (output file removed).

Follow-up: #741.

### Testing
- `make verify`, `go build ./cmd/ax ./cmd/ax-server ./cmd/ax-runner`, `go test ./...`
- **Not run**: E2E, the Postgres tier, `make test-local-install`. None of this has run in a real sandbox yet.

title: server: taskSpecMatchesExisting is not needed
body: CreateTask calls `taskSpecMatchesExisting` (internal/server/server.go) when it retries a Queued task that has no template yet, but it then replaces the incoming task with the stored one (`task = existing`), so the incoming spec is never used. We can drop the check and treat the retry as idempotent, or let the retry overwrite the spec since nothing has been provisioned yet.

title: Consider returning the actor transparently from CreateTask
body: CreateTask wraps everything in a Task, so the underlying Substrate actor is hidden behind AX's own status fields. Consider returning the actor transparently (e.g. as a field on the response) instead of mapping all of its state into Task.

title: ci: run the hero demo
body:
CI does not run `hack/hero-demo/run.sh`.  Nobody noticed it is broken until it was run by hand (#722). #690 will change how the demo detects completion again.

Proposal: run the demo's live steps in CI on pull requests, with a antigravity starter image (or fake agent so that no API key is needed?) . 

Follow-up to https://github.com/google/ax/pull/731#discussion_r4673551382.

Related: #722, #690, #739.

title: Reconsider AX recording whether a task completed or failed
body: Draft PR #743 has AX record a task as Completed or Failed from a status file its agent writes, and it shows how complicated collecting that signal is. AX has to poll every running task's runner through atenet-router, keep a working queue of the tasks whose end is not recorded yet, avoid resuming suspended actors, and run a separate single-replica observer to do it. Most sophisticated tasks will bring their own communication protocol for these events, such as a task API that reports progress, results and failures to their own systems. Those protocols carry far more than COMPLETED or FAILED, and AX's copy of the outcome would be a second, coarser source of truth. Should AX stay out of judging how a task ended, and leave it to the task's own protocol?

title: server: simplify CreateTask retries and model handlers
body:
Fixes #744. Fixes #718.

- `CreateTask` drops `taskSpecMatchesExisting`. A retry of a Queued task with no template runs the stored task and ignores the incoming spec, because the actor may already exist from the stored spec (`TaskManager.Suspend` restores the previous status when `SuspendActor` fails). Re-applying a Queued task with a different spec used to fail with `FailedPrecondition`; it now retries the stored task. Already provisioned tasks are still rejected as immutable.
- `UpdateModel` and `DeleteModel` no longer take the `model` lock. A Model has no Substrate side effects, and `UpdateModel` read the existing metadata before taking the lock anyway.
- `DeleteModel` no longer reads the model before deleting it. The store's `DeleteModel` (memory and Postgres) now returns `store.ErrNotFound` when nothing is deleted, which the handler maps to `NotFound`. Deleting tasks, workspaces and gateways is unchanged.
- Tests: step 2 of `TestServer_TransientSubstrateUnavailableRecovery` checks that a retry keeps the stored spec, and a new `TestDeleteModel` in both store packages covers deleting a missing model.

`make verify`, `go build`, `go test ./...` and the Postgres store tests (`postgres:17-alpine`) pass locally.

title: server: clean up internal/server and cmd/ax-server
body:
Findings from a review of `internal/server` and `cmd/ax-server`.

## Bugs

- `-template` and `-template-atespace` are dead: `TaskManager` stores `defaultTemplate`/`defaultTemplateAtespace` (`internal/controller/task.go`) but never reads them. Remove the flags, the startup log field, the `NewTaskManager` parameters, and the args in `deploy/ax-server.yaml`, `deploy/embed.go`, and `test/e2e/manifests/ax-server.yaml`.
- `UpdateModel` treats any store error in its `defaultMetadata` callback as "not found", so a transient read error on an existing model assigns it a new uid and createTime. Only `store.ErrNotFound` should mean create; other errors should return `Internal`.
- `recordFailure` ignores the `updateTask` error (`_ = s.updateTask(...)`), so a failed write can leave a stale stored state without a log line.

## Duplication

- The four List handlers unpack the request by hand; `pageStart(req.GetAtespace(), req.GetPageSize(), req.GetPageToken())` is enough because proto getters are nil-safe.
- `DeleteTask`, `SuspendTask`, and `ResumeTask` repeat the same lock, `getStoredTask`, and NotFound/Internal mapping; a `lockStoredTask` helper would remove it.
- Mapping Substrate errors to `Unavailable` (transient) or `Internal` is written out in `SuspendTask`, `recordFailure`, `DeleteWorkspace`, and `prepareWorkspace`, with another variant in `deleteTask`.
- `defaultMetadata` takes a callback that `saveGateway` ignores the arguments of, `CreateWorkspace` passes as nil, and `UpdateModel` uses to hide the bug above. Pass the previous `*ObjectMeta` directly.
- `DeleteGateway` reads the gateway before deleting it; let the store's `DeleteGateway` return `store.ErrNotFound`, as `DeleteModel` now does. Keep its lock, which orders deletes against `saveGateway`'s check-then-create.

## Small things

- `gateway.go` hard-codes `"default"` three times instead of `v1alpha1.DefaultAtespace`.
- Redundant defaulting: `clearStoredTaskState` re-defaults the atespace, `DeleteTask` checks for nil metadata, `SuspendTask`/`ResumeTask` nil-check `task.Status` (the task manager already does), and `CreateTask` handles a nil `task.Spec` after validation.
- `getStoredTask` is a one-line wrapper meant to keep handlers off `s.store` for tasks, but `deleteTask`, `listTasks`, and `CreateTask` call the store directly anyway. Enforce the rule or drop the wrapper.
- `ListModels` and `ListGateways` load every row and slice in memory, while tasks and workspaces page in the store.
- `cmd/ax-server`: the API `http.Server` has no `ReadHeaderTimeout` (the metrics server does); `err != http.ErrServerClosed` should use `errors.Is`; the `ADDR` env var is unprefixed unlike `AX_STORE`/`AX_RUNNER_VOLUME_IMAGE` and missing from the `-addr` help; `os.Exit` in the serve goroutines skips the deferred telemetry flush.
- Comments: the doubled `// --- gRPC AXServer implementation ---` / `// --- Tasks ---` header; `SuspendTask` does not use `recordFailure` like `ResumeTask` does, which is probably intended (a failed suspend should not fail the task) but should be stated.

## To investigate

- `DeleteWorkspace` does not check for tasks that still bind the Workspace, and `fetchWorkspace` turns NotFound into nil, so a task relying on its Workspace's profile would resume with an empty profile. Not verified what template resolution does then.

title: server: fix bugs and remove duplication from #749
body:
Part of #749: the bugs and the duplication. The small things are left for a follow-up. Stacked on #748; once it merges, this PR retargets to `main`.

## Bugs

- `-template` and `-template-atespace` are removed: `TaskManager` stored them but never read them. This also removes them from `NewTaskManager`, the `deploy/ax-server.yaml` args, the namespace rewrite in `deploy/embed.go`, and `test/e2e/manifests/ax-server.yaml`. A new `ax-server` started with an old manifest that still passes `--template` fails with "flag provided but not defined"; manifests rendered by the matching CLI are fine.
- `UpdateModel` treats only `store.ErrNotFound` as a new model. Before, any store error gave an existing model a new uid and createTime. `TestUpdateModel_StoreError` covers it.
- `recordFailure` logs a failed status write instead of ignoring it.

## Duplication

- `lockStoredTask` replaces the lock, load, and NotFound/Internal mapping copied into `DeleteTask`, `SuspendTask`, and `ResumeTask`.
- `substrateError` maps a Substrate error to `Unavailable` (transient) or `Internal` for `SuspendTask`, `recordFailure`, and `DeleteWorkspace`. `deleteTask` (passes Substrate's gRPC codes through) and `prepareWorkspace` (`FailedPrecondition` with the setup error) keep their own mapping.
- `defaultMetadata(meta, prev)` takes the stored metadata instead of a callback.
- `atespaceOrDefault` replaces the repeated defaulting, including the three hard-coded `"default"` in `gateway.go`.
- The List handlers read the request with nil-safe getters.

`DeleteGateway` still reads the gateway before deleting it; the store is unchanged.

`make verify`, `go build`, and `go test ./...` pass locally. The E2E and local install tiers were not run.

title: api: embed ateapi.v1.Actor in TaskStatus
body: Replace the flattened `status.actor` and `status.actorUid` strings in `TaskStatus` with an `ateapi.v1.Actor actor` field, still read live from Substrate and never stored. All task RPCs keep returning `Task`, and `TaskManager.Suspend`/`Resume` can fill it from the actor they already have instead of a second `GetActor` call.

title: hack: add a basic tour of features
body:
Adds `hack/tour.sh`, a guided tour of AX against the AX server of the current kube context. It prints each command before running it, waits for task state changes, and deletes everything it created on exit.

Steps:
0. Where AX runs: the current context and the runner image.
1. The smallest Task: apply, resume, and inspect a minimal Task.
2. A Gateway: the only way out of a sandbox.
3. A Workspace with git, inline files, and commands setup, prepared once, snapshotted, and reused by every task.
4. Bring your own agent: a stand-in agent that reads its goal, config, and MCP servers through the launcher contract.
5. Suspend and resume, with progress kept in the workspace.
6. Tasks are immutable: updating a Task's spec is rejected.
7. Fan out: two tasks from one workspace snapshot, each with its own isolated copy.
8. An agent on the Gemini API SDK (`gemini-4-hydrogen`) whose API key the Gateway injects, so the key never enters the sandbox. Skipped when `GEMINI_API_KEY` is unset.
9. Atespaces: the same Task name in separate tenants.
10. Models: create, update in place, and delete.

Usage: run `make build-local-cluster`, then `./hack/tour.sh`.
- `AX_TASK_IMAGE` defaults to the ax-runner image in `bin/ax-runner.digest` on `localhost:5001`.
- `TOUR_PAUSE=1` waits for Enter between steps, for presenting.
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` enables step 8. The tour stores it in Secret `default/tour-gemini-key`.
- `TOUR_TIMEOUT` sets the seconds to wait for a task state change (default 180).

Also:
- `hack/build-local-cluster.sh` passes the runner volume image it builds to `ax local start --runner-volume-image`, so prebuilt agent images without a runner, such as Antigravity's, run on the local cluster.
- `AGENTS.md` lists `tour.sh` under `hack/`.

title: ax local: atenet-router stays unready after its container restarts
body:
On the local cluster (`ax local start`, Kind), new workspaces stay in `Preparing` forever after Substrate's `atenet-router` container restarts once. Its Envoy sidecar is left in the `DRAINING` state, so the pod never becomes ready again and the `atenet-router` Service has no endpoints until someone restarts the pod. It has happened several times; this report is from one occurrence, and it is likely a Substrate bug that `ax local` hits often.

## Symptoms

- `ax get workspaces` shows new workspaces stuck in `Preparing`, and `ax describe workspace` shows no conditions. Tasks that need a fresh setup hang the same way.
- ax-server keeps retrying setup with a new actor, and every push times out:
  ```
  workspace setup attempt failed, retrying with a fresh setup actor ... error: running workspace setup: pushing /runner/v1alpha1/setup to actor default/ax-ws-setup-...: context deadline exceeded (last error: Post "https://atenet-router.ate-system.svc.cluster.local:443/runner/v1alpha1/setup": context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers))
  ```
- `kubectl -n ate-system get pods` shows `atenet-router` at `1/2` with 1 restart; `envoy` is the container that is not ready, and it has 0 restarts.
- `kubectl -n ate-system get endpoints atenet-router` is empty.
- The `envoy` readiness probe (`GET :9901/ready`) returns 503 with body `DRAINING`. `/server_info` reports `state: DRAINING` and `/stats` has `server.state: 1`. The new `atenet-router` container logs `Router dataplane health check failed ... unexpected status code 503` every second, indefinitely.
- Connections opened before the restart (e.g. a long-lived `ax ssh` stream) keep working, which hides the problem until something opens a new connection.

## What happened (timeline, UTC)

1. 09:16–09:20: the whole node stalled. The router's health checks against the ATE API, the Kubernetes API (`https://10.96.0.1:443/version`) and Envoy (`localhost:9901/ready`) all time out. Around the same time, `postgres-0` (09:16:57) and `ate-idp-server` (09:20:39) in `ate-system` also exit and restart, and Postgres logs `terminating connection due to administrator command (SQLSTATE 57P01)`.
2. 09:20:36: the `atenet-router` container gets SIGTERM (`Shutdown signal received; draining`), most likely from kubelet after the `/healthz` liveness probe (timeout 1s, period 10s, 3 failures) failed during the stall.
3. 09:20:49: during graceful shutdown it drains the dataplane (`Draining dataplane window=15s` → `Dataplane drained` → `Drain-complete marker written path=/var/run/atenet/drain-complete` → `Shutdown complete`, exit 0).
4. kubelet restarts only the `atenet-router` container. `envoy` has no liveness probe, so it is never restarted and stays `DRAINING` (uptime 139093s, `hot_restart_generation: 1`). The new router container does not take Envoy out of drain, and nothing else recovers it.

So the trigger is a temporary stall (likely the host VM being starved or paused, e.g. the laptop sleeping), but the bug is that it never recovers: draining is meant for pod shutdown, yet it runs on every router container restart, and the restarted router never undoes it.

## How to reproduce (hints, not yet verified)

- Restart only the router container while Envoy keeps running, e.g. from the Kind node: `docker exec ax-local-control-plane crictl ps --name atenet-router -q | xargs docker exec ax-local-control-plane crictl stop`. Then watch `kubectl -n ate-system get pod -l <router selector> -w` and `ax get workspaces` after `ax apply`ing a new Workspace.
- Or stall the node long enough for the `/healthz` liveness probe to fail: `docker pause ax-local-control-plane`, wait 2–3 minutes, `docker unpause ax-local-control-plane`. Sleeping the laptop with the cluster running is likely the most common real-world trigger.
- Check with `kubectl -n ate-system port-forward pod/<atenet-router pod> 9901` and `curl localhost:9901/ready` (expect `DRAINING`).

## Workaround

`kubectl -n ate-system rollout restart deploy/atenet-router`. Workspaces stuck in `Preparing` recover on ax-server's next setup retry or have to be re-created.

## Possible fixes

- Substrate: don't drain Envoy on a router container restart (only on pod termination), or have the router call Envoy's `/healthcheck/ok` and clear the drain marker on startup; or give the `envoy` container a liveness probe that fails while it is `DRAINING` without a router shutdown in progress.
- AX: have `ax local status` / `ax local start` detect an unready `atenet-router` and say how to fix it, and have workspace setup report the router's unreachability as a condition on the Workspace rather than leaving it silently in `Preparing`.

## Environment

- `ax version dev+3ec184a` (`ax local start`), Kind v0.33.0, Kubernetes v1.36.1, single node `ax-local-control-plane`, macOS arm64 host with a 4 CPU / 8 GB VM.
- Substrate images `ghcr.io/agent-substrate/substrate/atenet:v1.0.0` and `envoy-dataplane:v1.0.0`.

title: ax local: cleanup manifest patch on envoy liveness probe
body: Clean up the manifest patch introduced in https://github.com/google/ax/pull/735 once https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/issues/3601 is fixed

title: api: drop data-plane fields from TaskStatus
body:
Task status no longer contains anything from the data plane of the task's actor: how its command ended, its output, or retry context. An external orchestrator will be used for task status management and for suspending and resuming tasks. AX reports only what it knows as the control plane: its own `QUEUED` state, the actor's state on Agent Substrate, and conditions.

- Remove `TASK_STATE_FAILED` and `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`. `COMPLETED` was never set. A task whose actor could not be provisioned, or no longer exists, now has no state, and its `Ready` condition says why (for example `ActorCreationFailed` or `ActorNotFound`). When the actor exists, its live state is reported, and the failed call still returns its error.
- Remove `TaskOutcome` (`status`, `exitCode`, `output`) and `TaskStatus.previousFailure`, which nothing set. `ax describe` no longer prints `Exit Code`/`Output`, and `ax promote --suspend-source` no longer skips tasks with an outcome.
- Drop the `google/rpc/status.proto` import and the `buf.build/googleapis/googleapis` dependency, and renumber `TaskStatus` fields. This is a breaking change, which is fine for `v1alpha1`. Stored rows with removed fields or enum values still load, because the Postgres store discards unknown protojson fields.

Tested with `make verify`, `go test ./...`, and the Postgres store tier.

title: ax-server: take the router URL from --router-url, not ATENET_ROUTER_ADDR
body:
ax-server now takes the router URL from a `--router-url` flag and no longer reads `ATENET_ROUTER_ADDR`; `ax ssh` still does. Fixes #710.

- `--router-url` defaults to `https://atenet-router.ate-system.svc.cluster.local:443`, and ax-server exits at startup unless the value is an `http://` or `https://` URL.
- `cmd/ax-server` passes the URL to `TaskManager.RouterURL` and `NewHTTPSetupRunner`. `routerBaseURL`, which read the variable and turned a bare `host:port` into a URL, is gone, and tests set the URL directly instead of with `t.Setenv`.
- `deploy/ax-server.yaml` and `test/e2e/manifests/ax-server.yaml` pass the flag under `args` instead of setting the variable. An ax-server image from before this change exits on the unknown flag when started from the new manifest; a new one started from an old manifest uses the default.

Known pre-existing issue: `TaskManager.Resume` still returns success without pushing the task when the router URL is empty. After this change only tests that resume without a router reach that case.

title: install: name unavailable Substrate workloads in ax local status
body:
Part of #754

## Problem

`ax local status` looked only at `ate-api-server` and at the `proxy_arp` sysctl of the node. In #754 the `envoy` container of `atenet-router` stayed unready and the `atenet-router` Service had no endpoints, so new workspaces hung, while the status still read:

```
Substrate:     ate-api-server (1/1 available)
```

## Change

`KindProvider.Status` now reads every workload that `ax local start` installs for Agent Substrate, with one `kubectl get deployments,statefulsets,daemonsets -A`. When a workload has fewer available pods than it wants, the `Substrate:` line names it instead of `ate-api-server`:

```
Substrate:     degraded: atenet-router (0/1 available), atenet-egress (0/1 available)
```


## Not in this PR

#754 also asks that a Workspace report the unreachable router as a condition instead of staying in `Preparing` with no conditions. Arguable if we should let workspace to report the underlying subtrate status especially we could potentially make workspace 100% declaritive.

## Test

On a Kind cluster built from this branch (no liveness probe from #735, so Envoy stays drained):

```
$ ax local status --name ax-754
Cluster:       ax-754 (kind)
State:         Running
Kube Context:  kind-ax-754
Substrate:     ate-api-server (1/1 available)
AX Server:     ax-server (1/1 available in ax-system)


$ docker exec ax-754-control-plane pkill -TERM -f 'router --mode=ingress'
$ docker exec ax-754-control-plane pkill -TERM -f 'router --mode=egress'

$ kubectl --context kind-ax-754 -n ate-system get deploy atenet-router atenet-egress
NAME            READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE
atenet-egress   0/1     1            0
atenet-router   0/1     1            0

$ ax local status --name ax-754
```

title: Review how AX uses Actor and ActorTemplate before 1.0
body: Before cutting 1.0, review how AX maps tasks and workspaces onto Substrate Actors and ActorTemplates. Today each task gets its own actor, actors come from ActorTemplates shared by tasks with the same profile, and workspace setup runs in separate setup actors whose snapshots tasks start from. This model is hard to change once users depend on it, and it shapes upgrades (moving existing tasks to a new runner or image), external volumes, and other lifecycle capabilities such as fork and session reuse. The review should decide what to keep, what to change, and what must be settled before 1.0.

title: server: leave spec.sessionId empty when omitted
body:
Stop defaulting `spec.sessionId` to `metadata.uid` in `CreateTask` so one-off tasks write an empty `AX_SESSION_FILE`.

### Motivation
Launchers read `AX_SESSION_FILE` to tell one-off tasks apart from multi-turn sessions. In `agentexecutor/images#30` (and `#31`), `ax-antigravity` only deletes the remote Gemini API environment on exit when `AX_SESSION_FILE` is empty. Because `ax-server` defaulted `spec.sessionId` to `metadata.uid`, every server-created task passed a non-empty `AX_SESSION_FILE` and left its remote environment behind after finishing.

This changes the default added in #587 (from #542). `metadata.uid` still uniquely identifies each task; callers that want durable session state or lineage grouping set `spec.sessionId` explicitly.

### Changes
- `internal/server/server.go`: remove the `task.Spec.SessionId = task.Metadata.Uid` defaulting in `CreateTask`, and simplify `taskSpecMatchesExisting` to a nil-safe `proto.Equal` check.
- `pkg/apis/v1alpha1/task.proto` and `pkg/apis/v1alpha1/task.pb.go`: update the `session_id` comment (regenerated via `make verify`; no descriptor/field changes).
- `internal/apivalidation/task.go`, `runner/launcher.go`, `docs/manifests.md`, `docs/local_installer.md`: update comments and docs to note `spec.sessionId` stays empty when omitted.
- `internal/server/server_test.go`: assert omitted `sessionId` stays empty in the lifecycle test and add `TestServer_TaskSessionID` covering omitted/explicit values and `QUEUED` retry immutability mismatches.
- `test/e2e/promote_test.go`: set an explicit `sessionId` in `promoteManifest` so `TestE2E_Promote` keeps verifying non-empty `sessionId` preservation across `ax promote`.

### Impact check
- **In-flight `QUEUED` retry across upgrade:** dropping the UID shim in `taskSpecMatchesExisting` means a `QUEUED` task created by an older `ax-server` (with defaulted `sessionId == metadata.uid`) will reject a retry that omits `sessionId` with `FailedPrecondition`.
- **`agentexecutor/images` (`antigravity/`):** empty `AX_SESSION_FILE` keeps per-task state under `<workspace>/.ax` and deletes the remote environment on exit; non-empty retains it under `<workspace>/.ax/sessions/<id>`.
- **`agentexecutor/images` (`agents/antigravity`):** empty `AX_SESSION_FILE` skips symlinking `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli` into `/workspace/.ax/sessions/<id>`. `hack/hero-demo/task-starter.yaml` already sets `sessionId: hero-demo-session`.
- **`ax describe task` / `ax promote`:** `ax describe` already hides empty `sessionId`; `ax promote` copies `task.Spec` verbatim.
- **`agentexecutor/studio`:** already falls back to `task:<name>` when `sessionId` is empty.

Follow-up note for `agentexecutor/images`: once this merges, remove the note about server-side `spec.sessionId` defaulting in `antigravity/README.md`.

### Verification
```bash
make verify && git diff --exit-code && test -z "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)"
go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/ax
go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/ax-server
go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/ax-runner
go test -c -o /dev/null ./test/e2e
go test -count=1 ./...
go test -race -count=1 ./internal/server/... ./cmd/ax/... ./runner/... ./pkg/apis/v1alpha1/... ./internal/apivalidation/...
```
Note: Postgres store integration tests skip locally when `AX_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` is unset and run in CI against `postgres:17-alpine`.

title: server: store a task only once its actor exists
body:
`CreateTask` now provisions the actor first and stores the task only once the actor exists. A failed create returns the error and stores nothing. Fixes #698.

- When provisioning or the store write fails, `CreateTask` deletes the actor. An actor left by a failed delete or a crash is adopted by the next create of that name.
- A task that already exists is always rejected: the retry of a stored `QUEUED` task is gone, and `QUEUED` is no longer stored for a create.
- `metadata.uid`, `createTime` and the default `sessionId` are assigned when the task is stored.
- `ax apply` gives `CreateTask` five minutes, as it does `CreateWorkspace`, because `ax resume` can no longer finish a failed create.

Follow-up (#695): `ResumeTask` still stores `QUEUED` after a transient Substrate error. The next PR removes that and the `QUEUED` state with it, so a failed resume only returns its error.

title: api: validate resource names with k8s declarative validation
body:
Validate `metadata.name` and `metadata.atespace` with rules declared as `+k8s:` tags in the protos, from which Kubernetes `validation-gen` generates the checks, as Agent Substrate does. First step of #726.

- `make generate` now also runs `validation-gen` (pinned in `hack/tools/code-generator`) and writes `internal/apivalidation/zz_generated.validation.go`; `go.mod` gains `k8s.io/apimachinery` at the same release, `v0.38.0-beta.0`.
- Each create and update handler calls one request validator, such as `ValidateCreateTaskRequest`, which runs the generated checks and then the checks that are still written by hand.
- A request gets all its problems back at once, with paths that start at the request field: `task.metadata.name: Required value`. A problem found by a hand-written check reads `task: Invalid value: spec.profile: ...` until that check is moved.

Follow-ups:
- Move the hand-written checks to tags and custom validators, one proto file per PR: `common.proto`, `task.proto`, `gateway.proto`, `workspace.proto`.
- Clear the server-assigned fields before validating, as Agent Substrate does, together with the `common.proto` PR.
- Generate the egress rules that Agent Substrate declares for `Gateway`, and add rules for the fields that have none.
- Move both pins to `v0.38.0` when Kubernetes 1.38 is released.

title: make build-local-cluster and ax local pick different container engines
body:
On a host where both Docker and Podman are running (here: Docker via Colima and Podman on macOS), `make build-local-cluster` and the `ax local` commands pick different container engines. As a result, `ax local status` reports a healthy cluster as missing.

## Reproduce

1. Start both Docker (e.g. Colima) and Podman.
2. Run `make build-local-cluster`. It finishes with `Local environment "ax-local" is ready` and shows `State: Running`.
3. Run `ax local status`:

```
Cluster:       N/A
State:         NotFound
Kube Context:  N/A
Substrate:     N/A
AX Server:     N/A
```

4. Run `CONTAINER_CLI=podman ax local status`:

```
Cluster:       ax-local (kind)
State:         Running
Kube Context:  ax-local
Substrate:     ate-api-server (1/1 available)
AX Server:     ax-server (1/1 available in ax-system)
```

`kubectl --context ax-local get pods -A` shows everything running the entire time; only the status check fails.

## Cause

- `Makefile:36` prefers Podman: `CONTAINER_CLI ?= $(shell command -v podman 2>/dev/null || command -v docker 2>/dev/null)`. This value is passed to `hack/build-local-cluster.sh` and so to `ax local start`, which creates the Kind node container in Podman (`KIND_EXPERIMENTAL_PROVIDER=podman`).
- `executil.ResolveContainerRuntime` (`internal/install/executil/tools.go`) prefers Docker when `CONTAINER_CLI` is not set: it probes `docker info` first and then `podman info`. Every later `ax local` command (`status`, `stop`, `delete`, ...) run from a plain shell therefore selects Docker.
- `KindProvider.Status` (`internal/install/cluster/kind.go`) runs `kind get nodes --name ax-local` without `KIND_EXPERIMENTAL_PROVIDER`. Kind returns `No kind nodes found for cluster "ax-local"`, and Status returns `StateAbsent` ("NotFound") with a nil error. It does the same if `listNodes` fails outright, which hides the real problem.

The engine is not saved anywhere, so later commands cannot tell which one created the cluster.

## Impact

- `ax local status` wrongly reports NotFound, and users may think the cluster failed or disappeared.
- `ax local stop` / `delete` / `start` from a plain shell likely act on the wrong engine. For example, `ax local start` may create a second `ax-local` cluster under Docker while the Podman one keeps running, and both claim the same kube context name.
- It is likely to affect developers on macOS, where installing Podman next to Colima or Docker Desktop is common.

## Possible fixes

- Use the same preference order in both places, e.g. make the Makefile prefer Docker to match the CLI. Or move the selection into a single place that the Makefile asks, e.g. an `ax`-side helper.
- Save the engine used by `ax local start` (e.g. in the AX home's local environment state) and have later `ax local` commands use it unless `CONTAINER_CLI` overrides it.
- In `Status`, when the selected engine finds no nodes, check the other running engine and point to `CONTAINER_CLI`. Report a `listNodes` failure as an error instead of NotFound.

Workaround: `export CONTAINER_CLI=podman` (or whatever engine `make build-local-cluster` printed in `Building ... using ...`).

title: install: find the local cluster on whichever engine runs it
body:
Fixes #767.

With both docker and podman running, `ax local` always preferred docker, so it reported a cluster that podman runs (for example one created by `make build-local-cluster`, which prefers podman) as `NotFound`, and `start`/`stop`/`delete` could act on the wrong engine.

- `executil.RunningContainerRuntimes` returns every running engine (docker first), or only `CONTAINER_CLI` if set. `ResolveContainerRuntime` still stops at the first one.
- `KindProvider.resolveTools` takes the cluster name and, with more than one engine running, uses the one that has the cluster. Without a cluster it falls back to docker as before. This applies to `Up`, `Stop`, `Status` and `Delete`, so `ax local start` resumes a podman cluster instead of creating a second one on docker.
- `Status` returns an error when `kind get nodes` fails instead of reporting `NotFound`, and records the engine in `Status.Runtime`. `ax local status -o json` uses that engine for the `host` object.
- `docs/local_installer.md` explains how the engine is chosen.

Testing: `make verify`, `go test ./...`, and new unit tests for the new behavior. On a Mac with Colima and Podman both running, a podman cluster from `make build-local-cluster` now shows as `Running` in a plain `ax local status`, and `host.runtime` is `podman`. `make test-local-install` passes locally.

title: Release: automation across different repos, images and binaries
body:
1. Images (ax-server, ax-task, runner-volume, agy-cli) and AX public libraries (api, client): Relatively independent; these can be released as soon as the code is ready.
2. ax-studio: A separate repo that hosts the Studio frontend, a web app released as a binary.
    - It makes gRPC calls to ax-server to fetch resources such as tasks, so its go.mod must be updated whenever the ax-server API changes.
    - It tracks the default images (ax-server, runner-volume, etc.) to simplify environment provisioning.
3. ax CLI: Like ax-studio, it depends on the default images (ax-server, runner-volume, etc.).
4. install.sh: The installer script that downloads the ax CLI and ax-studio binaries. It needs to track the CLI and Studio versions.

We need automation or some bot instead of relying on human to manage those dependencies.

In the long term, if we migrate to an Electron app, we can drop install.sh and bundle ax-studio and the ax CLI into a single package.

cc @mayawang please update if you saw anything else when you cut the release.

cc @rakyll
