title: Decouple ax from ax-studio
body:
## Why

`google/ax` currently depends on `agentexecutor/studio` (via `ax studio`, `install.sh`, and `docs/releasing.md`), while `agentexecutor/studio` depends on `google/ax` in `go.mod` and shells out to `ax`. This creates a circular release dependency (AX's `install.sh` pins Studio's release version and SHA-256 before tagging AX, while Studio needs the AX release first) and couples the core CLI/installer to an optional UI.

The dependency should be strictly one-way: `agentexecutor/studio` -> `google/ax`.

## Scope

- Remove `ax studio` (`cmd/ax/studio_cmd.go`, `cmd/ax/studio_cmd_test.go`, `cmd/ax/main.go`) and `ResolveStudioBinary` (`internal/install/executil/tools.go`, `runner_test.go`). Users run `ax-studio` directly.
- Remove Studio download/pinning (`PINNED_STUDIO_VERSION`, `pinned_studio_sha256`, `install_studio`, `AX_STUDIO_*`) from `install.sh` and the Studio pre-release step from `docs/releasing.md`.
- Update `README.md`, `docs/local_installer.md`, and `AGENTS.md` to reference `agentexecutor/studio` as a standalone companion tool.
- Keep generic CLI contracts like `ax local status -o json` (`cmd/ax/install_cmd.go`).

title: cli: remove ax studio subcommand
body:
Removes the studio subcommand and Studio binary resolution from the ax CLI so dependencies flow strictly one way from [agentexecutor/studio](https://github.com/agentexecutor/studio) to google/ax. Studio launches standalone and already discovers the ax binary on its own, while local status JSON output stays intact as the machine-readable contract.

Studio installation in the shell installer stays scoped to #775, with only the next-step hint updated to point at the standalone binary.

Fixes #777

title: controller: return transient Substrate errors without a condition
body:
The task manager and workspace prepare no longer set a `SubstrateUnavailable` condition when a call fails with a transient error; they only return the error. Part of #695.

- After a failed resume a task is still `Queued`, now without a `Ready` condition. A Workspace whose prepare failed stays `Preparing`, now without conditions.
- `QUEUED` stays, as #695 describes. The follow-up note in #761 said the next PR would remove it; that is a separate question.
- `TestWorkspacePrewarm_CanceledContextStillPersistsStatus` becomes `TestWorkspacePrewarm_CanceledContextStaysPreparing`.

title: Make the runner volume image required
body: The runner volume image (`--runner-volume-image` / `AX_RUNNER_VOLUME_IMAGE`) is optional and defaults to empty, so tasks fall back to a runner baked into the task image. Prebuilt agent images from agentexecutor/images ship no runner, so they fail without it; AX should always mount a runner volume, defaulting to the release's `ax-runner-volume` image.

title: hack/hero-demo/run.sh: fails on stock macOS /bin/bash 3.2 (requires Bash 4+ declare -A)
body:
## Summary

`hack/hero-demo/run.sh` uses Bash 4+ associative arrays (`declare -A STATUS` / `declare -A NOTE` on lines 102–103). On macOS without Homebrew Bash (`5.3.x`), its `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang invokes stock `/bin/bash` (`3.2.57`) even from the default `zsh` shell, failing immediately when recording and printing the scoreboard.

*(For milestone `v0.4.0`.)*

## Reproduction

On a stock macOS machine (no Homebrew `bash` in `PATH`):

```bash
/bin/bash --version
# GNU bash, version 3.2.57(1)-release (arm64-apple-darwin25)

./hack/hero-demo/run.sh
```

Output:
```text
./hack/hero-demo/run.sh: line 102: declare: -A: invalid option
declare: usage: declare [-afFirtx] [-p] [name[=value] ...]
./hack/hero-demo/run.sh: line 103: declare: -A: invalid option
declare: usage: declare [-afFirtx] [-p] [name[=value] ...]
...
./hack/hero-demo/run.sh: line 105: 2. Warm Workspace Snapshot: syntax error: invalid arithmetic operator (error token is ". Warm Workspace Snapshot")
...
./hack/hero-demo/run.sh: line 436: 2. Warm Workspace Snapshot: syntax error: invalid arithmetic operator (error token is ". Warm Workspace Snapshot")
```

Note: invoking `zsh ./hack/hero-demo/run.sh` directly also fails because line 37 relies on `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` and 0-indexed array indexing.

## Suggested Fix

Keep the script Bash 3.2-compatible (matching `hack/tour.sh`, which avoids `declare -A` and runs cleanly on stock macOS `/bin/bash` `3.2.57`).

Because `STEPS` is already a 5-element indexed array and every call site passes `"${step}"`, replacing `declare -A STATUS` / `declare -A NOTE` with parallel indexed arrays and a small `step_index` lookup fixes lines 102–107 and 436 with zero changes to any of the `mark_pass` / `mark_stub` / `mark_fail` call sites:

```bash
STATUS=()
NOTE=()

step_index() {
  local i
  for i in "${!STEPS[@]}"; do
    if [[ "${STEPS[$i]}" == "$1" ]]; then
      printf '%s' "${i}"
      return 0
    fi
  done
  return 1
}

mark_result() {
  local idx
  idx="$(step_index "$1")" || return 1
  STATUS[$idx]="$2"
  NOTE[$idx]="$3"
}

mark_pass() { mark_result "$1" "🟢 PASS" "$2"; }
mark_stub() { mark_result "$1" "🟡 STUB" "$2"; }
mark_fail() { mark_result "$1" "🔴 FAIL" "$2"; }
```

And in the scoreboard loop (lines 431–437):

```bash
for i in "${!STEPS[@]}"; do
  if [[ -n "${ONLY_STEP}" && "${ONLY_STEP}" != "$((i + 1))" ]]; then
    continue
  fi
  printf "  %-34s | %-7s | %s\n" "${STEPS[$i]}" "${STATUS[$i]:-}" "${NOTE[$i]:-}"
done
```

title: server, controller: stop reporting failures as Ready conditions
body:
A task no longer gets a `Ready` condition that describes a failed call: the task manager only returns its errors, and a read that cannot reach Substrate returns the task without live status. Fixes #695.

- A read that cannot reach Substrate takes the second of the two options in #695: `GetTask` and `ListTasks` still succeed, and `ax get` shows the state as `Unknown` as before.
- `ReasonSubstrateUnavailable` and `ReasonInvalidResources` are removed. The other failure reasons stay for Workspaces, which store them.
- Nothing stored or returned the task manager's reasons any more, so callers see no difference there. Its tests now check that a transient error stays transient.

Not done: the metadata endpoint, an admission check for `spec.env`, and the launchers in agentexecutor/images, which keep working as they are.

body:
Simplifies the Start AX section of the README.

- Shortens the local and existing-cluster intros, and drops the Kubernetes 1.37+ requirement from the intro.
- Shows creating the WorkerPool as a `kubectl apply -f examples/workerpool.yaml` step after `ax install` instead of a paragraph.
- Replaces the release image and runner volume paragraph with one sentence on adding `--runner-volume-image` for prebuilt agent images.
- Drops the pointer to building from source and pushing custom images (still linked from the guides table).
- Links to the AX Studio and Agent Substrate repos without `#readme`, in the README and `docs/local_installer.md`.

title: skills: add an ax skill for driving the CLI
body:
Adds `skills/ax`, a short skill for driving the `ax` CLI: the apply/resume/describe/ssh/delete loop, a table of every command and its key flags, the rules that most often break a task (tasks start suspended, digest-pinned images, WorkerPool, manifest order, immutability, gateway egress), and a symptom table for debugging. `references/examples.md` has example manifests for a Workspace + Gateway + Task on a cloned repo, Gateway credential injection, and a Model.

Also adds the `/ax` row to the skills table in `AGENTS.md`.

title: api: remove TASK_STATE_QUEUED
body:
Removes `TASK_STATE_QUEUED`, the last task state AX stores. Since #761 only a transient `ResumeTask` failure sets it; nothing acts on it, and it hides the actor's state until the next suspend or resume succeeds. Draft: this is the "Resume" question #698 left open.

- A failed `ResumeTask` only returns its error and stores nothing; `recordFailure` and `IsAXTaskState` are gone.
- `TaskState` now has only the actor's states.
- A resume that fails before the actor is resumed leaves the task `Suspended` instead of `Queued`.
- A resume that fails because the runner does not accept the task in time leaves it `Running`, with `Ready=True` if its workspace was set up before, instead of `Queued`.

The last case already reads this way when the runner refuses the task (#756).
